findings.description: Adding flexbox to .small-action disables the button's float:right, dropping the action button's right-edge alignment. — WHAT: `.small-action` is now `display: flex`, and per the CSS Flexbox spec `float`/`clear` do not apply to flex items, so the existing `button { float: right }` inside `.small-action` is ignored and the button is laid out in source order immediately after `.small-action-desc`. WHY: the action button loses its right-edge alignment (it previously relied on `float: right` in the block layout), a visual regression in every flex-capable browser. HOW: if the button is a direct child, replace the float with `margin-left: auto` on the button (or `justify-content: space-between` on `.small-action`); verify the button's DOM position first.

Removing the float-based header layout without a non-flex fallback breaks header and small-action layout in IE8/IE9 and other non-flex browsers. — WHAT: this PR removes `float: left` from `.contents .title` and `float: right` from `.panel` and replaces the layout solely with `display: flex` (plus prefixed box syntax), leaving no layout fallback for browsers that support neither flexbox nor the old -webkit-box/-moz-box/-ms-flexbox syntaxes (IE8/IE9). WHY: in those browsers `.title` and `.panel` become stacked block elements — the login/panel controls drop below the title — because `margin-left: auto` and `order()` are no-ops in block layout; the same regression hits `.small-action-desc` in topic-post.scss, which lost its `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` padding that cleared the still-floated `.topic-avatar` (45px icon), so its text overlaps the avatar. HOW: retain the old float declarations alongside the flex ones (floats are ignored on flex items in supporting browsers) so non-flex browsers keep the previous layout.

order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper is likely a no-op because the header DOM still wraps it in a .title element, which is the actual flex item. — WHAT: `@include order(2)` is applied to `.extra-info-wrapper`, but the `order` property only affects flex items — direct children of a flex container — and the diff itself removed the `.contents .title { float: left }` rule, evidencing that a `.title` wrapper element existed between `.contents` and `.extra-info-wrapper` in the header DOM. WHY: if `.extra-info-wrapper` is still nested inside `.title` (which is the flex item, order 0), the `order(2)` silently has no effect and the header reordering this PR intends never happens; additionally the now-floatless `.title` wrapper becomes an opaque flex item that the removed `float: left` used to control. HOW: confirm the header template makes `.extra-info-wrapper` a direct child of `.contents` (or apply the order mixin to the `.title` wrapper instead).

missedGoldens.text: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

goldensDetail.text: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

findings.description: LoggerMiddleware log lines lose the traceID field after the refactor to context-sourced attributes. — WHAT: The traceID field was removed from the 'Plugin Request Completed' log line: logRequest no longer appends tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false), and the replacement m.logger.FromContext(ctx) only picks up attributes set via WithContextualAttributes (the sole registered contextual provider reads only logParamsContextKey), which the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware never populates with a traceID. WHY: Every plugin-request completion log emitted by this middleware now permanently lacks traceID, breaking trace-to-log correlation that previously existed. HOW: Re-add traceID to logParams (tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)) or have ContextualLoggerMiddleware add it to the context attributes.

LoggerMiddleware log enrichment is now silently dependent on ContextualLoggerMiddleware being wired upstream in the chain. — WHAT: pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, and uname are no longer added unconditionally in logRequest; they now come solely from m.logger.FromContext(ctx), which only returns them if the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware ran instrumentContext on the same context BEFORE this middleware (i.e., is placed upstream in the middleware chain). WHY: If the wiring does not register ContextualLoggerMiddleware or places it after LoggerMiddleware, these previously guaranteed log fields silently disappear, and the old InstrumentationMiddleware comment that required the enrichment middleware to sit at the top of the stack was removed without an ordering guarantee for its replacement. HOW: Verify the chain wiring registers NewContextualLoggerMiddleware before NewLoggerMiddleware, and add a comment/documentation stating the ordering requirement.

missedGoldens.text: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the

goldensDetail.text: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

findings.description: Serializer requires fields from both (mutually exclusive) spec versions, so no spec-compliant browser report can pass validation and all reports are rejected with 422. — WHAT: BrowserReportSerializer marks user_agent, destination, and attempts as required, but these fields belong to different, mutually exclusive spec versions (user_agent/age are Working Draft TR/reporting-1; destination/timestamp/attempts are Editor's Draft w3c.github.io/reporting, where user_agent was removed), so a report conforming to either spec fails is_valid() with 'This field is required.' WHY: the code comment states the intent is 'We need to support both specs', but only age/timestamp were made optional — every real browser report (e.g. a modern Chrome report with destination/timestamp/attempts but no user_agent) is rejected with HTTP 422 and the collector silently drops all data. HOW: make user_agent, destination, and attempts optional (required=False, allow_null=True) so reports from either spec validate, or implement a validate() that requires only the field set of one coherent spec.

Mutual-exclusion validators use truthiness so age:0/timestamp:0 slips past the check meant to reject reports carrying both spec fields. — WHAT: validate_timestamp and validate_age check `self.initial_data.get('age')` / `.get('timestamp')` for truthiness, so a zero value (age: 0 is a valid Working Draft value meaning 'report just generated') is treated as absent. WHY: a report carrying both age and timestamp — exactly the malformed case these validators exist to reject — passes validation whenever either value is 0, and the mutually exclusive contract is silently bypassed. HOW: check key presence instead of truthiness, e.g. `if 'age' in self.initial_data:` (and vice versa), or compare against None.

findings.description: Update inside the new catch block can throw (concurrent deletion) and abort the whole reminder batch, a failure mode this PR introduces. — WHAT: the new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the `catch` block (and the else-branch update) can itself throw (e.g. P2025 'record not found' when a concurrent invocation of this same cron endpoint — auth is a static API key, so overlaps are possible — or a booking-cancellation cleanup deletes the reminder after the fetch), and since there is no nested try/catch around it the exception escapes and aborts the entire for-loop. WHY: remaining reminders in the batch are never processed, no further retryCount increments happen, and `res.status(200)` at line 201 is never reached, so the cron request fails/500s — a failure mode that did not exist before this PR (the catch previously only logged). HOW: wrap the increment in its own try/catch (best-effort) or use `prisma.workflowReminder.updateMany({ where: { id: reminder.id, retryCount: reminder.retryCount }, data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } })` so a missing row is a no-op instead of a thrown error.

deleteMany's retryCount>1 branch is not scoped to method SMS, deviating from the SMS-only delete intent and risking deletion of non-SMS reminders. — WHAT: the second OR branch of the deleteMany — `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` — is not scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, unlike the first branch and the stated intent ('delete all scheduled sms reminders'). WHY: any non-SMS WorkflowReminder whose retryCount ever exceeds 1 (a value only the SMS scheduler writes today, but the column is on the shared WorkflowReminder model) is silently deleted regardless of method and regardless of scheduledDate, and future writers of the field would trigger data loss outside this file. HOW: hoist the method filter so it applies to both branches: `where: { method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, OR: [{ scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().toISOString() } }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] }`.

Unguarded retryCount update inside catch/else can throw and abort the entire cron run, skipping all remaining reminders. — WHAT: The new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the `catch` block (and the `else` branch) is unguarded — if it throws (e.g., P2025 when the row was concurrently deleted by the cancel flow or another run, or a transient DB error), the exception escapes the per-reminder try/catch and aborts the whole `for` loop. WHY: Previously the catch only logged, so this PR adds a new failure surface where one reminder's counter-update failing cancels Twilio scheduling for every remaining reminder in that cron run. HOW: Wrap the counter-update in its own try/catch so a failed counter-write cannot abort the loop, e.g. `try { await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...) } catch (e) { console.error("Failed to bump retryCount", e) }`.

deleteMany retryCount branch is not method-scoped and would delete any non-SMS reminder whose retryCount is ever bumped. — WHAT: The new second OR-branch of the deleteMany — `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` — is not scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` like the sibling branch, so it deletes workflow reminders of every method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) once their retryCount exceeds 1. WHY: Today only this SMS cron writes retryCount (verified by grep), so the blast radius is latent — but any future code path that bumps retryCount on non-SMS reminders would have those rows silently deleted by this SMS cron. HOW: Scope the branch explicitly, e.g. `{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`.

Temporary SMS lock (scheduleSMS returning undefined) is counted as a failure, so reminders are permanently deleted after two cron runs while locked. — WHAT: The new `else` branch treats `twilio.scheduleSMS` returning `undefined` as a send failure and increments `retryCount`, but scheduleSMS only returns `undefined` when SMS sending is temporarily locked (`isLockedForSMSSending` → `SMSLockState.LOCKED`, twilioProvider.ts:149-154) — a reversible administrative state, not a failure. WHY: While a user/team stays locked for two or more cron runs, their reminders are permanently deleted by the new `retryCount > 1` deleteMany — potentially days before the scheduled date — and the SMS is never sent even after the lock is lifted; previously the cron kept retrying until the date. HOW: Skip the retryCount increment for the undefined (locked) return, e.g. only increment in the catch (real Twilio/rate-limit failures) and leave locked reminders for the next run: `if (scheduledSMS) { ... } // no else-increment, or increment only a dedicated 'skipped' counter`.

missedGoldens.text: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also

goldensDetail.text: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

findings.description: Restarting a thread-based flusher never stops the old thread, leaving two flushers running concurrently on the same shards. — WHAT: when the flusher runs as a threading.Thread (produce_to_pipe set), _ensure_processes_alive skips process.kill() via the isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard yet still calls _create_process_for_shards, starting a second flusher thread for the same shards while the old one keeps running. WHY: both threads then concurrently poll buffer.flush_segments on the same Redis shards and produce to the same pipe, causing duplicate/racy segment flushing that the previous code path could not produce. HOW: in the restart branch, also stop the old thread (e.g., join it or record a per-process stop flag and skip restart until the old worker exits), or keep the isinstance guard but terminate/join the old worker before spawning the replacement.

Per-buffer get_memory_info() calls repeat full-cluster Redis memory scans N× per submit when the flusher is scaled to multiple processes. — WHAT: submit() now calls buffer.get_memory_info() once per flusher buffer in a loop, and each call walks the whole Redis cluster via iter_cluster_memory_usage, returning cluster-wide totals. WHY: with --flusher-processes > 1 (the stated goal of this PR), every message submit triggers N full-cluster memory scans instead of one, multiplying Redis INFO traffic N× while the used/available ratio is unchanged (each buffer reports the same cluster totals, so summing N copies only inflates the counters). HOW: call get_memory_info() once outside the loop (e.g., on a single buffer) since it is cluster-scoped, or gate the per-buffer scan behind an option.

Hung flusher threads are not killed before a replacement thread is spawned, causing duplicate flushes and masking hang detection. — WHAT: In _ensure_processes_alive, process.kill() is guarded by isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), so a hung flusher running as a threading.Thread (produce_to_pipe is not None) is never killed, yet _create_process_for_shards still spawns a replacement thread for the same shards. WHY: the old thread keeps polling the same Redis shards and producing the same segments to the pipe while the new thread does the same — duplicate spans produced — and because the orphaned thread keeps writing the shared healthy_since Value, hang detection stays masked until process_restarts hits MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS and the consumer is crashed. HOW: for the thread case, either set a stop flag the main loop checks and join the old thread before restarting, or skip restarting threads entirely and only report unhealthy.

join() skips terminating remaining flusher processes once the deadline is exhausted by earlier ones. — WHAT: join() breaks out of the process loop as soon as the shared deadline is exhausted (e.g. after next_step.join(timeout) or the first process's wait), so all remaining flusher processes are neither waited on nor terminated. WHY: with multiple flusher processes (the new multiprocessed design) a slow first process consumes the whole shutdown budget and the rest are abandoned mid-loop — they keep polling Redis until the daemon parent exits, or are killed abruptly at exit instead of being terminated cleanly. HOW: on deadline exhaustion, still call process.terminate() for each remaining multiprocessing.Process instead of breaking.

Memory check walks the whole Redis cluster once per flusher process on every submit instead of once. — WHAT: submit() now calls buffer.get_memory_info() once per flusher process, and each call runs iter_cluster_memory_usage over the entire Redis cluster (all nodes, via the shared client registry). WHY: with flusher-processes > 1 — the whole point of this PR — every message triggers N redundant full-cluster memory walks instead of one, adding N-1 extra Redis INFO round-trips per message in the hot path. HOW: call get_memory_info() on a single buffer (all shards are covered by the union of buffers, and iter_cluster_memory_usage is cluster-wide anyway) or memoize it for the submit interval.

findings.description: Narrowing the BuildIndex lock to only the cache write allows concurrent builds of the same key, risking on-disk index corruption, stale cache overwrites, and leaked indexes. — WHAT: removing the cacheMu lock from the whole BuildIndex body lets two goroutines build the same key concurrently (getOrCreateIndex is reached from Search RPCs and the watch-event handleEvent goroutine with no per-key guard), so both call bleve.New(dir, mapper) on the same directory for file-backed indexes, and the slower/staler build wins the `b.cache[key] = idx` write with no RV comparison, orphaning the other index without Close. WHY: concurrent bleve.New on one directory can corrupt or fail the on-disk index, stale data can overwrite a fresher index, and the losing in-memory index leaks — previously impossible because the mutex serialized all builds. HOW: guard per-key with a singleflight (e.g., golang.org/x/sync/singleflight) keyed by `key`, or re-check `GetIndex(key)` and compare resource versions before writing the cache, and Close the losing index.

New TotalDocs() log call races with the just-started watch goroutine's cache writes and can panic with 'concurrent map read and map write'. — WHAT: the newly added `s.log.Info("search index initialized", ..., "total_docs", s.search.TotalDocs())` runs immediately after the watch-event goroutine is started, and bleveBackend.TotalDocs() ranges over b.cache with no lock while handleEvent→getOrCreateIndex→BuildIndex can concurrently write b.cache[key]=idx under cacheMu. WHY: an event for a non-cached key arriving in that window causes a Go runtime panic ('concurrent map read and map write') during startup. HOW: snapshot the cache under cacheMu.RLock() inside TotalDocs, or pass the expected count from the init loop instead of calling TotalDocs.

goldensDetail.text: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

findings.description: Cached getForLogin results are not re-filtered by the login predicate, so stale cache can leak hidden/link-only/non-public IDPs onto the login page. — WHAT: The cached getForLogin path reconstructs IdentityProviderModels via getById and returns them without re-applying the login predicate, while the delegate path applies the full filter (ENABLED/HIDE_ON_LOGIN/LINK_ONLY plus org BROKER_PUBLIC). WHY: If the login cache holds an ID that no longer matches login criteria (stale cache / missed invalidation, or a wrapped model that loses flags), a hidden, link-only, disabled or non-public org IDP is rendered on the login page; the consumer only re-checks isEnabled and therefore does not compensate for isHideOnLogin(), isLinkOnly() or the org BROKER_PUBLIC/orgId conditions. HOW: Filter the reconstructed stream with the same predicate used for invalidation, e.g. `return identityProviders.stream().filter(getLoginPredicate());`

remove() adds an unconditional extra DB lookup of the IDP on every removal, even when the cached model is already available. — WHAT: remove() now calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) unconditionally on every removal, whereas previously it was fetched only when the alias cache entry was invalid. WHY: This adds an extra database round-trip to every IDP removal even when the cached model is already available in the else branch (cached.getIdentityProvider()), a small but unnecessary overhead on the admin write path. HOW: In the cache-valid branch reuse cached.getIdentityProvider() for registerIDPLoginInvalidation, and only fall back to idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) when cached is null.

update() compares the org-aware wrapped model against the raw model in getLoginPredicate, causing missed login-cache invalidation when the IDP's organization is disabled. — WHAT: `update()` passes the org-aware wrapped model returned by `getById(model.getInternalId())` as `original` to `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate`, while `updated` is the raw model, so `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` evaluates the organization-dependent `isEnabled()` (wrapper returns `org != null && provider.isEnabled() && org.isEnabled() && super.isEnabled()`) instead of the raw stored `isEnabled()`. WHY: when the IDP's organization is disabled, `test(original)` is false even though the IDP is raw-enabled/public and present in the login cache; if the update also keeps `test(updated)` false (e.g. toggling linkOnly, hideOnLoginPage, or BROKER_PUBLIC), the `!test(original) && !test(updated)` early-return in registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate skips invalidation, leaving a stale login-cache entry that surfaces the IDP on the login page (the bean only re-checks isEnabled, not linkOnly/hideOnLogin). HOW: use the raw delegate model for the comparison, e.g. `idpDelegate.getById(model.getInternalId())` instead of `getById(...)` in update().

findings.description: Client removal in V2 mode triggers ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled which throws UnsupportedOperationException inside the event listener. — WHAT: Overriding clients() to return ClientPermissionsV2 makes the AdminPermissions.registerListener cleanup path throw UnsupportedOperationException on client removal in V2 mode. WHY: On ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent the listener calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(...); management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, so deleting a client aborts with an unhandled exception. HOW: Do not wire the throwing V2 implementation into the cleanup path — e.g. keep the listener on the V1 client evaluator, or make setPermissionsEnabled a no-op in V2 rather than throwing.

hasPermission matches only on scope, not on the resource the permission was granted for, risking cross-resource over-grant. — WHAT: hasPermission matches granted scopes without verifying permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()), unlike UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission. WHY: A permission granted for a different resource (e.g. the 'all-clients' resource type resource, or another client's resource) can satisfy the check for the current client based on scope alone, over-granting fine-grained permissions. HOW: Add the resourceId guard before matching scopes, mirroring UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission.

Inconsistent owner-filtered lookup of the 'Clients' resource-type resource can make the all-clients permission checks always return false. — WHAT: hasPermission(String scope) fetches the 'Clients' resource-type resource with a 3-arg findByName(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId()) (owner-filtered), while the same resource is fetched elsewhere via AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource -> findByName(server, type.getType()) (no owner filter). WHY: If the resource-type resource was created with a different or null owner, this lookup returns null and the no-client permission checks (canManage(), canView(), canManageClientScopes(), canView(ClientScopeModel)) always return false, silently denying 'manage/configure all clients' grants. HOW: Reuse AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) for consistency.

Map-roles checks lack the canManage short-circuit that canConfigure and UserPermissionsV2.canMapRoles include, under-granting manage-only principals. — WHAT: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles only check the specific MAP_ROLES* scope and never short-circuit on canManage(client), unlike canConfigure(client) (which returns true if canManage(client)) and UserPermissionsV2.canMapRoles(user) (which returns true if canManage(user)). WHY: A principal with 'manage' (or MANAGE_CLIENTS) on a client is under-granted and cannot map roles for that client unless they also hold the separate map-roles scope. HOW: Return true when canManage(client) holds before checking the map-roles scopes.

Per-client resource lookup filters by owner server.getId() but the resource is created with owner server.getClientId(), so per-client permissions are never resolved. — WHAT: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) looks up the per-client resource with the 3-arg findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), which filters by owner = server.getId(). WHY: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with owner = resourceServer.getClientId() (line 179), and the working UserPermissionsV2 reference uses the 2-arg findByName without an owner filter, so when server.getId() != server.getClientId() the per-client resource is never found and canManage/canConfigure/canView/canMapRoles(client) silently fall back to the 'all clients' resource-type resource, disabling per-client fine-grained permissions. HOW: use the 2-arg lookup as UserPermissionsV2 does.

goldensDetail.text: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

findings.description: Team admin/owner permission check uses && instead of ||, denying non-owner admins. — WHAT: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses `&&` between `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)`, requiring the caller to be BOTH admin and owner. WHY: a team admin who is not an owner (or an owner who is not an admin, depending on `isTeamAdmin` semantics) is denied and gets FORBIDDEN, breaking guest-adding for legitimate users. HOW: use logical OR.

Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive, allowing blacklisted emails in different casing. — WHAT: The blacklist is lowercased but the input `guest` is compared without normalization, so `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` misses case variants. WHY: a blacklisted address like `Foo@Bar.com` bypasses the filter and is added as a guest (the same case-sensitivity also lets `guest === attendee.email` duplicate an existing attendee with different casing). HOW: lowercase the guest before both comparisons.

Calendar attendee update uses the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's, so non-organizer callers fail to update the organizer's calendar. — WHAT: The EventManager is constructed with the caller's credentials (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`) while the organizer's credentials were already fetched in the booking include (`booking.user.credentials`, lines 35-40) but are never used. WHY: when the caller is a team admin or attendee rather than the organizer, `updateCalendarAttendees` runs against the organizer's destination calendar using the caller's calendar credentials, which cannot access the organizer's calendar — so the organizer's calendar invite is not updated with the new guests. HOW: build the EventManager from the organizer (or at least with `booking.user.credentials`).

Guest-added emails are sent using the raw input list, causing duplicate emails to already-existing attendees. — WHAT: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw input array instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`. WHY: the callee sends an `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` to every attendee whose email is in `newGuests`; attendees already on the booking that are re-passed in the input remain in `evt.attendees` and match, so they receive a spurious 'you've been added' email even though they were excluded from the DB update. HOW: pass `uniqueGuests`.

Duplicate guest emails in the input are not deduplicated, creating duplicate attendee rows and duplicate calendar invite entries. — WHAT: `uniqueGuests` filters only against `booking.attendees` and the blacklist, never deduplicating the `guests` input against itself. WHY: submitting the same email twice (e.g. `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]`) inserts two attendee rows for the same booking (no `@@unique([bookingId, email])` exists on the Attendee model) and produces a duplicate attendee entry in the calendar invite via `evt.attendees`. HOW: deduplicate the filtered result, e.g. wrap in `[...new Set(...)]`.

Organizer lookup crashes with a 500 when booking.userId is null, despite the || 0 fallback implying it is expected. — WHAT: `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` throws when `booking.userId` is null/undefined because no user has id 0. WHY: the `|| 0` fallback shows the code anticipates a nullable `booking.userId` (Booking.userId is `Int?`), yet `findFirstOrThrow` raises an unhandled Prisma P2025, returning a 500 on the team-admin path for team/managed bookings without an owning user. HOW: guard the lookup — if `!booking.userId`, throw a TRPCError or fall back to `booking.user` (already included in the initial query).

goldensDetail.text: Case sensitivity bypass in email blacklist

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
This calls the email sender with the original guests, so existing attendees included in the input will be treated as new when sending notifications, leading to incorrect emails.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

findings.description: Character class `[a-zA-Z-_]` treats `-` as a range operator, so dashed-locale files fail to resolve to the English file and crash the build. — WHAT: The regex `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` does not treat `-` as a literal character — it parses `-_` as the range `Z`..`_`, so dashed locale codes are not matched. WHY: For any message file whose locale contains a dash (e.g. `messages_zh-CN.properties`, `messages_pt-BR.properties`, `messages_sr-Latn.properties`), the substitution to `_en.properties` silently fails, leaving `englishFile` pointing at a non-existent path, and `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` then throws FileNotFoundException wrapped in RuntimeException, breaking the Maven build. HOW: Escape the dash or place it at the end of the character class.

substring(start, length-end) can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when the common prefix/suffix overlap. — WHAT: `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when `start > value.length() - end` (common prefix and suffix overlap). WHY: If a key's value and sanitized value differ only in length such that the identical prefix and suffix consume the entire string, the beginIndex exceeds the endIndex and the verifier crashes with an unhelpful exception instead of reporting the illegal-HTML message. HOW: Guard the substring when `start + end >= value.length()` (or clamp the end index) before slicing.

PropertyResourceBundle reads UTF-8 message files as ISO-8859-1, garbling all non-ASCII text in comparisons and violation output. — WHAT: `PropertyResourceBundle(FileInputStream)` reads the `.properties` files with the ISO-8859-1 default of `Properties.load(InputStream)`, but Keycloak's message files are UTF-8. WHY: every non-ASCII character (Lithuanian/Slovak/Danish/Norwegian/Hungarian letters) is mis-decoded, so the sanitizer comparison runs on garbled strings and any reported violation message renders as mojibake, hurting the tool's ability to show translators what to fix. HOW: read with an explicit UTF-8 Reader, e.g. `new PropertyResourceBundle(new InputStreamReader(fis, StandardCharsets.UTF_8))`, at both line 68 and line 77.

findings.description: Device-limit error propagates into Authenticate and rejects anonymous access instead of just skipping tracking. — WHAT: Authenticate returns `nil, err` when TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, so a tracking/limit error hard-fails anonymous authentication. WHY: when device_limit is reached, any new (or >30d-idle) anonymous device gets ErrDeviceLimitReached from updateDevice and the anonymous client returns an error, rejecting the user's request (401/500) instead of allowing anonymous access; this turns a stats/anti-abuse limit into an access-control gate. HOW: treat ErrDeviceLimitReached as non-fatal — log it and still return the anonymous identity (only fail if the feature truly intends to deny access, in which case the error should be a deliberate auth error type, not a store sentinel).

updateDevice's 30-day window conflates stale-but-existing devices with new devices, rejecting returning devices as over-limit. — WHAT: updateDevice treats any 0-row update as ErrDeviceLimitReached, but its WHERE `updated_at BETWEEN (now-30d) AND (now+1min)` also misses existing devices that were idle >30 days (rows are kept until the 61-day cleanup). WHY: a returning device that still exists in the table but was inactive is reported as over-limit, so it is rejected even though it occupies no active slot (CountDevices only counts the last 30 days). HOW: distinguish 'device does not exist' from 'device is stale' — e.g. widen the lower bound to match DeleteDevicesOlderThan's keepFor (61 days) so any non-deleted device can be updated, and reserve ErrDeviceLimitReached for genuinely new device_ids.

Synchronous DB write added to the anonymous auth critical path replaces the previous fire-and-forget tagging. — WHAT: TagDevice was moved from a fire-and-forget goroutine (background ctx + 2min timeout) onto the synchronous anonymous authentication path. WHY: every anonymous request that misses the 29-minute localCache now blocks on a DB INSERT/UPDATE round-trip (plus a COUNT(*) when device_limit>0) before the identity is returned, adding latency to the anonymous hot path and coupling the write to the request context (a canceled request aborts the tag). HOW: keep the non-blocking write for the normal path and only perform the synchronous limit check/write when device_limit>0, or restore the detached background context for the store write.

Device-limit check and insert are not atomic, so concurrent requests can exceed the configured limit. — WHAT: CreateOrUpdateDevice performs a check-then-act (CountDevices then INSERT/UPDATE) with no lock or unique constraint enforcing the limit. WHY: two concurrent anonymous requests can both observe count < deviceLimit and both insert, pushing the tracked device count over the configured limit. HOW: enforce the limit atomically (e.g. run the count+insert in a transaction, or accept that the limit is soft and document it).

findings.description: Async legacy writes use the request context which is canceled when the handler returns, so legacy writes are silently dropped. — WHAT: the async legacy write goroutine derives its context from the request-scoped `ctx`, which the apiserver cancels as soon as the handler returns. WHY: since Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection return immediately after spawning the goroutine, the request context is canceled and `d.Legacy.Create` (and the other legacy writes) fails with context.Canceled, silently dropping the legacy write this PR exists to perform. HOW: use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` (or `context.Background()`) as the parent before applying the timeout.

Storage write failures are recorded against the legacy-duration metric instead of the storage-duration metric. — WHAT: the Create error path records a `recordLegacyDuration` metric for a Storage failure, and the Update error path (line 129) does the same. WHY: storage failures are written into the `dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds` histogram with the storage start time, corrupting the legacy metric and leaving the storage metric underreported. HOW: call `recordStorageDuration` instead.

Delete records the object name as the metric kind label, causing unbounded metric cardinality. — WHAT: the Delete success path passes `name` (the object name) as the `name`/kind label to `recordStorageDuration`. WHY: it creates one histogram series per object name (unbounded cardinality) and is inconsistent with the `options.Kind` label used everywhere else. HOW: pass `options.Kind`.

Delete stores the base logger in the context instead of the enriched logger, dropping log metadata. — WHAT: Delete puts the base logger `d.Log` into the context instead of the enriched `log` (built with name/kind/method). WHY: downstream logs emitted through the context lose the name/kind/method fields, and the enriched logger is unused. HOW: use `klog.NewContext(ctx, log)`.

DeleteCollection records the legacy write against the storage-duration metric instead of the legacy-duration metric. — WHAT: the DeleteCollection goroutine records the legacy write result via `recordStorageDuration` instead of `recordLegacyDuration`. WHY: legacy delete-collection outcomes are written to the storage-duration histogram, so the legacy metric never captures this operation and the storage metric is polluted. HOW: call `recordLegacyDuration`.

Mode3 Update drops the updateWrapper, causing UpdatedObject to be invoked twice against divergent old objects in the two stores. — WHAT: Mode3 Update passes the raw `objInfo rest.UpdatedObjectInfo` to both `d.Storage.Update` and the async `d.Legacy.Update`, dropping the `updateWrapper` caching used by the old code and by Mode1/Mode2. WHY: `objInfo.UpdatedObject` is now invoked twice against two different `oldObj`s (unified-store vs legacy-store current state); since mode 3 writes legacy async/best-effort and legacy can lag, the legacy write derives a different object than the unified store, causing divergence and defeating the safe-measure fallback. HOW: reuse the cached result by wrapping the storage result for the legacy call, e.g. `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, &updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: res}, ...)`.

goldensDetail.text: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.
Bug: calling recordLegacyDuration when storage operation fails should be recordStorageDuration.
Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.

findings.description: cook_method is read in Post#cook but never defined on Post, so the raw_html path raises NoMethodError or silently escapes the imported HTML. — WHAT: `Post#cook` reads `cook_method`, but `Post` defines no such method, accessor, or (in this PR) column, and only `topic_embed.rb:22` passes `cook_method:` (to PostCreator, not to Post). WHY: when `cook` runs on an imported post it raises NoMethodError, or — if PostCreator silently drops the option — `cook_method` is nil and the raw HTML is run through the normal cooking pipeline, which escapes it and silently breaks the embed feature. HOW: add `cook_method` to Post's attr_accessor (and ensure PostCreator assigns `opts[:cook_method]`), or add a DB column via migration.

i.content can be nil for feeds without a content element, so .scrub raises NoMethodError and aborts the job. — WHAT: `i.content.scrub` is called on a value that is nil for feed items that lack a `<content:encoded>`/`<content>` element (plain RSS 2.0 `<description>`-only feeds and many Atom feeds). WHY: `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError, crashing the entire poll_feed job mid-iteration so no subsequent items are imported. HOW: guard the nil with `i.content.to_s.scrub` or fall back to `i.description`.

Check-then-create with no unique index on embed_url lets concurrent jobs create duplicate topics for the same URL. — WHAT: `import` performs a non-atomic check-then-create (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then `TopicEmbed.create!`) with no unique constraint on `embed_url`. WHY: two concurrent jobs (poll_feed hourly + a retrieve_topic, or two poll_feeds) that both find no embed will each create a topic + embed for the same URL, producing duplicate topics — the code's own comment in topic_retriever.rb:36 acknowledges the race but nothing prevents it. HOW: add a unique index on `embed_url` and rescue/merge on the uniqueness violation.

Feed-controlled url is interpolated into raw HTML unescaped, enabling stored XSS via the raw_html cook path. — WHAT: the feed-controlled `url` is interpolated into an HTML string (line 13) without escaping, and the resulting HTML (including the feed's `contents`) is persisted as `raw` and rendered via the raw_html cook path (lines 22/36). WHY: a feed author — or a compromised feed — can put a single quote or `>` in the link to break out of the `href='...'` attribute and inject `<script>`/event handlers, giving stored XSS that executes in the forum's origin for any user viewing the embedded post. HOW: HTML-escape the url (e.g., `ERB::Util.html_escape`) before interpolation and sanitize the imported HTML.

open(url) is used without requiring open-uri, so Kernel#open may treat the URL as a file path and raise Errno::ENOENT. — WHAT: `import_remote` calls `open(url)` on a URL string, but this file (and its caller `lib/topic_retriever.rb`) never requires `open-uri`; only `poll_feed.rb:7` does. WHY: if `open-uri` has not been loaded, `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a filesystem path and raises `Errno::ENOENT`, breaking remote article retrieval. HOW: add `require 'open-uri'` at the top of topic_embed.rb (or rely on a global load order that is currently not guaranteed).

A single missing-embed request triggers a full-feed import, creating topics for unrelated feed items. — WHAT: perform_retrieve runs Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) for a single missing embed URL, and PollFeed imports every item in the configured feed. WHY: one embed request creates/revises topics for the entire feed (potentially hundreds of unrelated topics) and re-processes the full feed on each missing embed. HOW: filter the poll to the requested embed_url (e.g. pass embed_url through and skip non-matching items in poll_feed) or parse the feed and import only the matching item.

fetch_http lacks the embed_by_username presence guard, so an unset setting causes nil.downcase to raise. — WHAT: fetch_http calls SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase without a presence guard, unlike PollFeed#execute which checks SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present? before delegating. WHY: when the setting is nil/unset, nil.downcase raises NoMethodError and the retrieve job crashes. HOW: return early if SiteSetting.embed_by_username.blank? before calling .downcase.

poll_feed crashes with NoMethodError when SimpleRSS.parse returns nil for an invalid/empty feed. — WHAT: rss.items.each is called with no nil check on rss, and SimpleRSS.parse returns nil when the fetched body is empty, invalid, or not XML (e.g. a temporary HTML error page). WHY: a transient feed outage or misconfigured URL makes the hourly job crash with NoMethodError (nil.items). HOW: return early if rss.blank? before iterating.

Protocol-relative (//) URLs are mangled into wrong absolute URLs by absolutize_urls. — WHAT: absolutize_urls treats any href starting with '/' as a root-relative URL, so protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x match and sub(/^\/+/, '') strips both slashes. WHY: the URL becomes #{prefix}/cdn.example.com/x (wrong host/path) instead of being resolved to the same scheme. HOW: special-case '//' before the '/' branch (prepend uri.scheme + ':') and only strip a single leading slash for true root-relative paths.

findings.description: Backup-code error codes are referenced but never defined, breaking specific error handling. — WHAT: `ErrorCode.IncorrectBackupCode` and `ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes` are referenced in login.tsx (and next-auth-options.ts, disable.ts, DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx) but no definition of these members is added anywhere in this PR. WHY: if ErrorCode is a TS enum this is a compile error; if it is a plain object the runtime value is `undefined`, so `new Error(ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes)` yields message "undefined" and the client comparisons `res.error === ErrorCode.IncorrectBackupCode` / `ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes` never match, silently falling through to the generic "something went wrong" message. HOW: add `IncorrectBackupCode` and `MissingBackupCodes` to the ErrorCode enum/object (I grep'd for a definition and found only usages — verify the enum actually defines these members).

onEnable is deferred to the close button and is skipped when the dialog is dismissed another way. — WHAT: handleEnable no longer calls onEnable() after the TOTP code is accepted; it only sets step to DisplayBackupCodes and relies on the "close" button to invoke onEnable(). WHY: if the user dismisses the dialog via the X button, ESC, or clicking the backdrop (Dialog onOpenChange), onEnable() is never called, so the parent's 2FA toggle/state remains stale even though 2FA was already enabled server-side. HOW: also invoke onEnable() when the dialog closes (e.g., in onOpenChange or a cleanup path), or keep calling onEnable() on success and use the backup-codes screen purely as a display step.

TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable gained a third `backupCode` argument but the API module is not in the diff, so backup-code disable likely never reaches the endpoint. — WHAT: `TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable` is now called with a third argument `backupCode`, but `TwoFactorAuthAPI.ts` is not updated in this PR, so the new argument is very likely dropped before reaching the endpoint. WHY: the disable endpoint branches on `req.body.backupCode` to validate backup codes; if it is never forwarded, users who have lost TOTP access can never disable 2FA with a backup code — the request falls through to the TOTP branch and returns `SecondFactorRequired`. HOW: update `TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable` to accept and forward `backupCode` in the request body (alongside `password` and the TOTP `code`), matching the field name `backupCode` that `disable.ts` reads from `req.body`.

goldensDetail.text: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

findings.description: Raw JS arrays interpolated directly into Prisma.sql for = ANY(...) may not serialize to a valid Postgres array parameter. — WHAT: `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`/`buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` interpolate raw JS arrays directly into `Prisma.sql` via `= ANY(${array})`. WHY: this is the first `Prisma.sql` usage in the repo and Prisma serializes a directly-interpolated array as a single parameter whose SQL form is not guaranteed to satisfy Postgres `ANY(...)`; the integration tests only compare `Prisma.Sql` object structure (`toEqual`), so the SQL is never actually executed — it may error or match no rows when run. HOW: expand arrays into a value list with `Prisma.join`, e.g. `IN (${Prisma.join(teamIds)})`, or verify array-parameter serialization against the target Postgres version before relying on `ANY(${array})`.

Widened public options type makes teamId optional, silently yielding empty results for team scope instead of a compile error. — WHAT: the constructor's public `options` type was widened to `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` with `teamId?: number`, but `scope: "team"` still requires `teamId` in the zod schema. WHY: a caller passing `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` without `teamId` now type-checks yet silently fails `safeParse`, collapsing to `NOTHING_CONDITION` (empty results) instead of producing a compile-time error. HOW: keep `teamId` required for the team variant, e.g. define the public type as a discriminated union or `z.input<typeof schema>`, so invalid team-scope options fail at compile time.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org

goldensDetail.text: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

findings.description: AssignmentSource.queued uses an import-time default, so all instances share the module-load timestamp instead of their actual queue time. — WHAT: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at module import time, so every AssignmentSource constructed via `from_integration` (which omits `queued`) receives the module-load timestamp instead of the time the assignment was queued. WHY: the `queued` field never reflects the actual queue time, defeating its purpose and any future consumer that relies on it (e.g. staleness/ordering checks). HOW: use `dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance gets a fresh timestamp.

to_dict() leaks a raw datetime into a Celery task kwarg, which fails JSON serialization and breaks outbound assignee sync. — WHAT: `to_dict()` returns `asdict(self)`, which includes `queued` as a raw `datetime.datetime` object, and this dict is passed directly as `assignment_source_dict` into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs=...)` (sync.py:141-143). WHY: with Celery's JSON task serializer a `datetime` is not encodable, so enqueueing raises `EncodeError` and the outbound assignee sync task is never dispatched — regressing the exact sync path this PR touches. HOW: serialize `queued` to an ISO string in `to_dict` (e.g. `{**asdict(self), "queued": self.queued.isoformat()}`) and parse it back in `from_dict`.

missedGoldens.text: The method name has a typo: test_from_dict_inalid_data should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.
Method name says 'empty_array' but tests empty dict - consider renaming to 'test_from_dict_empty_dict' for clarity.

goldensDetail.text: Shared mutable default in dataclass timestamp
The method name has a typo: test_from_dict_inalid_data should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.
Method name says 'empty_array' but tests empty dict - consider renaming to 'test_from_dict_empty_dict' for clarity.
to_dict() returns a datetime for queued; if this dict is passed in task kwargs (e.g., via apply_async), JSON serialization may fail depending on the serializer, which can cause enqueue errors.

findings.description: MetricAlertDetectorHandler became an abstract, uninstantiable class while still being referenced as a detector_handler, causing a TypeError crash for any metric_alert_fire detector. — WHAT: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with `pass`, leaving four abstract methods (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, `build_occurrence_and_event_data`) unimplemented, so the class is uninstantiable. WHY: `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler = MetricAlertDetectorHandler` still points to it and `Detector.detector_handler` calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)` (models/detector.py:86) without a try/except, so any detector with type "metric_alert_fire" will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler` and crash `process_detectors` instead of returning `None`. HOW: implement the four abstract methods as stubs so the handler can be instantiated, or remove the `detector_handler = MetricAlertDetectorHandler` assignment until the class is actually implemented.

missedGoldens.text: Docstring says this returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. Consider updating the docstring to match the new return type.

goldensDetail.text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains pass, failing to implement its required abstract methods: counter_names (property), get_dedupe_value(), get_group_key_values(), and build_occurrence_and_event_data(). This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.
Docstring says this returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. Consider updating the docstring to match the new return type.

findings.description: Second downsize definition silently overrides the 4-arg version, breaking resize_emoji job with a TypeError. — WHAT: the new `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` redefines and overrides the existing `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`, since Ruby has no method overloading. WHY: `app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`; under the override this binds `dimensions=100` and `opts=100`, so `optimize` hits `opts[:allow_animation]` → `100[:allow_animation]` → TypeError, crashing the ResizeEmoji job. HOW: merge both signatures into one method that detects the options hash.

Loop over-compresses because tempfile.size stays stale after in-place convert, and downsize failures are ignored. — WHAT: the downsize loop relies on `tempfile.size` to reflect the rewritten file and ignores `OptimizedImage.downsize`'s return value. WHY: `downsize` runs `convert ... tempfile.path` in place; ImageMagick renames a temp file over the path (new inode), so the open Tempfile's `.size` (fstat on the original fd) keeps returning the pre-downsize size — the loop always runs all 5 iterations (over-compressing the image), and `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` stores the original filesize instead of the downsized one. A failed convert also returns false and is silently retried 5 times. HOW: re-stat the path after each downsize (`tempfile.size` after closing/rewinding, or read `File.size(tempfile.path)`) and break when downsize returns false.

Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores max_attachment_size_kb/max_image_size_kb site settings, blocking valid uploads and misreporting the limit. — WHAT: the client-side size check hardcodes `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024`, replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` (and `max_image_size_kb` in the 413 handler). WHY: non-image attachments are never downsized server-side, so sites configured with `max_attachment_size_kb` (or `max_image_size_kb`) above 10MB now reject valid uploads client-side, and the error message always reports 10240 KB regardless of admin settings — a regression from the previous per-type site setting. HOW: keep the 10MB cap only for images (which get downsized) and fall back to the site setting for attachments.

Auto-downsize flattens animated GIFs to a single frame for direct uploads because allow_animation detection keys off the extension-less tempfile path. — WHAT: The auto-downsize call passes `allow_animation: true`, but `OptimizedImage.optimize` only selects the animated instruction method when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, and `from` is `tempfile.path` which has no `.gif` extension for direct file uploads. WHY: Animated GIFs larger than `max_image_size_kb` are downsized via `downsize_instructions` (`convert #{from}[0] ...`), which keeps only the first frame and silently destroys the animation. HOW: Preserve the original extension on the tempfile (or base the animated-detection on `filename` instead of the tempfile path) so the `_animated` instructions are selected.

goldensDetail.text: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.

findings.description: The update action ignores all params and renders the same response as show, so the embed editing endpoint does not persist anything. — WHAT: Admin::EmbeddingController#update never reads or persists any request params — it renders the same serialized @embedding as #show. WHY: PUT /admin/embedding is a silent no-op, so the 'edit category/host relationships for embedding' feature cannot actually save any changes through this endpoint. HOW: read the submitted params (e.g. the embeddable_hosts with their category_id) and persist them before re-serializing.

update/destroy dereference a possibly-nil host record, causing NoMethodError 500s on unknown ids. — WHAT: update and destroy fetch the host with EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and use it without a nil guard. WHY: when the id is missing/unknown, host is nil, so save_host(nil) crashes on nil.host= and host.destroy raises NoMethodError, returning a 500 instead of a 404. HOW: raise Discourse::NotFound (or render_json_error) when the record is not found before proceeding.

before_validation dereferences host with sub! on a possibly-nil value, crashing instead of failing validation. — WHAT: the before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! without guarding for a nil host. WHY: when host is nil (e.g. a create request missing embeddable_host[host]), nil.sub! raises NoMethodError and aborts the save with a 500 instead of surfacing a validation error. HOW: coerce with to_s and use the non-bang sub so a blank value falls through to the format validation.

Host matching is case-sensitive on the input side, breaking embeds from hosts whose URL/referer uses an uppercase hostname. — WHAT: record_for_host lowercases the DB column (lower(host)) but compares it against the raw uri.host, which Ruby's URI does not downcase. WHY: an uppercase hostname in the referer or embed_url (e.g. 'http://Example.com/page') fails to match a stored 'example.com' host, so host_allowed? returns false and legitimate embeds are rejected with 'invalid referer host' (or silently skipped by TopicRetriever#invalid_host?). HOW: downcase the host before the lookup, e.g. `host = uri.host.downcase` or use `where("lower(host) = lower(?)", host).first`.

missedGoldens.text: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s n

goldensDetail.text: NoMethodError before_validation in EmbeddableHost

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

findings.description: String/Symbol locale mismatch in FallbackLocaleList#[] causes the default locale file to be loaded twice and pollutes the loaded-locales cache. — WHAT: FallbackLocaleList#[] mixes a String locale (from I18n.locale, set to a String in set_locale) with Symbol fallbacks (SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en). WHY: ensure_loaded! then feeds both forms to I18n.ensure_loaded! -> load_locale, which keys @loaded_locales by raw value and loads the file matching /\.#{locale}\.yml$/; on an English/default-locale site self["en"] returns ["en", :en], so en.yml is loaded twice and @loaded_locales ends up polluted with both "en" and :en. HOW: normalize the locale to a symbol so the list and the loaded-locales cache are consistent.

Unguarded .to_sym on SiteSetting.default_locale would raise NoMethodError if the setting is nil. — WHAT: SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym raises NoMethodError if default_locale is ever nil. WHY: any request whose locale resolves via a nil default_locale would crash in set_locale's I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! (self[nil] -> [nil, nil.to_sym, :en]). HOW: guard the nil/empty case, e.g. use (SiteSetting.default_locale.presence || 'en').to_sym.

Fallback translations resolved via default_locale are cached without default_locale in the key, leaving stale text when default_locale changes. — WHAT: The fallback chain now depends on the runtime-mutable `SiteSetting.default_locale`, but the translate_accelerator's LRU cache (key `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{backend.object_id}"` in translate_accelerator.rb:72) does not include default_locale, so a translation missing in the user's locale is resolved via default_locale and cached under the user-locale key. WHY: when an admin changes `default_locale` at runtime without an `I18n.reload!` (which resets `@cache`), subsequent lookups for that key keep returning the old default locale's fallback text. HOW: invalidate the accelerator cache when `default_locale` changes (e.g. call `I18n.reload!`), or fold `SiteSetting.default_locale` into the cache key.

findings.description: Billing flag inversion drops the org `slug` when team billing is disabled. — WHAT: The `slug` condition was inverted from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`. WHY: When team billing is disabled, newly created organizations now get `slug: null` on the Team record, which breaks org subdomain routing and defeats the slug-collision check (which queries `slug === slug`); when billing is enabled, the slug is now written directly instead of being held as `requestedSlug` pending payment. HOW: Restore the negation on the slug branch (keep the requestedSlug branch as-is).

Empty destinationCalendar array causes a null dereference in EventManager.create for Google Meet bookings. — WHAT: When no destination calendar exists, this now emits `destinationCalendar: []`, and the consumer in packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []; if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")` — dereferencing `.integration` without optional chaining. WHY: For a Google Meet booking with no destination calendar, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined and `.integration` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`, crashing booking confirmation instead of falling back to Cal Video (the old `?.integration` check was null-safe). HOW: Add optional chaining in EventManager: `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` (consistent with all sibling CalendarService consumers).

findings.description: Member routes expose the group id as params[:id], but add_members/remove_member require params[:group_id], causing a 400 on every request. — WHAT: add_members (and remove_member, line 85) read the group id with params.require(:group_id), but the routes define `delete "members"` and `put "members"` as member routes whose id param is :id, not :group_id. WHY: params.require(:group_id) raises ActionController::ParameterMissing, so every add/remove-members request returns 400 and both features are broken. HOW: use params.require(:id) (or params[:id]) to read the group id.

totalPages uses floor+1 instead of ceil, producing an extra empty page when member count is a multiple of the page size. — WHAT: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which overcounts by one whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit. WHY: for e.g. 50 members with limit 50 it shows 2 pages instead of 1, leaving the 'next' control enabled on the real last page and navigating to a phantom empty page (showingLast never becomes true). HOW: compute total pages as Math.ceil(user_count / limit).

findings.description: Conditional UI gating matches any passwordless WebAuthn credential, not only discoverable passkeys, potentially leaving non-discoverable-key users stuck in re-auth. — WHAT: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled gates the passkey conditional UI on currentUser.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(webauthnAuth.getCredentialType()), which is true for ANY WebAuthn passwordless credential — including non-discoverable security keys — not just discoverable passkeys that conditional UI actually supports. WHY: a user whose only passwordless credential is non-discoverable will be treated as passkey-enabled (PasswordForm.configuredFor now returns true for them), the conditional UI is rendered but cannot present their credential, and if they have no password they are stuck on a password form they cannot submit, breaking re-auth. HOW: verify getCredentialType() resolves to the stored credential type and, if the intent is passkey-only conditional UI, filter to discoverable/resident credentials rather than the generic isConfiguredFor(type) check.

Unverified `authenticators.authenticators` accessor and missing JS consumption may make the new authn_select form a no-op, silently breaking passkey re-auth. — WHAT: the new authn_select form iterates `authenticators.authenticators`, but this accessor is used nowhere else in the base theme and no `setAttribute("authenticators", ...)` exists in any in-scope file, so the attribute shape produced by AbstractWebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm is unverified; the diff also contains no JS change consuming the new `authn_use_chk` inputs. WHY: if fillContextForm exposes the credential list under a different key/shape (or passkeysConditionalAuth.js does not read the authn_select form), the re-auth allowCredentials list is never populated and the passkey re-auth fix silently does nothing or the template fails to render. HOW: confirm fillContextForm sets an object exposing getAuthenticators() (to satisfy `authenticators.authenticators`) and that passkeysConditionalAuth.js reads the `authn_use_chk` hidden inputs to build allowCredentials when isUserIdentified is true.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is sti

goldensDetail.text: ConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called without UserModel parameter

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

findings.description: Missing re-check after acquiring the write lock allows redundant recomputation and cache clobbering under concurrent first access. — WHAT: the double-checked locking is incomplete — after acquiring the exclusive lock the cache is not re-checked before recomputing. WHY: concurrent callers that passed the fast-path check while the cache was empty will each serialize on the lock and re-read/decode the manifest from disk, defeating the cache, and a transient read failure in one of them can overwrite a just-populated valid cache with nil (since result is nil on error) and return an error despite a valid cached value existing. HOW: re-check the cache under the write lock before recomputing.

goldensDetail.text: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

findings.description: Unconditional `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` access raises KeyError for integrations whose metadata lacks `sender` (which post_install only sets conditionally). — WHAT: The new sender check reads `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` unconditionally, but `post_install` only sets `metadata["sender"]` under `if state.get("sender")` (lines 376-377), and no pipeline view binds `sender` into state. WHY: When the re-install branch is reached (Integration exists but has no OrganizationIntegration), any Integration whose metadata lacks `sender` — including every install created by this new flow, since only `github_authenticated_user` is bound — raises `KeyError: 'sender'`, crashing the pipeline with a 500 instead of showing the failure page. HOW: Guard the access and treat a missing sender as unverifiable (or bind `sender` into pipeline state in OAuthLoginView so the comparison has a value to check): e.g. `sender = integration.metadata.get("sender") or {}` then compare `sender.get("login")` and return `error(...)` when it is absent.

Sender validation is skipped (fails open) when the Integration hasn't been created yet because the legacy DoesNotExist handler returns next_step before the new validation block runs. — WHAT: The sender validation added by this PR fails open when the Integration record does not yet exist — the earlier `except Integration.DoesNotExist: return pipeline.next_step()` short-circuits before the new validation block, so an install proceeds without comparing the authenticated GitHub user to the app installer. WHY: During the race window where the GitHub `installation` webhook has not yet created the Integration, the user is never validated against `metadata["sender"]["login"]`, undermining the exact security guarantee this PR adds. HOW: Fail closed — return `error(request, self.active_organization)` from the `except Integration.DoesNotExist` handler (or otherwise ensure the missing-integration path cannot bypass validation).

get_user_info's GitHub API call is not error-handled, so a transient GitHub/network failure crashes with a 500 instead of the friendly error page. — WHAT: `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` performs an HTTP request to GitHub but is not wrapped in error handling, unlike the token-exchange `safe_urlread` call which is wrapped in try/except. WHY: A network failure, GitHub 5xx/rate-limit, or non-dict response from the /user API raises an unhandled exception (or a TypeError from `"login" not in None`) and returns a 500, instead of the friendly `github-integration-failed` page the rest of the flow uses. HOW: Wrap the call in try/except and fall back to the error page on failure, mirroring the token-exchange block.

goldensDetail.text: Null reference if github_authenticated_user state is missing

findings.description: Constructor null-checks grantType twice instead of rawTokenId, leaving rawTokenId unvalidated. — WHAT: The constructor's fourth null-check validates `grantType` a second time instead of `rawTokenId`. WHY: `rawTokenId` can be null without any exception, so a malformed context can flow into `encodeTokenId` (producing a token id ending in ":null") or a null raw id downstream; the intended guard silently does nothing. HOW: replace the duplicated argument with `rawTokenId`.

New Context.getGrantType() is dead code, so grant type is never recorded on the client session and initial tokens always encode grant type as UNKNOWN. — WHAT: The grant type captured in `Context.grantType` (line 102) and exposed via `getGrantType()` (line 173) is never consumed anywhere — no caller sets `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` on the client session context. WHY: `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` reads `clientSessionContext.getAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE)` which is only ever set in the refresh flow (TokenManager:248), so every freshly issued token (authorization_code, password, client_credentials, etc.) encodes grant type "na"/UNKNOWN, defeating the PR's grant-type feature. HOW: in the token-issuance path, propagate the value before token creation, e.g. `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType())`, using the new getter.

Unchecked dereference of clientSession.getUserSession() can NPE during token issuance and ignores the userSession already passed to initToken. — WHAT: `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` dereferences `clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession()` and immediately calls `getPersistenceState()` with no null guard, ignoring the already-available `userSession` parameter passed to `initToken`. WHY: when the client session has no associated user session (or `getClientSession()` is null), token issuance throws a NullPointerException; using a different user-session object than the one the token is actually built from can also misclassify the session type. HOW: pass/use the `userSession` that `initToken` already has, or null-check before dereferencing.

AccessTokenContext constructor null-checks grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId. — WHAT: The fourth null-check validates `grantType` a second time instead of `rawTokenId`, so `rawTokenId` is never null-checked. WHY: A null `rawTokenId` is silently stored and later surfaces as the string "null" in `encodeTokenId` (or an NPE at a caller), defeating the constructor's defensive contract. HOW: change the argument to `rawTokenId`.

Context.grantType is captured but never consumed, so non-refresh tokens always encode grant type "na". — WHAT: The `grantType` captured into `Context` (line 102) and exposed via `getGrantType()` (line 173) is never propagated to the client session context attribute that `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` reads. WHY: The token encoder reads the grant type from `clientSessionContext.getAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`, which is only written in `TokenManager.validateToken` (refresh flow), so every token issued via authorization_code, client_credentials, device, ciba or password encodes the grant type as "na" — the PR's grant-type feature is non-functional for all non-refresh flows. HOW: in each grant's process path (or where the token is created) set `clientSessionContext.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType())` before token creation.

getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext NPEs when the client session or its user session is null. — WHAT: `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` dereferences `clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession()` without a null guard. WHY: `getClientSession()` returns null when the current client has no authenticated client session (and the session may be null in some flows), so token creation fails with a NullPointerException (HTTP 500) instead of falling back. HOW: guard the dereference and use the already-available `userSession` passed into `initToken` when the client session/user session is unavailable.
