findings.description: add_members and remove_member require params[:group_id] but the member route provides params[:id], crashing every member management call — WHAT: `add_members` and `remove_member` call `params.require(:group_id)` but the routes at config/routes.rb:88-89 are member routes (`delete/put "members"` inside `resources :groups`) that provide the group id as `params[:id]`, and the JS model (discourse/models/group.js:42,53) sends the id in the URL path with only `user_id`/`usernames` in the body — `group_id` is never present. WHY: Every attempt to add or remove a group member raises `ActionController::ParameterMissing: param is missing or the value is empty: group_id`, producing a 500 error and making both features completely non-functional. HOW: Replace `params.require(:group_id).to_i` with `params[:id].to_i` (or change the routes to pass `group_id`), matching how `update` and `destroy` already use `params[:id]`.

remove_member passes an integer id to a through-association delete instead of a record object — WHAT: `remove_member` calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` passing a raw integer to a `has_many :users, through: :group_users` association. WHY: For through-associations, `delete` expects ActiveRecord record objects, not integer ids — this may raise a `NoMethodError` or silently fail to remove the membership, making the remove-member feature broken even after the param mismatch is fixed. HOW: Find the user record first and delete it, e.g. `group.users.delete(User.find(user_id))`, or destroy the join record directly: `group.group_users.where(user_id: user_id).destroy_all`.

totalPages off-by-one when user_count is exactly divisible by limit creates a phantom empty page — WHAT: `totalPages` computes `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` without checking whether `user_count` is exactly divisible by `limit`. WHY: When `user_count % limit == 0` (e.g., 50 members with limit 50), `totalPages` returns 2 instead of 1, so `showingLast` is false on the last real page, enabling navigation to an empty phantom page that shows zero members. HOW: Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with a guard for `limit == 0`) instead of `Math.floor(...) + 1`.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. findings.description: Double-checked locking missing the re-check after acquiring the write lock at line 82, dismissed as a non-material micro-inefficiency rather than a correctness bug. — Double-checked locking missing the re-check after acquiring the write lock.

Error path sets entryPointAssetsCache=nil at line 103, causing a retry on the next call, which is pre-existing and unchanged by the PR. — Error path sets entryPointAssetsCache=nil causing a retry on next call.

Dev-mode serializes every call through the write lock, but this is not material because Dev calls re-read every time and are panic-recovery only. — Dev-mode now serializes every call through the write lock.

Write lock held during a fast file read on a cold-start-only/panic-recovery path is not a material slowdown, especially since the CDN HTTP branch is dead. — Performance lens: write lock held during a fast file read.

goldensDetail.text: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

findings.description: KeyError when accessing integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] if sender key was never set in metadata — WHAT: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` is accessed without verifying that the `sender` key exists in the metadata dict. WHY: The `setup` method (lines 376-377) only sets `sender` conditionally (`if state.get("sender")`), so an Integration that exists with `external_id=installation_id` and `status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE` but lacks a `sender` key in its metadata will raise an unhandled `KeyError`, crashing the request instead of returning a graceful error page. HOW: Use `.get()` with a default or check for the key's existence before accessing nested values, and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` if the key is missing.

Missing redirect_uri in OAuth2 token exchange causes GitHub to potentially reject the token request — WHAT: The OAuth2 token exchange request (lines 416-420) omits `redirect_uri` even though it was included in the authorize URL (line 408). WHY: GitHub requires the `redirect_uri` in the token exchange to match the one used during authorization; omitting it can cause GitHub to reject the token exchange, resulting in `access_token` not being in the response payload and the entire installation flow failing silently with a generic error. HOW: Add `"redirect_uri": redirect_uri` to the `data` dict passed to `safe_urlopen`.

safe_urlopen is called outside try/except, causing unhandled exceptions on network failures instead of graceful error page — WHAT: `safe_urlopen()` is called outside the try/except block, so if it raises a network exception (URLError, HTTPError, timeout), the exception is unhandled and propagates as a 500 error instead of showing the friendly error page. WHY: The try/except on lines 425-429 was intended to gracefully handle all token-exchange failures by setting `payload = {}` and then returning `error(...)`, but `safe_urlopen` at line 423 is outside its scope, so network failures bypass the graceful fallback. HOW: Move the `safe_urlopen` call inside the try block so all token-exchange errors are caught.

findings.category: Fix copy-paste bug in null check
findings.description: Checks grantType twice instead of checking rawTokenId, leading to null concatenation in encodeTokenId. — Line 73 contains a copy-paste bug where `Objects.requireNonNull` checks `grantType` twice instead of checking `rawTokenId`. This means `rawTokenId` can be null without throwing an exception, leading to null concatenation in `encodeTokenId`.

findings.category: Propagate grant type for non-refresh flows
findings.description: Grant type is never propagated to client session context for non-refresh flows, always defaulting to 'na'. — In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java` (line 57), `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` reads `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` from the client session context. However, `setAttribute.*GRANT_TYPE` is only set in `TokenManager.java` (line 248) for the refresh token flow. For authorization_code, client_credentials, and other grant flows, the GRANT_TYPE attribute is never set, so it defaults to 'na'. The `OAuth2GrantType.Context` class was modified to capture `grantType` from `formParams` (line 102) and a `getGrantType()` getter was added (line 173), but this getter is never called outside the class to propagate the grant type to the client session context.

Size comparison validation fails to detect when two grants have the same ID and same shortcut. — The validation on line 82 checks `grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()` to detect duplicate shortcuts/IDs. However, it would not detect the edge case where two grants have both the same ID and the same shortcut, as both maps would shrink equally.

Constructor checks grantType twice instead of checking rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId to propagate into the token ID. — WHAT: The constructor's null-check for rawTokenId is a copy-paste error — it checks grantType twice and never checks rawTokenId. WHY: A null rawTokenId is accepted silently, producing an AccessTokenContext whose getRawTokenId() returns null, which then propagates into encodeTokenId as a null segment in the token ID and into getTokenContextFromTokenId as a null rawId. HOW: Replace the duplicate check with Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed").

Grant type is encoded as "na" for all non-refresh-token grants because Constants.GRANT_TYPE is never set on the client session context for those paths. — WHAT: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext reads Constants.GRANT_TYPE from the client session context, but that attribute is set in only one place across the entire codebase — TokenManager.validateToken (line 248) hard-codes it to REFRESH_TOKEN on the refresh-token path. For all other grant types (authorization_code, password, client_credentials, token-exchange, device_code, etc.) the attribute is never set, so grantType resolves to null and falls back to "na". The PR added OAuth2GrantType.Context.getGrantType() (OAuth2GrantType.java:173) to expose the grant type from the token request, but no code ever reads it or sets the client session attribute from it. WHY: The grant type context encoded into the access-token ID is always "na" except for refresh-token grants, defeating the PR's stated purpose of making grant type available downstream (introspection, userInfo, etc.) for the majority of issued tokens. HOW: In the grant handling paths (or in initToken/createClientAccessToken), set clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType()) before initToken is called, using the newly-added OAuth2GrantType.Context.getGrantType() accessor.

findings.description: Silence drawer never opens in list view: clicking the visible "Silence notifications" button does nothing because the drawer guard requires an undefined rulerRule. — WHAT: GrafanaRuleListItem renders <RuleActionsButtons> with only promRule and no rulerRule, so in the alert list view the "Silence notifications" menu item (which has no ruler guard in AlertRuleMenu) becomes clickable but the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer never opens because RuleActionsButtons.V2 gates it on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` where rule=rulerRule=undefined. WHY: users see a working-looking "Silence notifications" button that silently does nothing when clicked. HOW: either pass a promRule-compatible silence drawer (render SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer from promRule when rulerRule is absent) or guard the silence menu item in AlertRuleMenu on prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(promRule) so the button only shows when a drawer can actually open.

Pause and Delete menu items never render in the new alert list view because their rendering guards still require an undefined rulerRule, despite grafana-based abilities being computed for them. — WHAT: GrafanaRuleListItem passes only promRule to RuleActionsButtons, leaving rulerRule undefined, which makes AlertRuleMenu's pause and delete menu items never render because their guards `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123) and `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165) are both false when rulerRule is undefined — even though canPause/canDelete can be true via the newly-added grafana ability path. WHY: Pause and Delete actions that were available in the old list view (which fetched ruler and passed rulerRule) silently disappear in the new list view, contradicting the PR's stated intent (comments at AlertRuleMenu lines 41-42, 66) to support these actions via promRule. HOW: update the rendering guards in AlertRuleMenu to also accept the promRule-based condition, e.g. `canPause && (rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) || prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule))` for pause and `canDelete && (rulerRule || prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule))` for delete, and pass promRule-derived data to the handlers.

RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.

findings.description: Salesforce Connection uses stale access_token after token refresh, causing auth failures — WHAT: The jsforce.Connection is constructed with the stale credentialKey.access_token and credentialKey.instance_url instead of the freshly refreshed accessTokenParsed.data.access_token and accessTokenParsed.data.instance_url. WHY: The new code refreshes tokens and saves them to the DB, but the Connection used for all subsequent API calls still uses the old (potentially expired) access token, causing authentication failures on every Salesforce API call. HOW: Use accessTokenParsed.data.access_token and accessTokenParsed.data.instance_url in the Connection constructor.

parseRefreshTokenResponse sets dummy "refresh_token" literal that callers persist to DB, breaking future refreshes — WHAT: parseRefreshTokenResponse sets refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token" when the token response omits it, and callers persist this dummy value to the database. WHY: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on, the sync endpoint response may not include refresh_token; the dummy "refresh_token" is then saved via key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token (line 451-452), corrupting the stored credential so all future token refreshes fail. The same issue affects Office365 CalendarService.ts:264 where the spread overwrites o365AuthCredentials.refresh_token with the dummy. HOW: In parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, do not set a dummy refresh_token — preserve the existing refresh_token from the credential instead of substituting a placeholder.

Webhook handler lacks HTTP method restriction, accepts non-POST requests — WHAT: The webhook handler does not check req.method, accepting any HTTP method. WHY: A webhook that writes credentials should only accept POST; non-POST requests reach zod.parse (line 31) and throw unhandled ZodErrors producing 500 responses instead of a proper 405, and GET/DELETE requests could trigger credential side effects if a body is present. HOW: Add a method guard at the top of the handler.

TOCTOU race in findFirst + create/update can create duplicate credentials — WHAT: The findFirst + create/update sequence has a TOCTOU race condition with no unique constraint or transaction. WHY: Two concurrent webhook calls for the same userId+appId can both find no existing credential (findFirst returns null), then both proceed to create, producing duplicate credential rows for the same user and app. HOW: Use a database unique constraint on (userId, appId) and prisma.credential.upsert, or wrap the find+create/update in a transaction.

response.statusText check fails over HTTP/2 where statusText is always empty — WHAT: The success check uses response.statusText !== "OK" instead of response.ok or response.status === 200. WHY: Per the WHATWG Fetch spec, HTTP/2 responses have an empty statusText (no reason phrases in HTTP/2), so this check always evaluates to true ("" !== "OK") and throws even for successful 200 responses, completely preventing token refresh over HTTP/2 connections. HOW: Use response.ok or response.status === 200 instead of response.statusText.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

findings.description: Making .small-action a flex container silently disables button{float:right} without a compensating margin-left:auto, so the action button loses right-edge alignment. — WHAT: Making `.small-action` a flex container (`@include flexbox()` + `@include align-items(center)`) turns its `button { float: right; }` into a no-op, because floats are ignored on flex items, yet no `margin-left: auto` (or `flex: 1` on the description) was added to re-right-align the button. WHY: the small-action button (e.g. topic status action buttons) shifts from the right edge to sit immediately after the description text — a visible layout regression. HOW: add `margin-left: auto;` to `.small-action button` to push it to the right edge of the flex row, mirroring the `margin-left: auto` already added to `.panel` in header.scss for the same float-removal reason.

findings.description: traceID is lost from plugin request logs because LoggerMiddleware.logRequest now relies on FromContext which does not include traceID in context attributes — WHAT: The traceID field is no longer included in plugin request log output because LoggerMiddleware.logRequest was changed to rely on FromContext(ctx) for context enrichment, but neither instrumentContext (in ContextualLoggerMiddleware) nor the new logRequest implementation adds traceID. WHY: Degrades observability by breaking log-to-trace correlation for plugin requests — operators can no longer search logs by traceID to find related plugin request entries. HOW: Either add traceID to the context attributes in instrumentContext (via tracing.TraceIDFromContext), or explicitly append it to logParams in logRequest as the old code did.

Removed instrumentContext call at line 110 results in passing context unmodified without enrichment. — The instrumentContext(ctx, endpoint, pluginCtx) call was removed from instrumentPluginRequest (line 110 in old code). Context is now passed unmodified instead of being enriched with pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, uname. This causes a broader loss of these attributes in logs if ContextualLoggerMiddleware is not properly wired or is misordered, though wiring could not be verified due to wire-generated code.

traceID is definitively lost from plugin request logs because it was removed and no contextual provider replaces it. — The traceID field was removed from explicit logParams in logRequest. Since no tracing contextual log provider exists in the registered providers (only logParamsContextKey is handled), traceID is definitively lost from plugin request logs.

NewContextualLoggerMiddleware constructor has zero production callsites, making its wiring unverifiable. — The NewContextualLoggerMiddleware() constructor is exported but has zero production callsites via grep. While the previous constructor had the same characteristic (indicating wire-generated wiring), the actual wiring of this middleware cannot be confirmed or denied.

missedGoldens.text: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the

goldensDetail.text: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

findings.description: Mutual-exclusivity validation uses truthiness instead of key presence, accepting reports missing both age/timestamp and bypassing the check when both are falsy. — WHAT: `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` test `self.initial_data.get("<other>")` for truthiness instead of key presence, and both fields are `required=False` with no `validate()` enforcing at-least-one. WHY: DRF only invokes `validate_<field>` when that field is present, so (1) a report missing both `age` and `timestamp` passes validation, violating the docstring's "exactly one required" contract, and (2) a report with both present but falsy (e.g. `age: 0, timestamp: 0`) bypasses the mutual-exclusivity check because `if 0:` is False. HOW: test key membership (`"age" in self.initial_data`) instead of truthiness, and add a `validate()` that raises when neither `age` nor `timestamp` is present.

IntegerField is too strict for the spec's DOMHighResTimeStamp (double) timestamp/age, rejecting or truncating fractional-millisecond values. — WHAT: `timestamp` and `age` are declared `IntegerField`, but the referenced Reporting API spec (comments at lines 33-34) types both as `DOMHighResTimeStamp`, i.e. a double that may carry fractional milliseconds. WHY: a spec-valid report carrying a fractional value (e.g. `timestamp: 1714800000.5`) is either rejected with 422 or silently truncated to an integer, dropping/corrupting legitimate reports — a regression from the prior unvalidated dataclass which accepted floats — undermining the collector's goal of capturing real-world data. HOW: use `serializers.FloatField(required=False, min_value=0)` for both fields to accept integer and fractional DOMHighResTimeStamp values.
Truthiness vs key presence check in validate_timestamp and validate_age. — Truthiness vs key presence check in validate_timestamp and validate_age.
IntegerField type mismatch for timestamp and age fields. — IntegerField type mismatch for timestamp and age fields.

findings.description: deleteMany retryCount condition is not scoped to SMS method, deleting non-SMS reminders — WHAT: The `deleteMany` OR branch for `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` is not scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, unlike the first OR branch. WHY: This deletes ANY WorkflowReminder record (including EMAIL and other non-SMS methods) with retryCount > 1, not just SMS reminders — confirmed that WorkflowReminder is a shared model used by EMAIL and SMS methods (see getWorkflowReminders.ts which queries the same model with `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL`). HOW: Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the second OR branch, or restructure the query so the method filter applies to both branches.

Temporary failures (SMS lock, rate limit) increment retryCount and cause permanent deletion of reminders — WHAT: When `scheduleSMS` returns `undefined` due to temporary conditions (SMS sending locked via `isSMSSendingLocked`, or rate-limited via `checkSMSRateLimit` throwing), the new `else` and `catch` branches increment retryCount as if it were a permanent failure. WHY: After 2 such temporary failures (retryCount goes 0→1→2), the next cron run permanently deletes the reminder via `retryCount: { gt: 1 }`, silently dropping SMS notifications that should have been sent once the lock/rate-limit lifts. The PR intent is to stop retrying permanently invalid numbers, not to delete reminders during transient outages. HOW: Distinguish between permanent failures (e.g. invalid phone number from Twilio API error response) and temporary failures (SMS lock, rate limit) — only increment retryCount for permanent failures, or skip the increment when `scheduleSMS` returns undefined due to a lock condition.

Catch block increments retryCount for message-preparation errors (not just SMS-sending failures), causing permanent reminder deletion after 2 transient non-SMS failures — WHAT: The catch block (lines 298-307) now increments retryCount for ANY exception thrown in the try block, which wraps message-preparation code (DB queries like `prisma.profile.findFirst` at line 220, `bookingMetadataSchema.parse` at line 243, `attendees[0].name` access at line 191) that runs BEFORE `scheduleSMS` is ever called at line 268. WHY: After 2 transient message-preparation failures (e.g., DB query timeout, malformed booking metadata, or empty attendees array causing TypeError), `deleteMany` at line 138 permanently removes the reminder — even though the SMS was never attempted. Before this PR, the catch block only did `console.log`, so the reminder persisted and was retried on subsequent cron runs. This is a regression: non-SMS-sending failures now count toward the retry limit and cause permanent deletion. HOW: Narrow the retryCount increment to only catch exceptions from the `scheduleSMS` call itself (wrap only the `twilio.scheduleSMS(...)` call and its result handling in an inner try/catch), or distinguish error types so message-preparation errors do not increment retryCount.

missedGoldens.text: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also

goldensDetail.text: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

findings.description: join() may skip terminating processes when deadline expires due to early break — WHAT: The `join` method breaks out of the process-termination loop when the deadline expires, skipping `process.terminate()` for the current and all remaining processes. WHY: If `next_step.join(timeout)` or waiting for earlier processes consumes the deadline, subsequent processes are never terminated, leaving them running with open Redis and Kafka connections until the main process exits — a regression from the old code which always called `terminate()` on its single process. HOW: Move the `process.terminate()` call into a `finally`-like pattern or iterate all processes for termination after the wait loop, e.g. collect processes that need termination during the wait loop and terminate them all after the loop completes.

Fixed sleep in tests can be flaky; wait on condition instead

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

findings.description: Newly added TotalDocs() call races with watch goroutine's concurrent map write, causing potential process crash — WHAT: The newly added `s.search.TotalDocs()` call iterates the bleve cache map without holding any lock, while the watch event goroutine (started 3 lines above) can concurrently write to the same map via BuildIndex. WHY: `TotalDocs()` in bleve.go does `for _, v := range b.cache` without acquiring `cacheMu`, but `BuildIndex` writes `b.cache[key] = idx` under `cacheMu.Lock()` — concurrent map iteration and map write is a Go data race that crashes the process with "fatal error: concurrent map iteration and map write". HOW: Add `b.cacheMu.RLock()` / `defer b.cacheMu.RUnlock()` in `TotalDocs()`, or move the `TotalDocs()` call before the watch goroutine is started.

missedGoldens.text: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire functi

goldensDetail.text: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

findings.description: remove(String) now performs an unconditional delegate getByAlias lookup, adding an extra database read even when the alias is cached. — WHAT: remove(String) now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) before checking whether the alias cache entry is warm. WHY: This performs an extra database read on every IDP removal even when the cached model is already available, regressing performance for a previously cache-only path. HOW: Keep the original structure and only fetch from the delegate when isInvalid(cacheKey) is true; otherwise read the cached entry and use its identity provider for login-cache invalidation.

Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.

findings.description: V2 client permission lookup uses a non-existent ResourceStore.findByName overload, causing a compile failure. — WHAT: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String) invokes resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()) with a third argument. WHY: ResourceStore.findByName is defined with only two parameters (ResourceServer, String), so this call will not compile and breaks the V2 client-permission evaluator. HOW: Change the call to resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId()).

V2 getClientsWithPermission returns the aggregate 'Clients' resource name as a client id, breaking downstream client lookups. — WHAT: getClientsWithPermission returns resource.getName() directly, which for V2 client resources is the client id or the all-clients resource name 'Clients'. WHY: The caller AvailableRoleMappingResource treats the returned strings as client ids and uses them to look up clients; including the literal 'Clients' type-resource name or any non-id value causes a failure when those ids are later resolved. The V1 implementation strips the 'client.resource.' prefix to return only real client ids. HOW: Return only the client-specific resource names that are actual client ids, and skip the all-clients resource (or strip any prefix the V2 schema uses).

Cleanup listener skips authorization resource removal when only the V2 fine-grained authz feature is enabled. — WHAT: The role/client/group removal listener now only executes cleanup when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled. WHY: If the V2 feature is enabled while V1 is disabled, deleting a role/client/group leaves stale fine-grained authorization policies and resources behind because the listener returns early. HOW: Also enable cleanup when Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, or route cleanup to the V2 management implementation if V2 is active.

registerListener only cleans up V1 fine-grained authz resources on role/client/group removal, missing V2 cleanup. — AdminPermissions.registerListener gates the cleanup of role/client/group removal on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) only, so V2 fine-grained authorization resources are not cleaned up when roles, clients, or groups are removed. The listener should also handle ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 or be made version-agnostic.

missedGoldens.text: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resou

goldensDetail.text: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

findings.description: Team permission check incorrectly requires both admin and owner roles. — WHAT: The team authorization check requires the caller to be both a team admin AND a team owner. WHY: Team membership roles are mutually exclusive (ADMIN vs OWNER), so this condition is almost always false and team admins/owners are incorrectly forbidden from adding guests. HOW: Change the && to || so either role grants permission: `const isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(...)) || (await isTeamOwner(...));`.

Calendar update uses the requester's credentials instead of the booking organizer's. — WHAT: The EventManager is constructed with the authenticated user's credentials (`ctx.user`), not the booking organizer's credentials. WHY: When a team admin or attendee adds guests to another user's booking, the calendar update runs with the wrong credentials and may fail or update the wrong calendar. HOW: Build the EventManager from the organizer user fetched at line 58 (or from `booking.user` with `getUsersCredentials(organizer)`), not from `ctx.user`.

Notification emails are sent to guests who were filtered out as duplicates or blacklisted. — WHAT: `sendAddGuestsEmails` is called with the raw `guests` input rather than the filtered `uniqueGuests`. WHY: Already-attending guests and blacklisted guests still receive an email announcing they were added, even though they were not persisted. HOW: Pass `uniqueGuests` instead of `guests`: `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, uniqueGuests);`.

Email blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive and can be bypassed by casing. — WHAT: Blacklist and duplicate-attendee checks compare emails case-sensitively while the blacklist array is lowercased. WHY: A blacklisted email such as `foo@bar.com` can be bypassed by submitting `Foo@Bar.com`, and duplicate attendees can be created by varying case. HOW: Normalize both sides: `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())` and compare `guest.toLowerCase() === attendee.email.toLowerCase()`.

Concurrent add-guests requests can insert duplicate attendees because the in-memory duplicate check is not atomic and the schema lacks a unique constraint. — WHAT: The duplicate-guest filter runs in memory and is followed by a non-atomic `createMany`, so concurrent requests can add the same attendee twice. WHY: With no unique constraint on `Attendee(bookingId, email)`, two parallel calls both see the guest as new and both insert a row, producing duplicate attendees and inconsistent calendar/email state. HOW: Add `@@unique([bookingId, email])` to the Attendee model and handle the conflict, or use a transaction/upsert that atomically checks and creates.

The organizer query falls back to user id 0 when booking.userId is null and crashes with a Prisma not-found error. — WHAT: The organizer lookup uses `booking.userId || 0`, so a booking without an organizer triggers `findFirstOrThrow` for a non-existent user id 0. WHY: Bookings for collective/team event types can have a null `userId`; an attendee adding a guest to such a booking causes an unhandled Prisma "not found" error instead of a controlled TRPC response. HOW: Guard the null case with an explicit TRPCError, or derive the organizer from the already-included `booking.user` relation when present.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
This calls the email sender with the original guests, so existing attendees included in the input will be treated as new when sending notifications, leading to incorrect emails.

findings.description: Fragile regex path construction can resolve the wrong English source file. — WHAT: The English file path is derived with regex replaceAll on the absolute path using a character class that can over-match and a literal replacement done as regex. WHY: A filename like messages_admin_lt.properties or a path with extra underscores/hyphens can produce an incorrect English path, causing a misleading RuntimeException or comparing against the wrong source file. HOW: Use String.replace for the literal resources-community substitution and a more precise suffix pattern such as "_[a-zA-Z]+(_[a-zA-Z]+)?\\.properties$".

Unescaping sanitized output can mask disallowed markup and let it pass verification. — WHAT: The sanitized output is unescaped with unescapeHtml4 before comparison. WHY: If the sanitizer encodes rejected markup (the stated reason for the unescape is numeric tags and quotes), that encoding is undone, so raw disallowed markup can compare equal to the sanitized value and pass verification. HOW: Compare against the escaped sanitizer output, or only selectively unescape known safe placeholders rather than the whole sanitized string.

Diff substring extraction can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException on overlapping prefix/suffix matches. — WHAT: The substring extraction for the error message has no guard that start + end does not exceed the string length. WHY: When sanitized is longer than value and shares both a prefix and a suffix (e.g. value="ab", sanitized="aab"), value.substring(start, value.length() - end) receives an inverted range and throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. HOW: Clamp end so that value.length() - end >= start before calling substring, or skip the diff truncation if the ranges overlap.

containsHtml fails to detect uppercase HTML tags, causing valid uppercase translations to be rejected. — WHAT: The containsHtml heuristic uses a case-sensitive regex `<[a-z]+[^>]*>` that only detects lowercase HTML tags. WHY: HTML tags are case-insensitive, so an English source string using uppercase tags (e.g., `<A HREF="...">`) is classified as containing no HTML; the verifier then applies POLICY_NO_HTML and rejects valid translations that reproduce the same uppercase markup. HOW: Compile the pattern with `Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE` (e.g., `Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>", Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE)`) or broaden the character class to include uppercase letters.

findings.description: Device limit is enforced with a count-then-write race, allowing concurrent requests to exceed the configured limit. — WHAT: CreateOrUpdateDevice performs a non-atomic count-then-insert/update when enforcing the device limit. WHY: Two concurrent anonymous requests with different device IDs can both observe count < deviceLimit and insert, causing the configured limit to be exceeded. HOW: Enforce the limit atomically, e.g. with a single UPSERT that fails when the count would exceed the limit, or wrap the count + write in a serialized transaction/lock.

updateDevice's 30-day updated_at window can reject legitimate returning devices as over the limit. — WHAT: updateDevice rejects a known device as "limit reached" when its stored updated_at is older than 30 days from the new timestamp. WHY: CountDevices excludes stale devices from the limit count, so a returning device that has been inactive for >30 days can hit the limit branch; updateDevice then fails to match the row and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached instead of re-tagging the existing device. HOW: Either remove the updated_at window filter in updateDevice so any existing device_id can be refreshed, or update the count query and limit semantics to treat stale-but-existing devices consistently.

findings.description: Create records storage failures using the legacy duration metric helper. — WHAT: On the storage-error path of Create the code calls recordLegacyDuration with the storage timer. WHY: This records the storage failure into the legacy-duration histogram with the wrong metric name/labels, making the Mode3 dashboard/alerts misleading. HOW: Change d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) to d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).

Update records storage failures using the legacy duration metric helper. — WHAT: On the storage-error path of Update the code calls recordLegacyDuration with the storage timer. WHY: Storage update failures are misreported as legacy-duration observations, breaking the per-mode metrics contract. HOW: Change d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) to d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).

Async legacy DeleteCollection is recorded as a storage duration observation. — WHAT: The async legacy DeleteCollection goroutine calls recordStorageDuration with the legacy timer. WHY: The legacy write duration is recorded into the storage-duration histogram, so the two stores' latencies are swapped in metrics. HOW: Change d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy) to d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy).

Delete discards the enriched logger values by installing d.Log instead of log. — WHAT: Delete builds a logger with WithValues but then puts the raw d.Log into the context. WHY: The name/kind/method fields are silently dropped from all log lines emitted by this method and by the storage layer it calls, making debugging harder. HOW: Change ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) to ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, log).

Async legacy Create can race on the mutable input object/options pointers. — WHAT: The async legacy Create goroutine closes over the mutable obj and options pointers without copying them. WHY: If the caller or the storage layer mutates obj/options after Create returns, the later legacy write can observe a different object/resourceVersion/options, causing the legacy 'safety' copy to diverge from what was written to unified storage. Mode1 avoids this by passing a DeepCopyObject() into its goroutine. HOW: Deep-copy the object returned by Storage.Create and pass the copy into the goroutine (and likewise avoid closing over the options pointer, e.g., by reading needed fields into local variables).

Async legacy writes are canceled when the HTTP request context ends. — WHAT: Every async legacy goroutine is tied to the incoming request context. WHY: When the HTTP request finishes the request context is canceled, which also cancels the 10s timeout context and aborts the legacy write. Because Mode3's writes to legacy are explicitly a safety measure that should complete independently of the caller, this can leave legacy out of sync with unified storage. HOW: Detach the goroutine from the request context, e.g., use context.WithoutCancel(ctx) (Go 1.21+) or context.Background() enriched with the logger, then apply the 10s timeout on top of that detached context.

Delete success path uses name instead of kind for the storage duration metric label. — WHAT: In Delete the success-path duration observation uses name as the kind label while the error-path uses options.Kind. WHY: The same method emits inconsistent metric label values for the same request, making aggregation by kind unreliable. HOW: Use options.Kind consistently: change d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) to d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).

Create's storage-error path records duration to the wrong metric histogram. — WHAT: On the storage-error path of Create the code calls recordLegacyDuration with the storage timer. WHY: The storage Create failure is recorded into the legacy duration histogram with no legacy call made, so dashboards for storage errors are silently empty while legacy error rates are inflated. HOW: Replace line 79 with d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).

Update's storage-error path records duration to the wrong metric histogram. — WHAT: On the storage-error path of Update the code calls recordLegacyDuration with the storage timer. WHY: Same misrouting as Create — storage update failures are logged in the legacy histogram, corrupting the dual-write observability. HOW: Replace line 163 with d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).

DeleteCollection's async legacy duration is recorded to the storage histogram. — WHAT: The async legacy DeleteCollection goroutine calls recordStorageDuration with the legacy timer. WHY: The legacy write duration is recorded into the storage histogram, so legacy latency and error signals are lost from the legacy metric. HOW: Replace line 200 with d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy).

Delete success path uses the object name as the metric kind label. — WHAT: In Delete the success-path duration observation uses name as the kind label while the error-path uses options.Kind. WHY: The metric label is named kind, so the success path records an object name where a kind is expected, breaking aggregations and making error/success series inconsistent for the same request. HOW: Replace line 140 with d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).

Delete stores the unenriched logger in the request context. — WHAT: Delete builds a logger enriched with name/kind/method but then puts the raw d.Log into the context. WHY: All subsequent logging inside Delete (and in the goroutine which inherits ctx) loses the name/kind/method fields, making correlated debugging harder. HOW: Change line 131 to ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, log).

Async legacy writes can be canceled when the HTTP request ends. — WHAT: Every async legacy write goroutine is tied to the incoming request context. WHY: Once the HTTP response is sent the request context is canceled, which cancels the 10-second derived context and aborts the legacy write — undermining the stated 'safe measure' purpose of writing to legacy. HOW: Detach the async context from the request context (e.g., use context.WithoutCancel or context.Background with a fresh timeout) while copying over trace/logger values.

Update no longer precomputes the updated object, letting Legacy diverge from Storage. — WHAT: Update no longer precomputes the updated object via updateWrapper; it passes the raw objInfo to both Storage.Update and Legacy.Update. WHY: Legacy re-evaluates objInfo.UpdatedObject against Legacy's own old object, so if Storage and Legacy differ the resulting legacy object can diverge from the authoritative storage object, breaking the safety-copy contract. HOW: Precompute the updated object from Storage's state (as the old code did) and pass an updateWrapper with that object to Legacy.Update, or at least pass the storage result object to Legacy.Update.

goldensDetail.text: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.
Bug: calling recordLegacyDuration when storage operation fails should be recordStorageDuration.
Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.

findings.description: Race condition in TopicEmbed.import can create duplicate topics for the same embed_url. — WHAT: Two concurrent imports of the same embed_url can both pass the blank? check and create duplicate topics/posts because the existence lookup is outside the transaction. WHY: Produces duplicate Topic/Post/TopicEmbed records when two RetrieveTopic jobs or a PollFeed job race for a new URL. HOW: Move the embed lookup inside the Topic.transaction and add a unique index/validation on embed_url, or use TopicEmbed.create! inside a rescue for duplicate key and retry.

raw_html cook method bypasses sanitization for externally fetched content, enabling stored XSS. — WHAT: Posts imported via TopicEmbed are stored with cook_method: raw_html and Post#cook returns raw unchanged, bypassing Discourse's HTML sanitization pipeline. WHY: An attacker who can inject content into the polled RSS feed or the embedded page (or who owns a permitted embeddable host) can store arbitrary HTML/JavaScript that is rendered to users as a stored XSS. HOW: Sanitize the imported HTML before storage (e.g., with a whitelist sanitizer) rather than rendering raw external HTML, or keep raw_html only for fully trusted sources.

PollFeed crashes when an RSS item has no content element. — WHAT: line 63 calls i.content.scrub without checking whether i.content exists. WHY: RSS/Atom items often provide description or summary instead of content, causing nil.scrub to raise NoMethodError and abort the entire scheduled feed poll. HOW: Fall back to description/summary and guard against nil: content = CGI.unescapeHTML((i.content || i.description || i.summary).to_s.scrub).

PollFeed processes an unbounded number of RSS items per run. — WHAT: poll_feed parses and iterates over every item in the feed with no limit or pagination. WHY: A large RSS/Atom feed can cause excessive memory use and long job runtime, and the hourly recurrence gives no back-pressure. HOW: Cap the number of processed items (e.g., rss.items.first(MAX_FEED_ITEMS)) and consider parsing the feed with a streaming parser or timeout for very large sources.

Non-atomic Redis setnx+expire can leave a permanent throttle key. — WHAT: retrieved_recently? uses two separate Redis commands, setnx then expire. WHY: If the process crashes between setnx and expire, the retrieved: key is created with no TTL and throttles the URL forever. HOW: Use a single atomic Redis command such as $redis.set(retrieved_key, '1', nx: true, ex: 60).

import_remote fetches URLs before validating the scheme, allowing SSRF to non-HTTP services on the allowed host. — WHAT: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` before `TopicEmbed.import` validates the HTTP/HTTPS scheme, and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only checks the host. WHY: An attacker who can supply an embed_url whose host matches `embeddable_host` (e.g., `ftp://allowed_host/...`) can make the server issue a non-HTTP request before the scheme guard rejects it, leading to SSRF/protocol smuggling. HOW: Add the same `/^https?\:\/\//` scheme guard at the start of `import_remote` (or in `TopicRetriever#retrieve` before `fetch_http`) and set an explicit read timeout on `open`.

Unescaped embed_url in the attribution footer allows attribute injection / stored XSS under raw_html rendering. — WHAT: The embed/feed URL is interpolated into the attribution footer HTML without escaping, and `cook_method: raw_html` causes `Post#cook` to emit the raw string unchanged. WHY: A URL containing `'` or `>` can break out of the `href` attribute and inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript into the embed view (stored XSS). HOW: HTML-escape `url` before building the link, e.g., `ERB::Util.html_escape(url)`.

findings.description: Concurrent backup-code logins can consume the same single-use code because the update is not atomic. — WHAT: The backup-code consumption path reads the encrypted codes, decrypts them, sets the used entry to null, and writes the result back with no concurrency control. WHY: Two concurrent login requests that present the same valid backup code can both read the same codes array, both mark the same index as null, and both updates succeed, allowing the single-use code to authenticate two separate sessions. HOW: Remove the used code from the array (e.g., with splice/filter) and serialize the smaller array, or use an optimistic-lock/versioned update and retry so that the second concurrent request fails and returns IncorrectBackupCode.

Third-party identity-provider guard can be bypassed by sending a dummy totpCode with a backup code. — WHAT: The third-party identity-provider guard is `if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode)`, so it allows the request to proceed whenever totpCode is truthy. WHY: A user whose account uses Google/SAML can log in with only an email and a backup code by also sending any non-empty string as totpCode, bypassing the intended requirement to authenticate through the identity provider. HOW: Include backupCode in the guard so the third-party check is only skipped when a legitimate second factor is present, e.g. `if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode && !credentials.backupCode)`.

Used backup codes are stored as null entries instead of being removed, leaving stale data and hiding the out-of-codes state. — WHAT: A consumed backup code is replaced by `null` in the encrypted array instead of being removed. WHY: Once all codes are used the column still holds an encrypted array of nulls, so the `MissingBackupCodes` branch is never reached and users always see "incorrect backup code" even though no valid codes remain; it also leaves stale single-use secrets in the stored ciphertext. HOW: Remove the used code from the array and, if the array becomes empty, store `null` instead of `[null, ...]`.

Backup-codes state lacks a type and formatBackupCode is referenced before declaration. — WHAT: backupCodes is initialized as useState([]) (inferred as never[]) and the formatBackupCode arrow is used inside handleSetup before its declaration. WHY: This creates a TypeScript contract error and a temporal dead-zone hazard; if handleSetup were invoked before initialization, it would throw a ReferenceError. HOW: Type the state as useState<string[]>([]) and move formatBackupCode above handleSetup (or declare it as a hoisted function).

Successful 2FA enable triggers a duplicate auto-submit because the TOTP value is not cleared. — WHAT: After the TOTP is accepted, handleEnable sets step to DisplayBackupCodes but leaves the 6-digit totpCode in the form, so the existing auto-submit useEffect runs again. WHY: This causes a second enable API call while the modal is still open, which can surface a spurious error or duplicate server-side side effects. HOW: Clear the TOTP value after success (e.g., form.setValue("totpCode", "")) and guard the effect so it only runs on the EnterTotpCode step.

Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

findings.description: The public options type allows omitting teamId for team scope, causing silent runtime validation failure and no-data conditions. — WHAT: `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` declares `teamId` as optional for every scope, but the runtime zod schema at `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema` requires `teamId` when `scope` is `"team"`. WHY: TypeScript callers can pass `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` without `teamId`, which compiles but fails `safeParse`, so the constructor sets `this.options` to `null` and all authorization conditions silently degrade to `1=0` (no bookings returned). HOW: Make `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` a discriminated union matching the zod schema, or reuse `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` as the constructor parameter type.

goldensDetail.text: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

findings.description: Dataclass default evaluates timezone.now() at class definition, giving all instances the same queued timestamp. — WHAT: The `queued` field uses `timezone.now()` as a dataclass default, which is evaluated once when the class is defined, so every `AssignmentSource` instance created via `from_integration` carries the same timestamp. WHY: The field is intended to record when the assignment source was queued, but it actually records module-import time, making any future ordering, TTL, or latency logic incorrect. HOW: Replace the default with `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance gets a fresh timestamp at creation time.

Abstract sync_status_outbound signature changed to include assignment_source but implementations and caller were not updated, creating a contract break. — WHAT: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` method was extended with an `assignment_source` parameter, but the concrete implementation in `src/sentry/integrations/example/integration.py` still uses the old three-argument signature and the only task caller does not pass the new argument. WHY: This leaves the interface contract inconsistent; any future caller or test that passes `assignment_source` to the example integration (or any other implementation not updated) will raise a TypeError, and type checkers will flag the implementation as not overriding the abstract signature. HOW: Either remove `assignment_source` from the abstract status-sync method if it is not needed (the change appears unrelated to status sync), or update all implementations and the caller in `sync_status_outbound.py` to accept and pass it consistently.

Dataclass default `timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class definition, causing shared timestamps across AssignmentSource instances. — WHAT: The `queued` field uses `timezone.now()` as a dataclass default, which is evaluated once when the class is defined, not per instance. WHY: Every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` value will carry the same frozen timestamp, breaking time-tracking semantics and potentially affecting equality/hashing for the frozen dataclass. HOW: Use a `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead of `timezone.now()` so each instance gets its own current timestamp.

Method name says 'empty_array' but tests empty dict - consider renaming to 'test_from_dict_empty_dict' for clarity.

findings.description: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and will crash when Detector.detector_handler tries to instantiate it. — WHAT: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but does not implement any of its abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data), so the class is abstract and cannot be instantiated. WHY: Detector.detector_handler instantiates group_type.detector_handler(self) at runtime, which will raise TypeError for any detector whose group type is MetricAlertFire. HOW: Either restore the concrete evaluate override on a non-abstract base, or add stub implementations of the four required abstract methods to MetricAlertDetectorHandler.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler became abstract but is still registered as a concrete detector handler, causing instantiation failures. — WHAT: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, making it uninstantiable. WHY: MetricAlertFire.detector_handler points to this class, and Detector.detector_handler instantiates it with the detector, so any metric_alert_fire detector will raise TypeError at runtime. HOW: Either implement the required abstract methods (get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data) in MetricAlertDetectorHandler, or mark it as an ABC and do not assign it as a concrete detector_handler for MetricAlertFire.

This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.
Docstring says this returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. Consider updating the docstring to match the new return type.

findings.description: Duplicate Ruby method definition overwrites the original downsize signature and breaks resize_emoji. — WHAT: The PR adds a second `downsize` class method, but Ruby method definitions do not overload by arity, so the second definition overwrites the first. WHY: The existing caller `resize_emoji.rb:14` invokes `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with five positional arguments; with only the four-argument method remaining, `opts` binds to the integer `100`, and `optimize` crashes when it evaluates `!!opts[:allow_animation]`. HOW: Keep a single `downsize` method and normalize the dimensions argument inside it, e.g. `dimensions = max_width.is_a?(String) ? max_width : "#{max_width}x#{max_height}"`, or rename the new four-argument variant.

API URL downloads bypass configured max upload size and use a hardcoded 10 MB cap. — WHAT: `FileHelper.download` now enforces a hard 10 MB limit instead of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. WHY: API-provided upload URLs can now fetch files far larger than the configured site limit, and non-image URL uploads are no longer rejected by size at all before reaching `Upload.create_for`. HOW: Restore the site-setting limit for the download, or apply the larger 10 MB cap only when the target is an image that will be downsized.

Downsizing loop retries blindly and falls through with oversized files on failure. — WHAT: The downsizing loop ignores the return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` and exits after a fixed number of attempts. WHY: If ImageMagick fails (corrupt/unsupported image) or the resized file remains above `max_image_size_kb` after five iterations, the code proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with an oversized tempfile, likely causing a server-side validation error instead of a clear early failure. HOW: Check the result of `downsize` and abort/return an error if it fails or if the file is still too large after the last attempt.

Client-side upload validation hardcodes 10 MB and ignores configured limits. — WHAT: Client-side file-size validation now uses a hardcoded 10 MB limit instead of the per-type site setting. WHY: `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` respected admin-configured limits for images and attachments; the hardcoded value breaks both, allowing users to select files the server rejects and showing the wrong maximum. HOW: Restore the site-setting lookup, e.g. `var maxSizeKB = Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'];`.

413 error handler reports a hardcoded 10 MB limit instead of the site setting. — WHAT: The 413 error handler now reports a hardcoded 10 MB maximum. WHY: The message no longer matches the actual server-side limit configured by the admin, misleading users when a request is rejected. HOW: Use the site setting that corresponds to the upload type, or if the type is not available here, report the configured image/attachment limit consistently with `validateUploadedFile`.

Animated GIF auto-downsizing fails because gifsicle receives an unsupported percentage resize argument. — WHAT: Animated GIF downsizing passes '80%' as dimensions to gifsicle's `--resize-fit`, but gifsicle expects pixel dimensions or `--resize-fit-scale` with a fraction. WHY: For uploaded GIFs, OptimizedImage.optimize selects downsize_instructions_animated → resize_instructions_animated, producing `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80%`, which gifsicle rejects; convert_with returns false, the loop retries five times, and the oversized GIF is uploaded unmodified. HOW: Compute target pixel dimensions from the image size before calling downsize, or route animated downsizing through a gifsicle-compatible scale syntax (e.g. `--resize-fit-scale 0.8`).

goldensDetail.text: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.

findings.description: Missing record guard in update/destroy causes 500 on unknown ids. — WHAT: update and destroy look up an EmbeddableHost with .first but do not check for nil before calling save_host / destroy. WHY: A request for a non-existent id raises NoMethodError instead of a 404. HOW: Add `raise Discourse::NotFound unless host` after the lookup in both actions.

save_host dereferences nested params without a presence guard. — WHAT: save_host accesses params[:embeddable_host][:host] and [:category_id] without verifying the nested param exists. WHY: A request missing the embeddable_host key crashes with NoMethodError on nil[]. HOW: Require and permit the nested params, e.g. `embed_params = params.require(:embeddable_host).permit(:host, :category_id)`, then read from embed_params.

before_validation returns nil for most hosts and halts validation. — WHAT: The before_validation block returns the value of the last sub!, which is nil when the host has no trailing path. WHY: In Rails 4 a falsey before_validation return halts the callback chain and causes save to fail silently for normal hosts. HOW: Make the callback return truthy, e.g. use non-mutating sub or end with `true`.

Case-insensitive host lookup only lowercases the database column, causing uppercase stored hosts to fail matching. — WHAT: record_for_host compares lower(host) against the raw URI host without lowercasing the input, so a stored host with uppercase letters does not match a referer with the same uppercase spelling. WHY: A legitimate embed request from a host saved as 'Example.com' is rejected because lower(host) = 'Example.com' never matches. HOW: Lowercase the input as well, e.g. where('lower(host) = lower(?)', host).first.

Host lookup ignores port while the model permits storing ports, breaking port-specific matches. — WHAT: record_for_host strips the port from the parsed referer URI while the model validation and storage allow a host value that includes a port. WHY: A host saved as 'example.com:8080' can never match a referer from 'https://example.com:8080/', so port-specific embed rules are silently ignored. HOW: Either normalize stored hosts to exclude ports in before_validation or include the port in the lookup when it is present and non-default.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

findings.description: Un guarded to_sym on SiteSetting.default_locale can raise NoMethodError when the setting is not yet loaded. — WHAT: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym without guarding against a nil value. WHY: The PR notes that SiteSetting.default_locale is not guaranteed to be fully loaded after startup; if it returns nil, any translation or ensure_loaded! call that resolves fallbacks will crash with NoMethodError. HOW: Use the safe navigation operator so a nil default_locale is dropped from the fallback chain: [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale&.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact.

Unguarded `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` in `FallbackLocaleList#[]` may fail when the setting is not yet loaded. — Guard the call to `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` because `default_locale` is not guaranteed to be loaded when `FallbackLocaleList#[]` runs, which can raise a `NoMethodError` on `nil`.

findings.description: Inverted billing guard sets the organization slug too early when team billing is enabled. — WHAT: The IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED guard for the organization slug and requestedSlug was inverted. WHY: When team billing is enabled the organization now gets its final slug reserved immediately instead of only a requestedSlug, bypassing the previous verification/billing gating and potentially allowing slug squatting or breaking the org onboarding flow. HOW: Restore the original predicates so slug is set only when billing is disabled and requestedSlug is set only when billing is enabled: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {})`.

Inverted billing guard removes the organization slug when team billing is disabled. — WHAT: The `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` guard for the organization `slug` field was inverted. WHY: When team billing is disabled, the organization is now created without a `slug`, which breaks routing and organization lookup for the non-billing flow. HOW: Restore the original condition so `slug` is set when billing is disabled: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`.

findings.description: Admin group membership routes use :id but the controller expects :group_id, causing every request to raise ParameterMissing. — WHAT: Member routes added inside `resources :groups` expose the group id as `params[:id]`, but `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` and `#remove_member` require `params[:group_id]`. WHY: Every add/remove members request will fail with `ActionController::ParameterMissing`, making the membership-management endpoints completely unusable. HOW: Change the controller to read `params[:id]` to match the rest of the admin groups endpoints, or define the routes with an explicit `:group_id` segment (e.g. nested `scope path: ":group_id"`).

remove_member bypasses Group#remove and redundantly saves the group after the join record is already deleted. — WHAT: `remove_member` deletes the membership with `group.users.delete(user_id)` instead of the model's `Group#remove(user)`, then calls `group.save` after the join record is already gone. WHY: It bypasses any callbacks or side effects in `Group#remove`, and if `group.save` fails validation the client gets an error response even though the user was already removed from the group. HOW: Load the user with `User.find(user_id)` and call `group.remove(user)`, or wrap the deletion and save in a transaction and avoid the redundant `save` on the parent group.

Pagination totalPages is off-by-one for member counts divisible by the page limit, leading to an empty final page. — WHAT: The totalPages computed property uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which reports one page too many when the member count is an exact multiple of the page limit. WHY: Users can click 'next' past the real last page and land on an empty page (e.g. 50 members / limit 50 shows page 1/2, then page 2 is empty). HOW: Replace the formula with Math.ceil(user_count / limit) or Math.floor((user_count - 1) / limit) + 1, guarding against user_count <= 0.

findings.description: Double-checked locking is missing the second check after acquiring the write lock, allowing redundant computation and potential nil overwrite of a valid cache. — WHAT: GetWebAssets uses double-checked locking but never re-checks entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the write lock. WHY: A goroutine that waited for the lock may still recompute, and a failed computation can overwrite a valid cached result with nil, forcing subsequent requests to redo the I/O. HOW: Add a second nil check (for non-dev environments) immediately after acquiring the write lock before computing.

findings.path: GetWebAssets (file path not stated in analysis)
findings.description: The write-lock path omits the required re-check of the cache after acquiring the lock, allowing concurrent goroutines to duplicate the expensive build. — The double-checked locking pattern added at lines 41-49 is missing the required second nil check of entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the write lock. Without that re-check, concurrent goroutines can each observe a nil cache, acquire the write lock in turn, and redundantly perform the expensive asset build.

findings.path: GetWebAssets (file path not stated in analysis)
findings.description: Holding the write lock around file I/O causes every Dev-mode request to be serialized, creating a performance regression. — The new write lock serializes every Dev-mode request through file I/O, which is a real performance regression compared to the previous behavior, even though it is not a correctness bug.

goldensDetail.text: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

findings.description: Unguarded metadata key access in the installer-login check can crash the GitHub integration pipeline. — WHAT: GitHubInstallation.dispatch accesses `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` without checking that the `sender` and `login` keys exist. WHY: If an Integration row lacks either key (legacy record, webhook without sender, or partial metadata), the pipeline raises a KeyError and fails to render the intended error page. HOW: Use `.get()` and fall back to `error()` when the installer login cannot be determined, e.g. `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")`.

Unhandled exceptions during GitHub OAuth token exchange and user-info lookup can crash the installation pipeline. — WHAT: OAuthLoginView does not catch exceptions from safe_urlopen or get_user_info, so network/API failures during token exchange or user lookup raise unhandled exceptions. WHY: This turns transient GitHub API failures into 500 errors instead of the graceful error page the surrounding code intends. HOW: Wrap both the safe_urlopen call and the get_user_info call in try/except and return error(request, self.active_organization) on any failure.

Requiring Integration.status=ACTIVE rejects installations that reference existing non-active integrations, regressing prior behavior. — WHAT: GitHubInstallation.dispatch now requires Integration.status == ObjectStatus.ACTIVE before continuing, whereas the old code accepted any existing Integration. WHY: Integrations in other statuses (e.g., DISABLED) that previously allowed installation now surface a generic invalid-installation error, breaking existing re-installation flows without being mentioned in the PR intent. HOW: Restore the previous behavior of looking up by external_id only and binding installation_id before next_step(), applying the ACTIVE check only if it is intentionally required.

findings.description: Duplicate null-check on grantType leaves rawTokenId unvalidated. — WHAT: The AccessTokenContext constructor validates the grantType parameter for null twice and omits validation of rawTokenId. WHY: A null rawTokenId slips through the intended non-null contract, and the duplicate grantType check is dead/ misleading code. HOW: Replace the second Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) with Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, 'Null rawTokenId not allowed').

Potential NPE when client session has no user session. — WHAT: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext dereferences clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession() without checking for null. WHY: If the client session has no associated user session, the next call to userSession.getPersistenceState() throws a NullPointerException instead of producing a safe UNKNOWN context. HOW: Guard the userSession lookup and fall back to AccessTokenContext.SessionType.UNKNOWN when it is null.

Constructor repeats grantType null check and omits rawTokenId null check. — WHAT: The AccessTokenContext constructor validates grantType for null twice and never validates rawTokenId. WHY: This silently accepts a null rawTokenId, violating the documented non-null contract and producing an encoded token id containing the literal string "null" instead of failing fast. HOW: Change line 73 from `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` to `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`.

Unprotected getUserSession() dereference can cause NPE for detached client sessions. — WHAT: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext dereferences clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession() without checking for null. WHY: A detached client session or a null user session causes a NullPointerException when the method calls userSession.getPersistenceState(), crashing token creation. HOW: Add a null guard for userSession and fall back to AccessTokenContext.SessionType.UNKNOWN, or pass the already-known userSession from TokenManager.initToken into the provider.
