findings.description: Pause and delete menu items are hidden in the ruler-less list view because their render conditions still require a rulerRule. — WHAT: The pause and delete menu items are gated on `rulerRule` even though `canPause` and `canDelete` now correctly include promRule-based abilities. WHY: In the alert list view `rulerRule` is undefined, so the conditions `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` and `rulerRule` are always false and the pause/delete items never render, making the new promRule permission checks useless for those actions. HOW: Change the render conditions to allow the actions when the corresponding grafana-prom ability is supported, and adapt the action callbacks/components (e.g. `MenuItemPauseRule`) to accept promRule-based data when rulerRule is absent.

The silence drawer cannot open in the ruler-less list view because it still requires a rulerRule. — WHAT: The `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, but in the alert list view `rule` (rulerRule) is undefined and only `promRule` is provided. WHY: Clicking "Silence notifications" in the list view sets `showSilenceDrawer` to true, but the drawer condition evaluates to false because no rulerRule exists, so the silence UI never opens despite the menu item being available. HOW: Update the drawer render condition to also accept prometheus-based Grafana alerting rules, and ensure `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` can operate on promRule data when rulerRule is absent.

Pause/delete menu items remain gated on the absent rulerRule in the alert list view, hiding actions that the new promRule abilities say are allowed. — WHAT: Pause and delete menu items are rendered only when `rulerRule` is present, even though `canPause` and `canDelete` now correctly include promRule-based abilities. WHY: In the alert list view `rulerRule` is undefined, so users with permission will not see the pause or delete options despite the abilities hook reporting the actions as allowed. HOW: Either make the gates depend only on the combined abilities (`canPause`/`canDelete`) and provide promRule-compatible implementations (e.g. `MenuItemPauseRule` needs a Grafana prom variant), or stop computing those abilities from promRule if the UI cannot act on them.

The silence drawer is unreachable from the alert list view because it requires the absent rulerRule. — WHAT: The silence drawer only renders when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true. WHY: In the alert list view `rule` (the RulerRuleDTO) is undefined, so the drawer never mounts and clicking "Silence notifications" in the menu has no effect. HOW: Render the drawer when the rule is a Grafana alerting rule regardless of whether it came from the ruler or prometheus representation, e.g. `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) || prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(promRule)`, and pass the appropriate rule representation to `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` or add a prom-aware variant.

goldensDetail.text: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.

RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.

findings.description: Empty secret defaults inadvertently enable credential sharing and allow webhook auth bypass. — WHAT: CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY are defaulted to empty strings. WHY: constants.ts computes APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED as the truthy check of those two variables, so these empty placeholders enable credential sharing by default; combined with the webhook's equality check, an attacker can bypass auth with an empty-value header and overwrite user credentials. HOW: Remove the empty defaults or set them to explicit placeholder comments, and make constants.ts require a non-empty value before enabling sharing.

Non-atomic findFirst+create can insert duplicate credentials under concurrency. — WHAT: The upsert path uses findFirst followed by conditional create. WHY: The Credential model has no unique constraint on (userId, appId), so two concurrent webhook requests can both pass the findFirst check and create duplicate credential rows for the same user/app. HOW: Use a Prisma upsert with a unique key, or add a unique index on (userId, appId) and upsert against it.

Office365 credential sync overwrites the real refresh token with a dummy string. — WHAT: The spread assignment merges parseRefreshTokenResponse's data into the credential keys. WHY: When credential sync is enabled, parseRefreshTokenResponse validates only a minimal schema and inserts the literal string 'refresh_token' when the provider does not return one; spreading that object over o365AuthCredentials overwrites the real Microsoft refresh token with the dummy value in the database. HOW: Preserve the existing refresh_token when the parsed response does not contain a real one, or avoid mutating the response in parseRefreshTokenResponse.

Zoom stores a dummy refresh token when credential sync is enabled. — WHAT: Zoom assigns the parsed refresh_token directly to the stored credential key. WHY: When credential sync is active, parseRefreshTokenResponse substitutes the literal 'refresh_token' for a missing field, so the Zoom credential key is persisted with a useless dummy refresh token, breaking subsequent token refreshes. HOW: Keep the previous refresh token unless the parsed response actually provides a new one.

Salesforce refreshes and writes tokens on every call but uses the stale access token. — WHAT: getClient now refreshes the access token and writes the credential on every SalesforceCalendarService instantiation. WHY: There is no token-validity guard, so every calendar operation performs an OAuth refresh network call and a database write; it also constructs the jsforce connection with the old, pre-refresh access_token, defeating the purpose of the refresh. HOW: Check token expiry before refreshing and use the newly obtained access_token when building the jsforce connection.

Salesforce refresh relies on statusText instead of response.ok. — WHAT: The success of the Salesforce refresh request is checked with response.statusText !== 'OK'. WHY: HTTP/2 responses typically have an empty statusText, and statusText is not a reliable indicator of success, so a valid 200 response can be rejected here. HOW: Use !response.ok or response.status === 200.

Webex token refresh cannot accept the minimal sync-endpoint response. — WHAT: Webex uses refreshOAuthTokens when credential sync is enabled, but then validates the response with webexRefreshedTokenSchema. WHY: The helper is documented to return only access_token/expiry from the sync endpoint, while the Webex schema requires scope, token_type, refresh_token, and refresh_token_expires_in, so token refresh will reject under credential sync. HOW: Use parseRefreshTokenResponse for the initial validation and keep the existing credential key fields that are not returned by the sync endpoint.

Salesforce refreshes tokens but constructs the connection with the old access token. — WHAT: After refreshing and persisting a new Salesforce access token, getClient constructs jsforce.Connection with the original credentialKey.access_token. WHY: The current operation uses a stale or expired token even though a fresh one was just obtained and saved, causing the connection to fail or use invalid credentials. HOW: Build the connection from the refreshed key object that was just written to the database.

Webhook handler uses unchecked zod parse, causing unhandled exceptions on invalid bodies. — WHAT: appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) is invoked without a try/catch or safeParse guard. WHY: An invalid webhook body throws an unhandled ZodError, which Next.js converts to a 500 instead of a controlled 400 and may leak stack details. HOW: Use safeParse and return a 400 with validation errors on failure.

parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on failure, making the caller's success check unreachable. — WHAT: parseRefreshTokenResponse throws an Error when parsing fails, but the caller then checks if (!accessTokenParsed.success). WHY: The success/failure branch is unreachable dead code because the helper never returns a failing safeParse result; the helper's contract does not match the safeParse-style usage in the callers. HOW: Change parseRefreshTokenResponse to return the safeParse result without throwing, or handle the thrown error explicitly and remove the unreachable check.

Outbound credential-sync request fetches tokens without authenticating the caller. — WHAT: When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens POSTs only calcomUserId and appSlug to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with no authentication header. WHY: The receiving endpoint returns access tokens based only on user/app identifiers; without verifying the caller, a leaked endpoint URL allows an attacker to fetch tokens for arbitrary users (IDOR). HOW: Include the shared CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET in a request header and validate it in the receiving webhook.

That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

findings.description: align-items mixin is missing -moz-box-align for the -moz-box display variant it emits. — WHAT: The align-items() mixin omits -moz-box-align even though flexbox() and inline-flex() create -moz-box/-moz-inline-box containers. WHY: In Firefox versions using the 2009 flexbox syntax, the container is created but items are not vertically aligned, producing a layout regression. HOW: Add -moz-box-align: $alignment; alongside -webkit-box-align.

align-items mixin emits invalid -ms-align-items property. — WHAT: The align-items() mixin outputs the non-existent property -ms-align-items. WHY: IE10 only supports -ms-flex-align (already present), so this line is invalid CSS that bloats the stylesheet and has no effect. HOW: Remove the -ms-align-items line.

float: right on .small-action button is ignored now that .small-action is a flex container. — WHAT: .small-action is now a flex container, but its nested button still uses float: right. WHY: Floats are ignored on flex items, so a direct-child button will no longer be pushed to the right, breaking the intended small-action layout. HOW: Either remove float: right and add margin-left: auto to the button, or place the button in a wrapper that uses margin-left: auto / justify-self within the flex container.

findings.description: New contextual-logger middleware is unused, so LoggerMiddleware loses plugin/request context fields. — WHAT: NewContextualLoggerMiddleware is defined but never wired into the plugin client middleware stack. WHY: MetricsMiddleware no longer enriches the context with a contextual logger, and LoggerMiddleware now reads the logger from context with FromContext, so pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, uname, and traceID are silently dropped from plugin request logs. HOW: Add NewContextualLoggerMiddleware to the plugin client middleware chain before LoggerMiddleware wherever the stack is assembled.

The extracted contextual-logger middleware is never wired, so LoggerMiddleware loses plugin/request context in logs. — WHAT: NewContextualLoggerMiddleware is defined but never wired into the plugin client middleware stack. WHY: The new LoggerMiddleware now relies on the context containing plugin/request attributes added by this middleware (via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info), so leaving it unwired drops pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, and uname from plugin request logs. HOW: Add ContextualLoggerMiddleware to the plugin client middleware construction (e.g., the wire set or decorator that currently composes NewMetricsMiddleware and NewLoggerMiddleware), placing it near the top of the stack so its enriched context flows through the logger and other middlewares.

goldensDetail.text: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

findings.description: Browser report age/timestamp validators use truthiness and omit a required-one check, accepting invalid reports with zero values or missing both fields. — WHAT: The mutual-exclusion validators for age and timestamp use truthiness checks, so age=0 or timestamp=0 are treated as absent. WHY: A report with both age=0 and timestamp=0 incorrectly passes validation, and a report with neither age nor timestamp is accepted even though the specs require one of them. HOW: Use explicit membership checks and add a validate method that requires at least one field and rejects both.

Browser report age field allows negative values due to missing min_value=0. — WHAT: The age field accepts negative integers because it has no min_value constraint. WHY: Browser report age represents elapsed milliseconds since report generation, which cannot be negative; invalid negative ages pass validation and are counted/processed. HOW: Add min_value=0 to the age IntegerField, mirroring the timestamp field.

findings.description: Monitor context returns the unmodified config instead of the copy with schedule_type display name substituted. — WHAT: get_monitor_environment_context builds a copied, mutated `config` dictionary but returns the original `monitor.config`, discarding the schedule_type display-name replacement. WHY: Issue-platform monitor context events will contain the raw schedule_type value instead of the human-readable display name, producing inconsistent/incorrect monitor context. HOW: Return the local `config` variable on line 168 instead of `monitor_environment.monitor.config`.

findings.description: SMS reminder cleanup deletes non-SMS reminders with retryCount > 1 due to unscoped OR branch. — WHAT: The retryCount cleanup branch in deleteMany is not scoped to SMS, so it deletes WorkflowReminder rows of any method (including EMAIL) with retryCount > 1. WHY: This SMS-only cron job now has a broader deletion contract than intended; if any other code path ever increments retryCount for non-SMS reminders, those reminders will be silently removed. HOW: Move the method filter to the top level so both branches apply only to SMS reminders: `where: { method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, OR: [{ scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().toISOString() } }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] }`.

The unscoped retryCount deleteMany branch can incorrectly delete EMAIL and WHATSAPP WorkflowReminder rows. — The deleteMany OR condition's retryCount branch is unscoped to SMS, so it can delete EMAIL and WHATSAPP WorkflowReminder rows when retryCount > 1. The retry-count deletion branch should be scoped to SMS reminders only, matching the surrounding cron handler's responsibility.

missedGoldens.text: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also

goldensDetail.text: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

findings.description: Unjoined/unclosed child processes and buffers leak on flusher restart. — WHAT: _ensure_processes_alive kills an unhealthy child process and immediately calls _create_process_for_shards, which overwrites self.processes[process_index] and self.buffers[process_index] without joining or closing the old process/buffer. WHY: On a crash or hang the parent can drop the last reference to a running/zombie process and to a SpansBuffer that may hold Redis connections, causing resource leaks that are now multiplied across N flusher processes. HOW: After process.kill(), call process.join() (with a timeout), explicitly close the old SpansBuffer if it has a close method, and only then create and store the replacement.

Flusher join/terminate does not actually join each process and skips remaining processes on timeout. — WHAT: join() busy-waits for each flusher process but never calls process.join(), then calls terminate(); if the deadline expires while waiting, it breaks out and leaves remaining processes unterminated. WHY: Without a real join(), terminate() can be issued against a process that is mid-flush or mid-produce, risking partial Kafka writes and orphan/zombie children; the early break also means shutdown is not applied to every process, violating the ProcessingStrategy join contract. HOW: Replace the busy-wait loop with process.join(timeout=remaining_time) for each process, then terminate/join any still-alive processes, and continue the loop for all processes rather than breaking on timeout.

Memory backpressure check over-counts Redis memory by the number of flusher processes, causing false rejections. — WHAT: submit() sums ServiceMemory from get_memory_info() across every per-process SpansBuffer, but each SpansBuffer connects to the same Redis cluster via get_redis_client(), so the same cluster memory is counted once per flusher process. WHY: With num_processes > 1 the used/available ratio is multiplied by the process count, causing false spans.buffer.max-memory-percentage backpressure and MessageRejected even when Redis has plenty of headroom. HOW: Query memory once using the original buffer (or a single representative SpansBuffer covering all assigned_shards) instead of summing across all self.buffers.values().

Explicit flusher_processes=0 is reinterpreted as one-process-per-shard. — WHAT: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats an explicit `max_processes=0` as `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. WHY: A caller passing `--flusher-processes=0` to disable multiprocessing/spawn no flusher processes instead gets one process per shard, violating the CLI contract and unexpectedly spawning many processes. HOW: Use a None check instead of truthiness: `self.max_processes = max_processes if max_processes is not None else len(buffer.assigned_shards)`.

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

findings.description: Concurrent builds for the same key can create duplicate indexes now that BuildIndex is no longer fully locked. — WHAT: With the coarse BuildIndex lock removed, concurrent callers for the same NamespacedResource can each create and build a separate bleve index before the cache write. WHY: This leaks a bleve index and may leave the cache pointing to an index that misses events written to the other one; for large file-backed indexes it also wastes disk/I/O. HOW: Add a per-key build lock or check GetIndex again under the write lock before assigning b.cache[key], and consider returning the already-cached index if another goroutine populated it.

Removing the coarse BuildIndex mutex allows concurrent builds for the same key, causing file-backed index conflicts and cache overwrites. — WHAT: BuildIndex no longer serializes index creation for the same NamespacedResource, so concurrent callers can build duplicate indexes for the same key. WHY: For file-backed indexes both builders use the same directory path, causing on-disk conflicts, cache overwrites, and leaked index objects. HOW: Re-introduce synchronization around the cache check + build for a given key, e.g. by checking the cache under a lock at entry and using a per-key mutex/once so only one goroutine builds while others wait and reuse the result.

goldensDetail.text: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

findings.description: Login-cache invalidation on update is skipped when the org-aware wrapped `original` reports isEnabled()=false (e.g. organization disabled), leaving stale IDPs in the getForLogin cache after updates that should remove them. — WHAT: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate tests getLoginPredicate() against `original`, which update() obtains from getById() — a method that always returns createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(...), i.e. an org-aware wrapped model whose isEnabled() can be false even when the stored IDP is enabled (this PR's own bean change, 're-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped', proves wrapping alters isEnabled). The cached login sets are built from idpDelegate.getForLogin (raw DB state), so membership is based on the stored flags, not the wrapped ones. WHY: when the IDP's organization is disabled, predicate(original) is false although the IDP IS in the cached login set; if an admin update during that window makes the raw updated model also fail the predicate (hide_on_login=true, broker_public=false, link_only=true), line 405 skips invalidation, the stale id stays in the login cache, and because the login-page bean only re-checks isEnabled (not hideOnLogin/BROKER_PUBLIC), the IDP wrongly reappears on the login page once the organization is re-enabled — the admin's change silently never takes effect for the cached login views. HOW: compute the predicate for `original` from the unwrapped stored model (e.g. use idpDelegate.getById(model.getInternalId()) for the comparison, or add a variant of createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel that exposes the raw model) so the before/after comparison uses the same unwrapped state that determines cache membership.

The login cache accumulates one id set per distinct organizationId inside a single cluster-replicated cache entry with no eviction, causing unbounded growth and O(N) copy on every new organization's first login. — WHAT: getForLogin caches all results under a single revisioned entry per (realm, FetchMode), keyed internally by searchKey = organizationId (or ""), and every distinct organization that renders a login page permanently appends a new Set<String> of internal IDP ids to that one cache value via the merging IdentityProviderListQuery constructor (putAll(previous.searchKeys)); entries are never individually evicted. WHY: in realms with many organizations the entry grows unboundedly (N orgs × the full realm-level login IDP id set duplicated into each org's set), is replicated across the Infinispan cluster on every change, and each first-time login for a new organization performs an O(accumulated-size) map copy plus invalidateObject on the login hot path — total copy work grows quadratically with organization count. HOW: cap the number of cached searchKeys (e.g. only cache the null/"" organization result and serve per-organization ALL queries from the delegate, or bound the map with an LRU-style eviction by re-creating the query without the oldest key), or key the cache by (realm, mode, organizationId) so entries stay small and independently evictable.

Invalidation predicate excludes org-linked non-public brokers even though getForLogin(ALL/ORG_ONLY, orgId) returns them, leaving the new login caches stale when such brokers are created, removed, enabled, or hidden. — WHAT: the new getLoginPredicate() clause `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` makes the Infinispan invalidation helpers (registerIDPLoginInvalidation / registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate) treat organization-linked non-public brokers as non-login IDPs, but getForLogin(ALL, orgId) and getForLogin(ORG_ONLY, orgId) (default method, lines 176-178) return exactly those brokers for members of that organization. WHY: creating, deleting, enabling/disabling, or toggling hideOnLogin/linkOnly on an org-private broker no longer invalidates the `.idp.login.ALL` / `.idp.login.ORG_ONLY` cache entries introduced by this PR, so organization members see a stale broker list on the login page (a newly enabled or newly linked private broker never appears; a broker switched to hideOnLogin stays visible because the bean only re-filters isEnabled) — behavior that was always fresh before this caching layer existed. HOW: drop the org-visibility clause from the predicate used for invalidation (keep only Objects::nonNull plus the LoginFilter reduce), so any login-eligible IDP change invalidates the per-FetchMode login caches; over-invalidation is safe here, under-invalidation is not.

Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.

goldensDetail.text: Recursive caching call using session instead of delegate

findings.description: Client deletion crashes with UnsupportedOperationException when FGAC v2 is enabled because the removal listener now routes into the throwing ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled stub — WHAT: The new clients() override makes the AdminPermissions.registerListener ClientRemovedEvent handler call ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. WHY: When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and the listener (guarded by the V1 feature, which V2 implies) fires synchronously during client deletion, so deleting any client — and realm deletion, which removes clients — fails with a 500 and the transaction rolls back; before this PR the listener used V1 ClientPermissions.setPermissionsEnabled, which performs the cleanup. HOW: Make ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled tolerate the disable path invoked by system listeners (e.g., no-op or delete the client's authorization resources/policies when enable=false) instead of throwing unconditionally.

getClientsWithPermission relies on findByType("Clients") but V2 per-client resources are created without a type, so per-client permissions are never listed — WHAT: getClientsWithPermission iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients", ...), but the V2 per-client resource creation path (AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource) creates resources via resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner) without ever calling setType, unlike V1 ClientPermissions.initialize which explicitly sets resource.setType("Client"). WHY: If per-client resources carry no type, findByType matches nothing and the method always returns an empty set, so its caller AvailableRoleMappingResource.java:229 silently filters out all clients for fine-grained admins; additionally the all-clients type resource (named "Clients") is not excluded from the iteration and can leak into the returned ID set. HOW: Set the type on per-client resources at creation (resource.setType(resourceType) in getOrCreateResource) and skip the type resource (resource.getName().equals(AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)) inside the findByType consumer.

hasPermission passes a possibly-null all-clients type resource to findByResource on realms lacking the new Clients type resource — WHAT: In hasPermission(ClientModel, scope), when the per-client resource is absent, the fallback AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) can return null (the "Clients" type resource does not exist for realms that enabled admin permissions before this PR introduced the type), and the result is passed straight into authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without a null check. WHY: If findByResource dereferences the resource (e.g., resource.getId() in the JPA store), every canManage/canView/canConfigure(client) evaluation for an admin without the manage-clents realm role throws a NullPointerException on such realms. HOW: Return false when the fallback type resource is null before calling findByResource.

MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() override exposes throwing ClientPermissionsV2 stubs (UnsupportedOperationException) to pre-existing callers such as ClientResource.getManagementPermissions (lines 705-720). — Recorded finding #1: MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() override exposes the new ClientPermissionsV2 stubs to pre-existing callers. Verified via grep that ClientResource.getManagementPermissions (management/permissions endpoint, lines 705-720) calls isPermissionsEnabled/resource/getPermissions, which throw UnsupportedOperationException in the new ClientPermissionsV2, so this pre-existing endpoint now fails at runtime through the same changed line.

V1 stores per-client resources with type "Client" but V2 getClientsWithPermission queries findByType("Clients"), so the V2 query misses the V1-created resources. — Recorded finding #2: Resource type mismatch — V1 creates per-client resources with setType("Client") while V2 getClientsWithPermission queries findByType("Clients"), so the V2 query will not match the resources created under V1. The per-resource evaluatePermission loop noted in the performance review sits on these same lines and is not a distinct issue.

The getResourceTypeResource fallback in hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) can be null, creating a null-dereference risk. — Recorded finding #3: Null-risk fallback — hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) falls back to getResourceTypeResource, which may return null, creating a null-dereference risk in that path.

missedGoldens.text: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resou

goldensDetail.text: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

findings.description: Team admins/owners are always denied because the admin and owner checks are ANDed instead of ORed. — WHAT: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin() and isTeamOwner() with && instead of ||. WHY: a team membership has exactly one role, so no user can be both ADMIN and OWNER at once — the expression is always false, and team admins/owners (who are neither the organizer nor an attendee) always get FORBIDDEN when trying to add guests to team event bookings. HOW: replace && with ||.

Calendar attendee update uses the requester's credentials rather than the organizer's, so it targets the wrong user's calendars for non-organizer callers. — WHAT: EventManager is constructed with the requesting user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and {...user}) instead of the booking organizer's. WHY: the calendar event being updated lives on the organizer's calendar, so when an attendee or team admin (not the organizer) adds guests, the attendee/credential lookup runs against the wrong user's connected calendars and the organizer's calendar event is not updated — the handler even includes booking.user.credentials at line 38 but never uses them. HOW: build the EventManager from booking.user and its credentials instead of ctx.user.

Call to EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees has no discoverable definition in the repo, risking a TypeError after the attendee rows are already committed. — WHAT: eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) is called, but a repo-wide search finds no definition of updateCalendarAttendees (or of the EventManager class) anywhere — the only match is this call site. WHY: if the method does not exist on EventManager, every addGuests call throws a TypeError after prisma.booking.update has already persisted the new attendees, returning a 500 while leaving guests added and no calendar/email side effects. HOW: verify the method exists on @calcom/core/EventManager (or add it / call the correct existing method) and handle its failure before or transactionally with the attendee insert.

Guest blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive on the guest side, allowing trivial bypass and duplicate attendees. — WHAT: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased but the incoming guest email is never lowercased before the includes() check. WHY: a blacklisted address submitted with different casing (e.g., Banned@x.com vs banned@x.com) bypasses the blacklist and is added as an attendee; the adjacent duplicate check (guest === attendee.email) is likewise case-sensitive and can create duplicate attendee rows for the same mailbox. HOW: normalize with guest.toLowerCase() in both the blacklist comparison and the existing-attendee comparison.

Raw input guest list is sent to the email routine instead of the filtered uniqueGuests, re-emailing existing attendees. — WHAT: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw input guests array instead of uniqueGuests. WHY: the callee (packages/emails/email-manager.ts sendAddGuestsEmails) emails every booking attendee whose email appears in that list, so any pre-existing attendee emails included in the request receive a 'new guests added' notification even though they were not added by this call. HOW: pass uniqueGuests instead of guests.

Guests can be added to cancelled bookings because the booking fetch ignores status. — WHAT: the booking lookup does not filter on booking.status, so guests can be added to cancelled (or otherwise non-active) bookings. WHY: attendees are persisted and 'guests added' calendar-invite emails are sent for an event that no longer exists, misleading the new guests and mutating a cancelled record. HOW: add a status check (e.g., reject when booking.status === BookingStatus.CANCELLED/REJECTED) before updating.

Null booking.userId falls back to id 0 in findFirstOrThrow, causing an unhandled 500 for team bookings without an assigned user. — WHAT: the organizer is loaded with prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }), which throws when booking.userId is null. WHY: bookings without an assigned user (e.g., collective team bookings where userId is null) hit the id: 0 fallback, findFirstOrThrow throws, and the mutation fails with a 500 instead of a controlled error — even for callers who passed the permission check. HOW: handle the null userId case explicitly (resolve the team host or throw a typed TRPCError).

Adding guests bypasses the seatsPerTimeSlot capacity limit for seated event types. — WHAT: new attendees are created via createMany without any check against eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot. WHY: for events with seats enabled, seatsPerTimeSlot is a hard capacity invariant — this endpoint lets any existing attendee add unlimited guests and overbook the slot beyond its seat limit, which the normal booking flow enforces. HOW: when seatsPerTimeSlot is set, reject if existing attendee count + uniqueGuests.length would exceed it.

Duplicate emails within the guests array are not deduplicated, so createMany inserts duplicate Attendee rows for the same booking and the guest is emailed multiple times. — WHAT: uniqueGuests is not deduplicated within the input array itself — the filter only excludes emails already on the booking or blacklisted, so duplicate emails inside the same guests payload all pass through to createMany. WHY: submitting guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"] creates two Attendee rows with the same email on the same booking (verified: the Attendee model in packages/prisma/schema.prisma has no @@unique([bookingId, email]) constraint, so nothing at the DB layer prevents it), and sendAddGuestsEmails then emails that guest twice — the 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' invariant the handler claims to enforce is not actually upheld. HOW: dedupe the input before filtering, e.g. wrap guests in a Set first.

goldensDetail.text: Case sensitivity bypass in email blacklist

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
This calls the email sender with the original guests, so existing attendees included in the input will be treated as new when sending notifications, leading to incorrect emails.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

findings.description: Prefix/suffix trimming in the new diff-reporting code can overlap and throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the build instead of reporting illegal HTML. — WHAT: the prefix/suffix trimming loops that build the 'Illegal HTML' diagnostic are only bounded individually, so start + end can overlap and substring() is invoked with begin > end. WHY: when the sanitizer strips a trailing fragment whose tail coincidentally matches the kept content (e.g. value 'x' sanitizes to 'x', producing start=8 and end=4 so sanitized.substring(8, 4) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException), the Maven build crashes with an obscure stack trace instead of reporting the illegal HTML, and no further keys or files are validated. HOW: clamp the end loop so the trimmed regions cannot overlap, e.g. while (end < sanitized.length() - start && end < value.length() - start && ...).

Locale-suffix regex has an accidental Z–_ range and excludes digits/hyphens, so such locale files would not resolve to the English bundle and would crash the build. — WHAT: the locale-stripping regex '_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties' uses a character class that is accidentally the range Z–_ (matching [, \, ], ^, _) and excludes digits and hyphens. WHY: a locale file whose suffix contains digits or hyphens (e.g. messages_es_419.properties) would not match, so englishFile keeps the same locale filename under resources/ instead of _en.properties, producing a FileNotFoundException wrapped in RuntimeException that crashes the build; the unintended range characters are also matched. HOW: use an explicit class such as '_[a-zA-Z0-9_-]*\.properties' (or '_[^_]*\.properties') to cover all locale suffixes.

The prefix and suffix trimming loops at lines 103-111 overlap, causing the shared region to be processed by both loops. — The prefix and suffix trimming loops at lines 103-111 overlap: the two loops' ranges share a common region, so trimming is applied to the same characters by both loops. Adjust the loop bounds so the prefix-trimming and suffix-trimming regions are disjoint.

The locale-stripping regex at line 75 accidentally forms a Z-_ character-class range that matches unintended characters. — The locale-stripping regex at line 75 contains an accidental Z-_ range in its character class: the hyphen is interpreted as a range operator between 'Z' and '_', so the class also matches unintended characters ('[', '\\', ']', '^'). Escape the hyphen or move it to the start/end of the character class so only the intended characters are matched.

findings.description: Non-atomic count-then-insert lets concurrent anonymous requests exceed the configured device limit. — WHAT: the device-limit enforcement in CreateOrUpdateDevice performs a non-atomic check-then-act: CountDevices (SELECT COUNT(*)) followed by a conditional INSERT outside any transaction or lock. WHY: concurrent anonymous auth requests (TagDevice now runs synchronously in every request, see client.go:44) can both observe count < deviceLimit and both insert, so the configured device limit is silently exceeded — undermining the limit this PR adds. HOW: enforce the limit atomically, e.g. run the count check and the insert inside a single transaction with appropriate isolation (or use a single conditional INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < limit statement).

Failing anonymous auth on device-limit errors lets unauthenticated clients exhaust client-controlled device slots and deny service to legitimate anonymous users for 30+ days. — WHAT: anonymous authentication now hard-fails when TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, while the device IDs that consume limit slots come from the unauthenticated, client-controlled X-Grafana-Device-Id header (impl.go:119) and occupied slots count against the limit for 30 days (anonymousDeviceExpiration window used by CountDevices in database.go:110). WHY: an unauthenticated attacker can send requests with random device IDs to exhaust all device_limit slots; every legitimate new anonymous user then gets an authentication error (HTTP 401) instead of access, for up to 30+ days — before this PR tagging was fire-and-forget and could never block authentication. HOW: distinguish 'new device rejected by limit' from auth failure (log and continue authenticating, as done for other tagging errors), or validate/rate-limit device-ID claims before persisting them so unauthenticated clients cannot burn the licensed capacity.

Rejected over-limit devices are only rejected once: the failed tag attempt leaves a 29-minute local-cache entry, so a simple retry authenticates and bypasses the configured device limit. — WHAT: failing anonymous auth on ErrDeviceLimitReached (new in this PR) is bypassed on retry because tagDeviceUI in impl.go sets the local cache key (a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{}) at impl.go:146, 29-minute TTL) BEFORE calling CreateOrUpdateDevice and never removes it when CreateOrUpdateDevice fails with ErrDeviceLimitReached. WHY: a new device over the limit is rejected only on its first request; any retry within 29 minutes hits the cache at impl.go:142-144, tagDeviceUI returns nil without touching the DB, and Authenticate succeeds — so the configurable device limit this PR adds is effectively unenforced against every client that retries (enforcement degenerates to failing one request per device ID per 29-minute window). HOW: on error from CreateOrUpdateDevice in tagDeviceUI (impl.go:152-154), delete the cache key before returning the error (e.g. a.localCache.Delete(key)), so failed tags are retried against the store and ErrDeviceLimitReached is enforced on every request.

findings.description: Async legacy writes inherit the request context, so they are canceled as soon as the HTTP handler returns and the legacy mirror write is silently dropped. — WHAT: the fire-and-forget goroutine derives its context from the incoming request ctx via context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...). WHY: DualWriter is a rest.Storage invoked synchronously from apiserver REST handlers (dualwriter.go:127-178), so ctx is the HTTP request context, which net/http cancels the moment the handler returns — the async legacy Create returns immediately with context.Canceled and the legacy mirror write is silently lost, defeating mode 3's 'safe measure' purpose; the same pattern exists in Delete (lines 108-114), Update (lines 134-141) and DeleteCollection (lines 161-167). HOW: detach from request cancellation before applying the timeout, e.g. ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 10*time.Second, errors.New("legacy create timeout")) (keeps klog values set by klog.NewContext while dropping cancellation).

Storage Create/Update failures are recorded against the legacy metrics histogram instead of the storage one. — WHAT: on failure of d.Storage.Create, the error path calls d.recordLegacyDuration(...) instead of d.recordStorageDuration(...). WHY: metrics.go:54-62 shows legacy and storage are separate HistogramVecs, so a storage failure is recorded as a legacy error (with storage timing) and the storage error metric is never observed — dashboards/alerts for mode 3 attribute failures to the wrong backend; the identical mistake exists in Update's error path at lines 127-130 (d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) after d.Storage.Update fails). HOW: replace with d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) in both error paths.

Delete records the per-object name into the Prometheus `kind` label, creating unbounded time-series cardinality. — WHAT: the success path of Delete passes the object `name` as the third argument to recordStorageDuration, which metrics.go:59-62 maps into the `kind` label of the dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds histogram (label set defined as {"is_error","mode","kind","method"} at metrics.go:23). WHY: every distinct object name creates a new Prometheus time series — unbounded label cardinality that grows with the number of deleted objects and can blow up the metrics store, and every other method passes options.Kind so the label is also semantically wrong. HOW: use d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).

DeleteCollection records the legacy store's duration/errors into the storage metrics histogram. — WHAT: inside DeleteCollection's async goroutine, the result of d.Legacy.DeleteCollection is recorded with d.recordStorageDuration instead of d.recordLegacyDuration. WHY: legacy delete-collection latency and errors are attributed to the storage histogram while the legacy histogram never observes them, corrupting the per-backend duration/error metrics that the dual-writer rollout relies on (verified the two recorders write to separate HistogramVecs in metrics.go:54-62). HOW: change to d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy).

Legacy Update recomputes UpdatedObject from its own old object instead of reusing the storage-updated object, so legacy and unified storage can silently diverge. — WHAT: Update now passes the raw objInfo to d.Legacy.Update; the removed code pre-resolved the object (Storage.Get + objInfo.UpdatedObject) and wrapped it in updateWrapper (dualwriter.go:222-238, whose UpdatedObject returns the fixed pre-computed object) so legacy persisted the exact object storage wrote. WHY: rest.UpdatedObjectInfo.UpdatedObject is now executed a second time, inside the legacy store, against legacy's own old object — if legacy's copy is stale (the common case during migration) or the objInfo applies mutations, legacy writes different content than unified storage, so the two backends this mode is meant to keep in sync diverge silently; objInfo implementations are also not guaranteed to be safe/idempotent across two UpdatedObject invocations. HOW: resolve the updated object once (as the old code did, e.g. via d.Storage.Get + objInfo.UpdatedObject before calling Storage.Update) and pass &updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: obj} to d.Legacy.Update.

Update error path records the storage failure into the legacy metrics histogram instead of the storage one. — WHAT: the error branch of Update records the failed d.Storage.Update duration via d.recordLegacyDuration instead of d.recordStorageDuration. WHY: storage update failures are observed in the legacy duration histogram (wrong metric vector) and are never counted in the storage duration histogram, making storage-side update error rates invisible in monitoring. HOW: call d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) in this branch, matching the success path two lines below.

Mode3 tests never await or assert the async legacy write, so the legacy dual-write could be removed without failing any test. — WHAT: the mode3 tests register legacy mock expectations (setupLegacyFn) but never synchronize with or assert the fire-and-forget goroutine that performs the legacy write — dw.Create/dw.Update return before the goroutine runs and no AssertExpectations/WaitGroup/channel is used. WHY: the async legacy dual-write, the core safety behavior of mode 3, is effectively untested: removing every legacy `go func(){...}()` block from dualwriter_mode3.go would leave this entire suite green, so a regression that silently drops legacy writes cannot be caught. HOW: have the tests signal completion from the legacy mock (e.g., a channel closed inside a .Run callback) and wait on it, plus m.AssertExpectations(t), before asserting results.

findings.description: raw_html cook_method serves unsanitized third-party feed HTML as cooked post content, enabling stored XSS from RSS imports. — WHAT: For posts with cook_method == raw_html, cook returns the raw column verbatim as the served HTML, bypassing PrettyText's whitelist sanitizer and the :after_post_cook plugin filter. WHY: Combined with PollFeed doing CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content) (poll_feed.rb:35) and TopicEmbed.import passing no sanitization, third-party RSS feed entries become stored, unsanitized HTML on Discourse topic pages — a compromised or malicious feed on the embeddable host can inject <script> and steal sessions of Discourse readers, including staff. HOW: Sanitize imported content before storing (e.g. run contents through a whitelist sanitizer such as Sanitize/PrettyText in TopicEmbed.import), or have cook still sanitize raw_html instead of returning it raw.

embed.post is used unguarded; a destroyed post makes revise! raise NoMethodError and aborts the whole feed poll loop. — WHAT: When a TopicEmbed record exists, the code uses embed.post without a nil guard and passes it straight into PostRevisor.new / revise!. WHY: If the post was destroyed after the embed was created (no dependent-destroy wiring on TopicEmbed/Post for this association), embed.post is nil, revise! raises NoMethodError, and — because PollFeed#poll_feed loops over all feed items calling import — one stale embed record aborts the entire hourly feed poll (sidekiq retry is disabled). HOW: Skip or recreate when the post is missing.

content_sha1 is updated even when the revision fails, permanently suppressing future content updates for that embed. — WHAT: content_sha1 is persisted via embed.update_column regardless of whether revisor.revise! actually applied the new content. WHY: If the revision fails (revise! returns false instead of raising), the embed row now records the NEW sha while the post still has the OLD body — every subsequent poll computes the same new sha, sees content_sha1 == embed.content_sha1, and skips the update, so the post stays stale permanently. HOW: Only update the sha when the revision succeeds.

Feed items without a content element cause nil.scrub NoMethodError that aborts the entire hourly poll. — WHAT: i.content.scrub assumes every feed item has a content element; SimpleRSS returns nil for elements absent from an item (e.g. RSS 2.0 items that only carry description). WHY: nil.scrub raises NoMethodError, which propagates out of poll_feed and kills the entire hourly job mid-loop — with sidekiq_options retry: false the remaining items are never imported until the next run, which then dies on the same item again. HOW: Coerce to string or skip items without content.

Non-atomic setnx+expire can leave a permanent throttle key, blocking retrieval of that embed URL forever. — WHAT: The throttle key is written with setnx and then given a TTL in a separate expire call, which is not atomic. WHY: If the process crashes or is killed between the two calls, the key "retrieved:<url>" exists forever with no expiry, so that embed URL is permanently treated as retrieved_recently? and can never be fetched again. HOW: Set the value and TTL atomically.

open-uri calls in Sidekiq workers have no timeout, so an unresponsive feed/embed host can hang worker threads indefinitely. — WHAT: open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) (and open(url) in TopicEmbed.import_remote) use open-uri with no open/read timeout inside Sidekiq job workers. WHY: An unresponsive or slow embeddable host blocks a worker thread indefinitely; with hourly polling plus per-URL retrieve jobs, a hanging host progressively exhausts the Sidekiq worker pool and stalls all other jobs. HOW: Fetch with explicit timeouts (e.g. Net::HTTP with open_timeout/read_timeout, or Timeout.timeout) and rescue network errors so one bad host cannot hang the queue.

Protocol-relative URLs (//host/path) in imported content are mangled into invalid same-host paths. — WHAT: absolutize_urls treats protocol-relative URLs ('//cdn.example.com/img.png') as path-relative because they satisfy start_with?('/'), rewriting them to 'http://host/cdn.example.com/img.png'. WHY: any feed or article using protocol-relative links/images (common in RSS content) gets broken links and broken images in the imported post. HOW: exclude '//'-prefixed values from the rewrite.

Port is wrongly omitted for non-default scheme/port combinations (http on 443, https on 80). — WHAT: The port-elision check drops the port whenever it equals 80 or 443 regardless of scheme, so 'https://host:80' or 'http://host:443' produce a prefix missing the non-default port. WHY: absolutize_urls then generates absolute links pointing at the wrong port, breaking links/images for embeddable hosts running on a non-default scheme/port combination. HOW: compare against the scheme's default port instead of hardcoding both values.

Each new embed URL synchronously re-downloads and re-imports the entire RSS feed inside a user-triggerable job. — WHAT: perform_retrieve executes the full Jobs::PollFeed synchronously for every cache-miss embed URL when feed polling is enabled. WHY: the retrieved_recently? throttle is keyed per embed_url, so N distinct article URLs each trigger a complete feed download plus a TopicEmbed.import scan of every feed item inside a job enqueued by the public EmbedController#best endpoint — O(N × feed size) network and import work driven by unauthenticated traffic to the embedded site. HOW: rely on the hourly scheduled PollFeed (remove the inline execute), or enqueue a single coalesced poll job instead of running it inline per request.

Check-then-create on embed_url without a unique constraint allows duplicate topics for the same embed URL under concurrent imports. — WHAT: TopicEmbed.import does a check-then-create (where(embed_url: url).first followed by TopicEmbed.create! inside the transaction) with no uniqueness guarantee on embed_url. WHY: the hourly PollFeed has no throttle and can run concurrently with RetrieveTopic.fetch_http for the same new URL (RetrieveTopic even runs PollFeed itself), and staff bypass the redis throttle, so two concurrent imports can create duplicate topics and duplicate TopicEmbed rows for the same embed_url. HOW: add a unique index on topic_embeds.embed_url and use find_or_create_by (or rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique and reload).

findings.description: onEnable() was removed from the success path and only fires via the Close button, so dismissing the backup-codes dialog any other way leaves parent state stale (2FA shown as disabled) and the modal unrestarted. — WHAT: After a successful 2FA enable (response.status === 200), onEnable() is no longer called here — it only fires from the Close button on the DisplayBackupCodes step. WHY: If the user dismisses the dialog via the X button, overlay click, or Escape (all routed through onOpenChange, line 166) instead of the Close button, the parent is never notified that 2FA was enabled, so the settings UI keeps showing 2FA as disabled even though it is enabled server-side; additionally resetState() is never called, so reopening the modal lands on the stale backup-codes step instead of ConfirmPassword. HOW: Fire onEnable() immediately upon the successful enable response (keep DisplayBackupCodes purely informational), or invoke onEnable() + resetState() from the dialog's onOpenChange handler whenever the current step is DisplayBackupCodes.

Non-atomic check-then-consume of backup codes allows two concurrent login requests to redeem the same one-time backup code. — WHAT: Backup-code redemption is a non-atomic read-modify-write: the encrypted blob is decrypted, the code is located with indexOf, and only afterwards is the nulled-out array written back with prisma.user.update. WHY: Two concurrent authorize() calls presenting the same backup code both read the same ciphertext and both pass the indexOf check before either update commits, so a one-time backup code can be used twice; the per-email rate limiter throttles attempts but does not serialize concurrent in-flight requests. HOW: Make the claim atomic — e.g. run the check-and-consume inside a serializable transaction (or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE), or use updateMany({ where: { id: user.id, backupCodes: user.backupCodes }, data: {...} }) and reject when count === 0 because a concurrent request already consumed the code.

New error codes ErrorCode.IncorrectBackupCode / MissingBackupCodes are referenced in four files but no definition was found — compile error if ErrorCode is an enum, undefined error values if it is an object. — WHAT: This PR references ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes and ErrorCode.IncorrectBackupCode (also in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:55,63 and the two modals), but ErrorCode.ts is not part of this diff and my repo-wide search for these identifiers found only the usages, never a definition. WHY: If the ErrorCode enum/object was not extended, an enum declaration makes this a TypeScript compile error (TS2339) breaking the build, and a plain-object declaration makes these evaluate to undefined — `throw new Error(undefined)` and `res.json({ error: undefined })` degrade the new backup-code error handling so clients fall through to the generic 'something went wrong' branch and the res.error comparisons in login.tsx:176-177 never match. HOW: Verify packages/features/auth/lib/ErrorCode.ts defines both members (e.g. IncorrectBackupCode = 'incorrect-backup-code', MissingBackupCodes = 'missing-backup-codes'); add them if absent. Note: the search index available to me was demonstrably partial (even SecondFactorRequired's definition could not be located), so this needs verification rather than being asserted as missing.

backupCode is passed as a new third argument to TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable, but the helper is unchanged in this diff — if it doesn't forward the parameter, the disable-with-backup-code flow is dead. — WHAT: handleDisable now passes backupCode as a third argument to TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable(password, totpCode, backupCode), but the TwoFactorAuthAPI helper is not part of this diff and its definition could not be located to confirm it accepts and forwards the new parameter (the pre-PR call was disable(password, totpCode)). WHY: If the helper still builds its POST body only from (password, code), the backup code is silently dropped, req.body.backupCode is undefined in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts, and the new 'lost access' disable flow always fails with SecondFactorRequired — users who lost their authenticator cannot disable 2FA. HOW: Verify apps/web/components/settings/TwoFactorAuthAPI.ts (disable method) includes backupCode in the request body sent to /api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable; add it if absent. Note: the search index available to me was demonstrably partial (the helper file could not be located at all), so this needs verification rather than being asserted as broken.

It notes that backupCodes[index]=null prevents reuse because a string input can never match null, but states the race concern is already covered by an existing finding rather than dismissed.

Existing finding (referenced, not restated): an ErrorCode-definition concern for the MissingBackupCodes error thrown in next-auth-options.ts. — The analysis references an existing finding (explicitly 'not restated'): an ErrorCode-definition concern related to the MissingBackupCodes error that next-auth-options.ts throws when the user has no backup codes.

Existing finding: in EnableTwoFactorModal, the onEnable callback only fires from the modal's close path. — The analysis references an existing finding: the 'onEnable-only-fires-from-close' defect in EnableTwoFactorModal, i.e., the onEnable callback is only invoked from the modal's close path.

Existing finding (already reported): the backup-code update is non-atomic. — The analysis references an 'already-reported non-atomic update' as an existing finding; the performance-lens pass found no new loops/queries beyond it. The update described in the surrounding context is the backup-code consumption write (backupCodes[index]=null followed by persisting the user).

goldensDetail.text: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

findings.description: Org/team authorization SQL is returned with a top-level OR and no enclosing parentheses, so composing it with additional ANDed filters breaks precedence and widens the authorization condition. — WHAT: getBaseConditions (and getAuthorizationConditions) can return a raw SQL fragment containing a top-level OR — e.g. `("teamId" = ANY(...)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true) OR ("userId" = ANY(...)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = false)` produced by the reducers at lines 171-174/204-207 and returned unwrapped at lines 74-77 when filterConditions is null. WHY: the previous WhereInput return type was structurally safe to compose, but a raw fragment with a top-level OR silently breaks precedence for any consumer that embeds it as `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND <extra filters>` — AND binds tighter than OR, turning `(authA) OR (authB) AND extra` into `authA OR (authB AND extra)`, which widens the authorization clause and returns bookings outside the intended filters. HOW: always wrap the composed result in parentheses, e.g. make the reducers return `Prisma.sql`(${joined})`` or have getBaseConditions/getAuthorizationConditions return `Prisma.sql`(${authConditions})`` so the fragment is safe to embed.

The filter-only branch in getBaseConditions is dead code because authorization conditions are never null, masking the assumption that denial could be a falsy value. — WHAT: the `else if (filterConditions)` branch in getBaseConditions is unreachable — getAuthorizationConditions() is typed `Promise<Prisma.Sql>` and every code path (including deny and invalid-options paths) returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, so `authConditions` is always truthy. WHY: dead code indicates a logic mistake (the author appears to have assumed auth conditions could be null as in the old API where the array was filtered for null); behavior is currently correct only because denial is expressed as the truthy `1=0` fragment, and future refactors that return null for deny would silently drop the authorization constraint via this branch. HOW: remove the dead branch or restructure so the deny case is explicit, e.g. combine only non-null filter conditions with the always-present auth condition.

getBaseConditions returns an unparenthesized top-level OR fragment, which will compose incorrectly (and break authorization scoping) if any caller appends an AND condition. — getBaseConditions returns an unparenthesized top-level OR fragment (lines 118-119, produced by the reduces at 215-218 and 248-251). If any caller ever appends an AND condition to this fragment, operator precedence will break the intended authorization scoping, so the OR fragment should be wrapped in parentheses. Currently latent: the only existing usage (integration test line 483) appends nothing, so no live bug today, but it is a composability/authorization-scoping hazard.

The else-if/else null-handling branches in getBaseConditions are unreachable because getAuthorizationConditions() never returns null. — The else-if/else branches in getBaseConditions are unreachable dead code because getAuthorizationConditions() never returns null, so the null-handling paths can never execute. Remove the dead branches (or change getAuthorizationConditions so null is actually possible) to avoid misleading future maintainers.

findings.description: Dataclass field `queued` uses import-time `timezone.now()` default instead of `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`, giving every instance a stale timestamp. — WHAT: the `queued` field default `timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the dataclass is defined (at module import), not each time an AssignmentSource is created. WHY: every AssignmentSource produced by from_integration() silently carries the process-import timestamp instead of the time the assignment was actually queued, so any consumer of `queued` (logging, latency measurement, or future cycle-detection logic) reads a permanently stale value. HOW: use a default_factory so the timestamp is computed per instance.

findings.description: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an uninstantiable abstract class wired as MetricAlertFire's detector_handler, crashing any detector of that type at runtime. — WHAT: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but implements none of its abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data), so the class cannot be instantiated. WHY: StatefulDetectorHandler enforces these via abc.ABC, and MetricAlertFire.detector_handler = MetricAlertDetectorHandler means Detector.detector_handler (which calls group_type.detector_handler(self)) will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...` for any detector of type metric_alert_fire processed by process_detectors — previously the handler was instantiable and evaluate() returned []. HOW: either implement the four abstract methods on MetricAlertDetectorHandler (even as stubs returning empty values, e.g. counter_names = [], get_dedupe_value/get_group_key_values returning trivial values, build_occurrence_and_event_data raising NotImplementedError), or keep it subclassing DetectorHandler until the stateful implementation lands.

This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.
Docstring says this returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. Consider updating the docstring to match the new return type.

findings.description: Duplicate downsize definition overrides the 4-positional-arg version, breaking Jobs::ResizeEmoji which still calls it with 5 arguments. — WHAT: The diff adds a second `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` definition while leaving the original `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` in place, so Ruby discards the 5-argument version. WHY: `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` (app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14) still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 arguments, which now raises `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (given 5, expected 3..4)` — every emoji resize job crashes. HOW: Delete the dead 4-arg downsize definition and update resize_emoji.rb to the new contract: `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, "100x100", opts)`.

Animated-GIF detection keys off the tempfile path extension, which browser multipart tempfiles lack, so auto-downsized animated GIFs are silently flattened to a static first frame. — WHAT: `OptimizedImage.downsize` is called with `tempfile.path`, but the animated-GIF branch in `optimize` only triggers when the `from` path matches /\.GIF$/i — and for normal browser uploads `file.tempfile` is a Rack multipart tempfile with no file extension (e.g. /tmp/RackMultipart123). WHY: animated GIFs larger than max_image_size_kb that are uploaded through the composer go through `convert #{from}[0]`, which keeps only the first frame — animation is silently destroyed even though the site has allow_animated_thumbnails enabled and the code explicitly passes allow_animation. Only API URL downloads work, because FileHelper.download appends the original extension to its tempfile. HOW: give the tempfile a path carrying the original extension before downsizing so the GIF detection in optimize can match.

Hardcoded 10MB client-side limit drops per-type site settings, breaking attachment validation and sites with image limits above 10MB. — WHAT: The client-side size check now hardcodes `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` for every upload, replacing the per-type `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` lookup (and the 413 handler at line 246 hardcodes 10MB in the error message too). WHY: attachments are no longer validated against max_attachment_size_kb client-side — users can select oversized attachments that only fail after a full server round-trip — and sites configured with max_image_size_kb above 10MB now have legitimate image uploads blocked by the browser even though the server would accept them; the 413 message also reports a wrong limit whenever the configured limit differs from 10MB. HOW: keep the 10MB ceiling for images (matching the new server-side downsize budget) but retain the site setting for attachments.

missedGoldens.text: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsi

goldensDetail.text: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.

findings.description: update/destroy crash with NoMethodError (500) instead of 404 when the embeddable host id does not exist. — WHAT: update and destroy look up the host with EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and then call host.destroy / save_host(host) without a nil check. WHY: for an unknown or stale id (double-delete, outdated admin list, direct API call) host is nil, so nil.destroy at line 16 and nil.host= inside save_host at line 23 raise NoMethodError, returning a 500 instead of a 404. HOW: raise Discourse::NotFound when the record is missing before touching it.

before_validation crashes with NoMethodError on nil host instead of producing a validation error. — WHAT: the before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! twice without guarding against a nil host. WHY: when create/update is submitted without params[:embeddable_host][:host] (or any code saves an EmbeddableHost with host unset), nil.sub! raises NoMethodError and the request 500s instead of surfacing the format validation error. HOW: coerce/guard before normalizing, e.g. assign via self.host = host.to_s.sub(...).sub(...) so nil becomes an empty string that fails validation cleanly.

Hosts saved with a port pass validation but can never match in record_for_host because uri.host strips the port. — WHAT: the validation regex (line 2) explicitly allows a port (:[0-9]{1,5})? in the stored host, but record_for_host looks up records using only uri.host, which never includes the port. WHY: an admin can successfully save 'example.com:3000', yet EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? will never match referers from that origin, so embedding from any host on a non-default port is silently rejected and TopicEmbed.import (topic_embed.rb:36) never finds its category. HOW: include the port in the lookup key when present, e.g. build the candidate as uri.host plus ":#{uri.port}" for non-default ports and match either form, or strip the port at save time and reject storing one.

EmbeddingController#update silently ignores all input and changes nothing while returning success. — WHAT: the update action is identical to show — it renders the freshly built @embedding OpenStruct and never reads or persists any params. WHY: any client (admin UI or API consumer) that PUTs embedding changes receives a successful response while nothing is saved, a silent contract break for an endpoint named update. HOW: remove the update action until there is something to persist, or have it apply the submitted attributes before rendering.

Host validation regex rejects valid domains with TLDs longer than 5 chars or punycode double-hyphen labels — WHAT: the host validation regex restricts the TLD to 2-5 lowercase letters ([a-z]{2,5}) and permits only a single hyphen or dot between labels ([\-\.]{1}). WHY: valid hostnames with TLDs longer than 5 characters (e.g. example.technology, example.museum, example.international) and punycode/IDN labels containing double hyphens (e.g. xn--nxasmq6b.example) fail validation, so admins cannot register those sites as embeddable hosts and embedding is silently broken for them. HOW: relax the regex, e.g. widen the TLD group to [a-z]{2,} (or [a-z]{2,63}) and allow multiple hyphens per label, e.g. /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.][a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i.

goldensDetail.text: NoMethodError before_validation in EmbeddableHost

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

findings.description: New per-site fallback chain (SiteSetting.default_locale) is not part of the translate accelerator's process-global LRU cache key, so fallback translations leak across multisite sites with different default locales and go stale on locale changes. — WHAT: The new fallback chain makes I18n.t results depend on SiteSetting.default_locale (per-site in multisite), but lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72 caches zero-arg translations in a process-global LRU keyed only by "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}" — the fallback chain/site is not part of the key. WHY: In a multisite cluster where two sites have different default_locale, a key missing in the requested locale resolves through different fallback chains per site, but whichever result is cached first is served to the other site until the 300-entry LRU evicts it — users see text in the wrong fallback language, nondeterministically; the same stale cache serves the old fallback language after an admin changes default_locale at runtime. HOW: Include the fallback chain (or SiteSetting.default_locale) in the cache key in translate_accelerator.rb, e.g. k = "#{key}#{config.locale}#{SiteSetting.default_locale}#{config.backend.object_id}", or bypass the cache for lookups that miss in the primary locale.
