Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the

goldensDetail.text: Thread-safety issue with lazy @loaded_locales

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

findings.description: getSubGroupsCount() now silently returns null on concurrent deletion, propagating a nullable result to GroupRepresentation and any unboxing caller without an audited contract. — WHAT: getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when the delegate lookup returns null (concurrent group deletion), changing the method's contract from non-null count to nullable without any audit of the callers. WHY: the only caller visible in this checkout (GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount) passes the value to representation.setSubGroupCount(...) so null propagates silently into GroupRepresentation.subGroupCount and out through the admin REST API, and any other consumer of GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() that unboxes the Long (assignment to long, comparison such as count > 0, arithmetic) will throw the very NPE this PR is meant to eliminate; note that every other 'group not found' path in this same class (getDelegateForUpdate, isUpdated) throws IllegalStateException("Not found in database") rather than returning null, so this is also an inconsistent failure mode. HOW: either mark GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() as nullable in the interface and verify every caller tolerates null (no unboxing), or throw the same IllegalStateException used elsewhere in this class so the failure is explicit instead of a silent null count.

GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount can now return null after switching to modelSupplier.get() with a null check for concurrent deletion. — Null-return contract change in GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount: the lookup switched from getGroupModel() to modelSupplier.get() with an added null check, so the method can now return null when the group is concurrently deleted (the underlying delegate lookup cacheSession.getGroupDelegate().getGroupById(realm, cached.getId()) returns null on concurrent deletion). The reviewer verified this introduces no stale-null memoization (LazyModel only caches non-null results), no downstream NPE (the only production caller, GroupUtils.toRepresentation, passes the value to GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount(Long) which accepts boxed Long), but the method's return contract is now nullable.

missedGoldens.text: The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

goldensDetail.text: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.
The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

missedGoldens.text: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cach

In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) rega

goldensDetail.text: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

findings.description: Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition creates slug-less orgs when billing is off and grants slugs before payment when billing is on. — WHAT: The condition for setting the organization's `slug` was inverted from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`, while the `requestedSlug` metadata condition was left unchanged. WHY: When team billing is disabled (self-hosted/OSS installs), organizations are now created with a null slug, breaking the org subdomain/URL; when billing is enabled, the slug is granted immediately at creation (bypassing the payment-gated flow where the slug should only live in metadata.requestedSlug until subscription, mirroring teams/create.handler.ts) and both slug and requestedSlug are set redundantly. This change is also unrelated to the PR's destinationCalendar purpose, suggesting an accidental edit. HOW: Restore the negated condition on the slug line: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`.

Empty-array destinationCalendar reaches EventManager.create's unguarded `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` and crashes confirmation of Google Meet bookings with no destination calendar. — WHAT: When neither the booking nor the confirming user has a destination calendar, the evt now carries `destinationCalendar: []`, which flows through handleConfirmation into EventManager.create where `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` is followed by an unguarded `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` check (packages/core/EventManager.ts, the line right after the new @NOTE destructure). WHY: For a booking whose location is Google Meet with no destination calendar set, the destructured `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined and accessing `.integration` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`, crashing the booking confirmation. HOW: Guard the access in EventManager.create (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`), or omit the empty array here so consumers keep receiving null/undefined.

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also app

goldensDetail.text: Potential null reference if mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined if evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

findings.description: add_members/remove_member require params[:group_id] but the member route and JS client only provide params[:id], so both endpoints always raise ParameterMissing — WHAT: `add_members` (and identically `remove_member` at line 85) reads the group id via `params.require(:group_id)`, but the new routes (`delete "members"` / `put "members"` declared directly inside `resources :groups` in config/routes.rb:78-79) are member routes, so the group id arrives as `params[:id]`, and the JS client (discourse/models/group.js addMembers/removeMember) only sends `usernames`/`user_id` in the request body — `group_id` is never present. WHY: `params.require(:group_id)` raises ActionController::ParameterMissing on every request, so adding and removing group members from the admin UI always fails. HOW: use the member-route param: `group = Group.find(params[:id].to_i)` (or change the routes/JS to actually supply group_id).

group.users.delete is given an integer id instead of a User record, raising ActiveRecord::AssociationTypeMismatch — WHAT: `remove_member` passes an integer (`user_id = params.require(:user_id).to_i`) to `group.users.delete(user_id)` on the `has_many :users, through: :group_users` association. WHY: ActiveRecord's collection delete runs `raise_on_type_mismatch` on each argument and raises ActiveRecord::AssociationTypeMismatch (User expected, got Fixnum), so removing a member 500s even once the group_id param issue is fixed. HOW: look up the record and delete the instance, e.g. `group.users.delete(User.find(user_id))` or reuse the existing `group.remove(user)` helper from app/models/group.rb.

totalPages uses floor+1 instead of ceil, producing a phantom empty last page whenever user_count is a multiple of limit — WHAT: `totalPages` computes `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which overcounts by one whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 users / limit 50 yields 3 pages instead of 2). WHY: on the real last page `showingLast` (currentPage == totalPages) stays false, so the next action runs and sets `offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)` = user_count, the server returns an empty member list, and the UI lands on a phantom empty page ("3/3"). HOW: use `Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit"))` (the user_count == 0 guard above already handles the empty case).

members list is rendered but findMembers() is never called on initial page load, so the admin group page shows no members until paging — WHAT: the template iterates `members` (`{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`), but a repo-wide grep for findMembers shows it is only invoked from the next/previous actions and after add/remove — nothing calls `model.findMembers()` when the admin group page is first rendered. WHY: the member list is empty on initial page load for an existing group (and the pager shows 0/0) until the admin clicks next/previous or adds/removes a member. HOW: call `findMembers()` when the route sets up the controller/model for an existing group (e.g. in the admin group route's setupController/afterModel).

Admin group template references itemView="group-member" but no GroupMemberView exists, crashing member list rendering and leaving the removeMember action untriggerable. — WHAT: The template renders group members with `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, but no `GroupMemberView` (or `view:group-member` registration) exists anywhere in app/assets/javascripts — a repo-wide grep for `group-member|GroupMemberView` returns only this template line. WHY: Ember 1.x resolves the itemView string through the container when the {{each}} block instantiates item views; with no matching class it raises an assertion in debug builds and a createChildView(undefined) TypeError in production, so the admin group page render blows up as soon as `members` becomes non-empty (reachable today: `addMembers` succeeds server-side, then group.js calls `findMembers()` which populates `members` and forces the {{each}} to re-render). Additionally, the per-member UI that would trigger the controller's `removeMember` action has no view to live in, so members can never be removed from this page. HOW: add the missing view, e.g. `Discourse.GroupMemberView = Ember.View.extend({ templateName: 'admin/templates/group-member' })` with a remove button that calls `get('controller').send('removeMember', this.get('context'))`, or drop `itemView="group-member"` and render the remove control inline in the {{each}} block.

HTTP method mismatch in .remove_member - test uses PUT but remove_member action expects DELETE

goldensDetail.text: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.

findings.description: New hidden authn_use_chk inputs in passkeys.ftl have no JS consumer in the repo, making the block dead markup (or a missing JS counterpart) for the re-auth passkey flow. — WHAT: The new hidden 'authn_use_chk' inputs (credential IDs) rendered in the authn_select form have no consumer anywhere in the codebase — a repo-wide grep for 'authn_use_chk' returns only this template, and neither passkeysConditionalAuth.js nor webauthnAuthenticate.js (referenced below) reads them. WHY: If the accompanying JS that collects these credential IDs into the WebAuthn allowCredentials list is missing, the block is dead markup and the re-authentication passkey flow this PR intends to fix will still not restrict the assertion to the already-identified user's credentials; it also needlessly embeds the user's WebAuthn credential IDs in the page HTML. HOW: Verify passkeysConditionalAuth.js reads input[name="authn_use_chk"] to build allowCredentials when isUserIdentified is true; if no such consumer exists, either add it or remove this block.

PasswordForm.configuredFor now declares passkey-only (passwordless) users as configured for a required password step, which can strand them on an unsatisfiable password page if the template lacks the passkey UI. — WHAT: configuredFor now returns true for a user who has a passkey but NO password credential, and authenticate() renders the standard password page (createLoginPassword) after merely filling WebAuthn context data. WHY: For a REQUIRED PasswordForm execution, such users previously had configuredFor=false (routing to an alternative or required-action setup); now they land on a password field they cannot satisfy, and they can only proceed if the login-password template actually renders the passkey conditional-UI macro — if it does not, the user is hard-stuck in the flow. HOW: Ensure the login-password template includes the passkeys.ftl conditionalUIData macro (gated on enableWebAuthnConditionalUI), or only advertise configuredFor=true for passkey-only users when the password page can actually offer the passkey option.

Passkey conditional UI is now offered during re-authentication with no visible guard that the submitted passkey belongs to the already-identified user. — WHAT: fillContextForm is now invoked while context.getUser() is already set (re-authentication), and UsernamePasswordForm.action routes any passkey submission to webauthnAuth.action without any visible check that the asserted passkey belongs to the already-identified user. WHY: In a step-up/re-authentication flow, if WebAuthnPasswordlessAuthenticator.action simply re-derives the user from the credential (its implementation is outside this change and could not be verified here), a passkey belonging to a different account would complete the re-authentication as that other identity, breaking identity continuity of the flow. HOW: In the passkey action path, when context.getUser() != null (re-auth), reject the assertion unless the credential's owning user equals context.getUser().

missedGoldens.text: ConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called without UserModel parameter

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is sti

goldensDetail.text: ConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called without UserModel parameter

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

findings.description: Direct subscript of integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] raises KeyError for integrations whose metadata lacks a recorded sender, crashing the reinstall path with a 500. — WHAT: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` is subscripted directly even though `build_integration` (lines 376-377) only sets `metadata["sender"]` conditionally (`if state.get("sender")`), and no code in src/sentry ever binds a `sender` pipeline state. WHY: on the reinstall path (Integration row exists without OrganizationIntegration — e.g., reinstall after uninstall leaves the Integration row behind), any integration whose metadata lacks "sender" (all integrations created before sender recording, or created via flows that never pass sender) raises KeyError, producing a 500 instead of the intended github-integration-failed.html page — the new security check crashes open rather than failing closed. HOW: use safe access and treat a missing/unknown sender as a verification failure, e.g. `sender_login = integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` followed by `if not sender_login or pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != sender_login: return error(...)`.

Fresh-install path skips the authenticated-user-vs-installer check, letting an attacker claim an unrecorded GitHub App installation_id while authenticated as a different GitHub user. — WHAT: the fresh-install branch (`except Integration.DoesNotExist: return pipeline.next_step()`) completes the pipeline without ever comparing the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user (`github_authenticated_user`, bound in OAuthLoginView) to the person who installed the GitHub App, while OAuthLoginView.bind_state("installation_id", ...) accepts an arbitrary installation_id from the query string (lines 397-399) before any state validation. WHY: the PR's stated guarantee — fail when the authenticated GitHub user differs from the app installer — is unenforced for installations not yet recorded in Sentry's DB, so anyone who obtains an unclaimed sentry-io app installation_id (abandoned direct-from-GitHub installs are never recorded; installation IDs are enumerable) can run the pipeline in their own session, authenticate as themselves, and attach the victim GitHub org's installation (with its repo access) to their own Sentry organization. HOW: on the DoesNotExist path, verify with the OAuth access token that the authenticated user can actually access the claimed installation (e.g., GitHub's GET /user/installations) before calling pipeline.next_step(), or fetch the installation via the GitHub App API and compare its account/events sender to github_authenticated_user.

Token exchange and GitHub /user fetch are unguarded, so network or API failures produce a 500 instead of the friendly installation-failed page. — WHAT: the OAuth token exchange (`safe_urlopen`, line 423) and `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` (line 434) sit outside the try/except that only wraps `safe_urlread`/payload parsing, so network failures to github.com or a non-200 from api.github.com/user raise instead of rendering the error page. WHY: transient GitHub unavailability, timeouts, or an expired/invalid access token turn a recoverable installation failure into an unhandled 500 during the setup pipeline, contradicting the PR's goal of gracefully failing the installation on verification problems. HOW: wrap the token exchange and get_user_info calls in the same (or a broader) try/except and fall through to `return error(request, self.active_organization)` on failure.

pipeline.signature has no definition anywhere in src/sentry (only these two new usages exist), so the OAuth step either crashes with AttributeError or, if defined elsewhere as a provider-static hash, the state check binds nothing per-session. — WHAT: `pipeline.signature` is read at lines 402 and 412, but a bare-word search across all of src/sentry finds no definition of `signature` anywhere — no property, class attribute, or annotation on Pipeline or elsewhere; the only occurrences in the entire tree are these two new usages. WHY: if the attribute does not exist, the first dispatch of OAuthLoginView raises AttributeError and the GitHub installation flow 500s immediately, before any redirect to GitHub; and even if it is defined outside the indexed tree with the usual upstream semantics (md5 of the provider key), the value is a static per-provider constant, so the `state` check at line 412 validates nothing per-session and provides no CSRF/session binding for the OAuth callback. HOW: verify that Pipeline actually defines `signature`; if not, add a per-session nonce (e.g., generate a random token, store it via pipeline.bind_state, and compare against it on callback) instead of relying on a missing or provider-static value.

goldensDetail.text: Null reference if github_authenticated_user state is missing
OAuth state uses pipeline.signature (static) instead of a per-request random value

The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation

findings.description: Call to non-existent AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken breaks compilation of the new encoder provider. — WHAT: Line 54 calls AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), but a repo-wide search for 'ShouldUseLightweightToken' matches only this call site — the method does not exist in AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper or anywhere else. WHY: The module fails to compile, so no access token can be issued; if the method is added by a companion change it must be merged together, otherwise initToken (TokenManager.java:1053) is dead code. HOW: Add a static getShouldUseLightweightToken(KeycloakSession) helper to AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper (or call the existing lightweight-token check used elsewhere) before relying on it here.

New factory implements a missing interface and calls missing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut(), breaking compilation and provider wiring. — WHAT: This factory references two symbols that do not exist in the codebase: (a) TokenContextEncoderProviderFactory in the implements clause (line 36) — no such interface file exists (TokenContextEncoderProvider.java declares only the provider interface), and (b) OAuth2GrantTypeFactory (import line 31, used at lines 72, 110, 126-128) including calls to getShortcut(), which is declared nowhere in the org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants package. WHY: The code does not compile, and because the SPI factory interface/registration is missing, TokenManager.initToken's session.getProvider(TokenContextEncoderProvider.class) (TokenManager.java:1052) would return null and NPE on every access-token issuance even if compilation were fixed. HOW: Add the TokenContextEncoderProviderFactory interface (extending ProviderFactory<TokenContextEncoderProvider>) plus its provider-factory registration, and add getShortcut() to the grant-type factory SPI (or look the shortcut up from an existing source) as part of this PR.

Grant-type context is only wired for the refresh flow, so all initially issued tokens encode grantType as 'na'. — WHAT: Constants.GRANT_TYPE is set on the ClientSessionContext only in validateToken (refresh flow, line 248); a repo-wide search for setAttribute(.*GRANT_TYPE finds no other setter, so the grantType read by DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext (line 57) is null for every initial token issuance and is encoded as 'na'. WHY: Access tokens issued via authorization_code, client_credentials, password, device, token-exchange, etc. all carry grant-type 'na' — the PR's advertised grant-type context only ever works for tokens created by refresh, and the grantType field newly captured in OAuth2GrantType.Context (line 102) is never consumed. HOW: In the grant processing path (e.g., AbstractOIDCGrantType/TokenEndpoint where clientSessionCtx is built), propagate the grant type — for example clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType()) — before TokenManager.initToken runs.

Constructor null-checks grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId. — WHAT: The constructor checks Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") at line 73, duplicating the grantType check from line 72 and never validating rawTokenId. WHY: A null rawTokenId is silently accepted despite the guard's intent, producing '...:null'-style encoded ids or NPEs later in encodeTokenId string concatenation semantics, and the exception message is misleading when grantType is null. HOW: Change line 73 to Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed").

Refresh flow sets grantType="refresh_token", which has no registered OAuth2GrantType shortcut, so encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException and every refresh-token request fails. — WHAT: The refresh flow sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE to OAuth2Constants.REFRESH_TOKEN ("refresh_token") on the client session context, but no OAuth2GrantType provider with id "refresh_token" exists anywhere in the codebase (repo-wide grep shows zero OAuth2GrantType implementations/factories), so DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getShortcutByGrantType("refresh_token") always returns null and encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException("Cannot encode token with unknown grantType: refresh_token") at DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:111. WHY: Once the encoder provider is wired in, every refresh-token request reaches initToken → getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext → encodeTokenId and fails with a 500, completely breaking the refresh-token grant — the one flow this PR annotates with a real grant type (all other flows fall back to the registered "na" shortcut and encode fine). HOW: Either register a refresh_token OAuth2GrantType implementation with a 2-char shortcut so the factory maps resolve it, or make encodeTokenId fall back to the UNKNOWN ("na") shortcut instead of throwing when getShortcutByGrantType returns null, e.g. `String grantShort = factory.getShortcutByGrantType(tokenContext.getGrantType()); if (grantShort == null) { grantShort = UNKNOWN; }`.

findings.description: New ruler-less list view can never show Delete/Pause menu items and Silence is a no-op because AlertRuleMenu and the silence drawer still require the rulerRule that the list no longer fetches. — WHAT: The new ruler-less list view renders RuleActionsButtons/AlertRuleMenu without a rulerRule, but the downstream components still gate actions on the ruler rule: AlertRuleMenu renders Delete only when `canDelete && rulerRule` (AlertRuleMenu.tsx:165) and Pause only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (AlertRuleMenu.tsx:123), and RuleActionsButtons.V2 mounts SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` (RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:104) — all false when rulerRule is undefined. WHY: In the new alert list view the Delete and Pause menu items never appear (making the newly added grafanaDeleteAbility/grafanaPauseAbility dead code), and clicking 'Silence notifications' sets showSilenceDrawer=true but the drawer never mounts, so silencing from the list view silently does nothing — a functional regression versus the previous list which passed the ruler rule. HOW: Thread a pause/silence/delete capability that works from the GrafanaPromRuleDTO (e.g., relax the guards to also accept the grafana prom rule path: render Delete when canDelete using the identifier-based delete modal, and support SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer/MenuItemPauseRule from promRule), or keep these abilities disabled in the list until the UI supports them.

Refactored useAllAlertRuleAbilities loses the isFederatedRuleGroup check, making federated Mimir rule groups appear editable/removable. — WHAT: The refactored useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` — dropping the previous `const isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group);` check that made rules in federated (Mimir) rule groups immutable. WHY: For federated rule groups, Update/Delete/Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently abilities are now reported as supported whenever the ruler is available and the user is editable/removable, so the UI can offer edit/delete/pause on federated rules that must not be modified through this cluster (previously blocked via immutableRule). HOW: Restore the federated detection — e.g., compute `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` in useAllAlertRuleAbilities and pass it (or the CombinedRuleGroup) into useAllRulerRuleAbilities so immutableRule still includes federated groups.

skipToken path in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities still reports Duplicate as supported, which can wrongly enable Duplicate for cloud rules when their ruler is unavailable. — WHAT: When callers pass skipToken (rule is undefined — used by AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons.V2 for non-Grafana prom rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities still returns Duplicate as [AlwaysSupported, grafanaRulesPermissions.create] because `loading` from useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(undefined) is false, making MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported. WHY: In AlertRuleMenu the abilities are OR'ed (`canDuplicate = (ruler…) || (grafana…)`), so for a data-source (Mimir/Cortex) rule whose ruler is unavailable or still loading — where the ruler-based duplicate ability is NotSupported — the Duplicate menu item is now shown to any user with Grafana alert-rules create permission; previously it was hidden until the ruler was available. HOW: Short-circuit when the rule is undefined/skipToken so every action returns [NotSupported, false] (e.g., in useGrafanaPromRuleAbility/useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities return a disabled abilities object when `rule === skipToken`).

New prom-based abilities hook restricts ModifyExport to alerting rules, hiding the Export action for Grafana-managed recording rules in the ruler-less list view. — WHAT: The new useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gates AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport on prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule), which returns false for recording rules, while the old ruler-based code gated it on rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule) (true for any Grafana-managed rule, including recording rules — see the removed hunk '[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [isGrafanaManagedAlertRule, exportAllowed]'). WHY: In the new ruler-less list view (GrafanaRuleListItem passes only promRule, so rulerRule is undefined and the ruler fallback in AlertRuleMenu yields supported=false), Grafana-managed recording rules lose the Export menu action that was previously available — a silent feature regression, since exporting recording rules to provisioning format is supported. HOW: Use the any-grafana-rule guard for ModifyExport, e.g. '[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule), exportAllowed]' (keeping the alerting-only restriction only for Pause/Restore where it is semantically correct).

goldensDetail.text: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.

RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.

findings.description: Salesforce CalendarService uses prisma.credential.update without importing prisma, breaking the whole integration. — WHAT: `prisma.credential.update` is called at line 96 but `prisma` is never imported in this file (the imports at lines 1-20 contain no prisma import). WHY: every Salesforce calendar operation constructs this service, so getClient throws a ReferenceError ('prisma is not defined') — or fails TypeScript compilation — making the entire Salesforce integration unusable. HOW: add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";` to the imports.

Salesforce connection is built with the stale access token even though a fresh one was just refreshed and saved. — WHAT: after fetching fresh tokens (lines 75-99), the jsforce.Connection is constructed with the OLD `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`/`instance_url`. WHY: this code path runs because the stored access token is expired, so the connection is initialized with a token Salesforce will reject with 401; the freshly refreshed token that was just saved to the DB is never used for this session. HOW: use the parsed fresh values when building the connection, e.g. `instanceUrl: accessTokenParsed.data.instance_url, accessToken: accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

Webhook filters/ creates credentials by appMetadata.slug which is undefined, so Prisma ignores the appId filter and overwrites an arbitrary credential of the user. — WHAT: the credential lookup/create uses `appMetadata.slug`, but app-store metadata objects have no `slug` property (verified: no `slug:` in appStoreMetaData.ts or any app `_metadata.ts`), so `appId` is `undefined`. WHY: Prisma silently drops `undefined` fields from `where`, so `findFirst({ where: { userId, appId: undefined } })` matches the user's FIRST credential of ANY app and `update` overwrites that credential's key with the synced keys — syncing one app corrupts another app's stored credentials; the create path likewise writes a credential with a missing appId. HOW: use the key that was used for the lookup, e.g. `appId: app.slug` (the App table slug that indexed appStoreMetadata), instead of `appMetadata.slug`.

Office365 passes a hyphenated appSlug that will not match the App table slug, breaking the credential-sync callback. — WHAT: `refreshOAuthTokens` is called with appSlug "office365-calendar", but the app-store metadata key / App table slug for this integration is "office365calendar" (no hyphen — matching how zoomvideo passes "zoomvideo" and webex passes "webex"). WHY: the credential-sync endpoint echoes this appSlug back to the new /api/webhook/app-credential handler, which does `prisma.app.findUnique({ where: { slug: reqBody.appSlug } })` — "office365-calendar" matches no App row, so the sync callback 404s and Office 365 token sync never persists. HOW: pass "office365calendar" as the appSlug.

Webex wraps refresh in refreshOAuthTokens but still parses with the full Webex token schema, so sync-mode responses always fail validation. — WHAT: the refresh fetch is now wrapped in `refreshOAuthTokens`, whose sync-mode branch returns the sync endpoint's response containing only an access token and expiry (per its own doc comment), but the response is still parsed with the strict `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` (requires `scope` literal, `token_type` literal, `refresh_token`, `refresh_token_expires_in`). WHY: when credential sharing is enabled, the parse always fails and refreshAccessToken rejects with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned", so Webex meeting creation breaks for synced credentials. HOW: route the response through `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseBody, webexRefreshedTokenSchema)` like zoom/office365 do, or skip the strict schema when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is active.

In sync mode the Zoom refresh writes expiry_date = NaN because the stripped parse result has no expires_in, permanently breaking Zoom token parsing afterwards. — WHAT: switching to `parseRefreshTokenResponse` means that in credential-sync mode the parsed data only contains `access_token` (plus an injected placeholder `refresh_token`); `expires_in` is stripped, so the unchanged line below computes `key.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)` = NaN and stores it. WHY: on the next getToken call, `zoomTokenSchema.parse(credential.key)` rejects NaN for `expiry_date: z.number()`, so every Zoom operation fails with "Zoom credential keys parsing error" once a synced refresh has occurred. HOW: when expires_in is absent, use the expiry returned by the sync endpoint or leave the previous expiry_date unchanged instead of writing NaN.

Webhook throws unhandled ZodError/decrypt exceptions on bad input instead of returning a 400. — WHAT: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` (line 31) and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` (lines 57-59) throw on malformed input with no try/catch. WHY: any request that passes the secret check but has an invalid body shape, undecryptable payload, or non-JSON decrypted content produces an unhandled 500 (and in some Next.js setups an HTML error page) instead of a clean 4xx, which also breaks the calling sync service's error handling. HOW: use `safeParse` and return 400 on failure, and wrap the decrypt/JSON.parse in a try/catch returning 400.

Salesforce refresh relies on response.statusText === "OK" which is not guaranteed (empty under HTTP/2). — WHAT: token refresh success is detected via `response.statusText !== "OK"` instead of checking `response.ok`/status code. WHY: `statusText` is an empty string on HTTP/2 responses (Node fetch/undici), so a successful Salesforce token response can be misclassified as an error and throw HttpError 400; conversely it couples correctness to an optional protocol detail. HOW: use `if (!response.ok) throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: response.statusText || String(response.status) });`.

Webhook findFirst→create is a TOCTOU race with no unique constraint on Credential(userId, appId), allowing duplicate credentials whose stale copies are never updated again. — WHAT: the findFirst-then-create sequence is a check-then-act race — the Credential model (schema.prisma:253-272) has no unique constraint on (userId, appId), only plain indexes, so two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app both find no row and both insert a credential. WHY: duplicate Credential rows are created for the same user/app, and because this handler (and Cal.com generally) reads credentials via findFirst, only one row is ever updated/read afterwards — the duplicate keeps stale keys indefinitely with no way to reconcile. HOW: perform the lookup-and-write inside a serializable transaction (prisma.$transaction with isolationLevel: 'Serializable') and retry on serialization failure, or add a @@unique([userId, appId]) constraint (after dedup) and switch to upsert on that compound key.

Credential update path does not clear the invalid flag, so syncing fresh keys never revives a credential previously marked invalid after a failed refresh. — WHAT: the update branch only writes `key` and never resets the credential's `invalid` flag, even though Cal.com sets credential.invalid = true when a token refresh fails (zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:368, webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:305, googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:115). WHY: a user whose credential was marked invalid receives fresh, working keys from the parent app store, but the credential stays flagged invalid, so Cal.com continues treating the integration as broken — the sync silently fails to restore it, defeating the purpose of the endpoint for exactly the credentials that most need re-syncing. HOW: add invalid: false to the update data so a successful key sync revives the credential.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

findings.description: align-items mixin is missing -moz-box-align, so the Gecko box fallback provided by flexbox() never receives cross-axis alignment. — WHAT: The align-items mixin omits the -moz-box-align declaration while its sibling mixins flexbox() and order() both include old-Gecko fallbacks (display: -moz-box, -moz-box-ordinal-group). WHY: On browsers that receive the -moz-box display fallback (old Firefox), flex items are never cross-axis aligned — the header contents, small-action rows, and bullet badges this PR converts will not be vertically centered/baselined there, contradicting the PR's stated 'all prefixes' goal. HOW: Add the Gecko box-align line to the mixin.

Button inside the newly-flexed .small-action keeps float:right, which flex items ignore, so it loses its right-edge alignment. — WHAT: .small-action is converted to a flex container (@include flexbox()) but its child 'button { float: right; }' rule (lines 555-559) was not migrated — floats have no effect on flex items, and unlike .panel in header.scss the button was not given 'margin-left: auto'. WHY: Any button rendered directly inside .small-action (the rule's existence implies one exists) will stop being right-aligned and will instead sit immediately after .small-action-desc, a layout regression for small-action posts. HOW: Mirror the pattern this PR already used for .panel by adding margin-left: auto to the button rule.

Removing the float fallbacks for .title/.panel leaves the header unlaid-out (panel stacked below title) in browsers with no flexbox support. — WHAT: The float fallbacks (.title { float: left; } and .panel { float: right; }) were removed and replaced with flex-only positioning (margin-left: auto on .panel, order on .panel/.extra-info-wrapper), which only takes effect when one of the five flex display values from flexbox() is supported. WHY: On any browser with no flexbox support at all (e.g., IE9, which the -ms-flexbox prefix does not cover), .title and .panel become plain block elements — the panel/login buttons drop below the logo at full width, breaking the header layout; keeping the floats would have been a zero-cost fallback since floats are ignored on flex items. HOW: Retain 'float: left' on .title and 'float: right' on .panel alongside the new flex rules.

missedGoldens.text: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

goldensDetail.text: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

findings.description: LoggerMiddleware now depends on the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware being wired ahead of it (no wiring change is present in this diff) and permanently drops the traceID field from the plugin request log. — WHAT: logRequest now sources pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname exclusively from m.logger.FromContext(ctx), which only works if the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware runs before LoggerMiddleware in the client middleware chain, and the explicit traceID extraction (tracing.TraceIDFromContext) was deleted with no replacement in instrumentContext. WHY: the diff registers NewContextualLoggerMiddleware nowhere (grep finds zero call sites for it and for NewMetricsMiddleware), so if the chain assembly is not updated in tandem — and ordered with ContextualLoggerMiddleware above LoggerMiddleware — the 'Plugin Request Completed' egress log silently loses pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID and uname, and traceID is lost unconditionally even with correct wiring since neither the logger middleware nor instrumentContext adds it anymore. HOW: in the middleware chain assembly (pluginsintegration wiring), replace NewInstrumentationMiddleware with NewMetricsMiddleware AND insert NewContextualLoggerMiddleware at the top of the stack, ahead of NewLoggerMiddleware; additionally either have instrumentContext append the traceID (tracing.TraceIDFromContext) or keep the explicit traceID logParam in logRequest.

Adding FromContext to the plog.Logger interface is a breaking change for any other implementers (fakes/test doubles) that were not updated in this diff. — WHAT: the Logger interface gained a new required method FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger, but only grafanaInfraLogWrapper (pkg/plugins/log/logger.go) implements it in the visible code. WHY: any other type that implements plog.Logger (fakes/test doubles used by plugin manager tests or alternative loggers) no longer satisfies the interface and fails compilation with 'missing method FromContext' — I searched the repo for other implementations and could not confirm none exist outside this snapshot. HOW: add FromContext to every existing Logger implementation (a safe default is `func (f *Fake) FromContext(context.Context) Logger { return f }`), or verify via a full build that grafanaInfraLogWrapper is the only implementer.

missedGoldens.text: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the

goldensDetail.text: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

findings.description: Required destination/attempts fields reject all Working Draft-format browser reports with 422, contradicting the stated 'support both specs' intent. — WHAT: `destination` and `attempts` are declared as required serializer fields, but the W3C Working Draft report format (https://www.w3.org/TR/reporting-1/, cited in the comment directly above) defines only type/url/user_agent/body/age — `destination` and `attempts` are Editor's Draft additions, and only `age`/`timestamp` were made optional. WHY: browsers sending Working-Draft-style reports (with `age`, without `destination`/`attempts`) fail validation and get HTTP 422, so this experimental data-collection endpoint drops exactly the real-world reports it exists to gather. HOW: make the non-overlapping fields optional, e.g. `destination = serializers.CharField(required=False)` and `attempts = serializers.IntegerField(required=False, min_value=1)`, matching the age/timestamp handling.

Field-level age/timestamp validators never run when the field is absent, so reports with neither age nor timestamp validate successfully despite both specs requiring one. — WHAT: `validate_age` and `validate_timestamp` are field-level validators that only run when their respective field is present in the input, so a report containing neither `age` nor `timestamp` passes validation — the docstring contract 'Validate that age is present' can never be enforced by a validator that is skipped when age is absent. WHY: both cited specs require exactly one of `age` (Working Draft) or `timestamp` (Editor's Draft), so structurally incomplete reports are accepted and counted as valid browser reports. HOW: replace the two field validators with an object-level `validate(self, attrs)` that raises ValidationError unless exactly one of age/timestamp is present.

A single invalid report aborts the whole batch with 422 before any valid reports are processed, dropping all valid telemetry in the batch. — WHAT: on the first invalid report in a batch the endpoint returns 422 immediately, before the metrics loop over `validated_reports` runs, so every valid report in the same batch is dropped without being recorded. WHY: browsers send reports as batched arrays, and one malformed or unknown-typed report (e.g., a report type not yet in BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES) poisons the entire batch, silently losing telemetry this collector exists to capture. HOW: skip invalid reports (log and `continue`) and still process the valid ones, reserving 422 only for payloads where nothing is processable.

Import of non-existent `sentry.api.fields.actor.ActorField` breaks module import for all detector endpoints — WHAT: `from sentry.api.fields.actor import ActorField` imports a class that does not exist anywhere in the repository — there is no `actor.py` under `src/sentry/api/fields`, no `class ActorField` definition repo-wide, and no other file imports anything from `sentry.api.fields.<submodule>`. WHY: importing this validator module raises ModuleNotFoundError at import time, so every workflow_engine endpoint that imports `BaseDetectorTypeValidator` fails to load (broken create/update detector endpoints). HOW: add `src/sentry/api/fields/actor.py` defining `ActorField` (returning an object with `is_user`/`is_team`/`id`, as the owner-handling code expects), or remove the import and the owner feature.

Runtime-unsubscriptable `serializers.Serializer[Any]` raises TypeError at import, breaking the collector endpoint module — WHAT: `class BrowserReportSerializer(serializers.Serializer[Any])` subscripts DRF's `Serializer` in a base-class list, which is evaluated at runtime; stock DRF serializers do not define `__class_getitem__`, this is the only runtime-subscripted serializer in the entire codebase, and no `django_stubs_ext`/monkeypatch is enabled anywhere in the repo. WHY: raises `TypeError: type 'Serializer' is not subscriptable` at module import time, so the browser reporting collector endpoint module fails to load. HOW: drop the subscript — `class BrowserReportSerializer(serializers.Serializer):` (the `[Any]` parameterization adds nothing at runtime here).

findings.description: Mutated config copy is discarded; the returned monitor context uses the original config so the schedule_type display substitution never takes effect (carried over verbatim from mark_failed.py). — WHAT: get_monitor_environment_context builds config = monitor_environment.monitor.config.copy() and substitutes the human-readable schedule_type into that copy, but the returned dict uses monitor_environment.monitor.config (the original), so the mutation is silently discarded and the copy is dead code. WHY: the emitted monitor context in the occurrence event payload keeps the raw integer schedule_type instead of the display value the code intends, and the misleading copy/mutate pattern invites future edits to the wrong object. NOTE: this defect was carried over verbatim from the deleted get_monitor_environment_context in mark_failed.py — it is pre-existing, not introduced by this refactor, but it now lives in these added lines. HOW: return the mutated copy in the payload.

get_monitor_environment_context drops the schedule_type substitution by returning the raw monitor config instead of the display-substituted copy it computed. — get_monitor_environment_context computes a display-substituted copy of the monitor config but then returns monitor_environment.monitor.config, so the schedule_type substitution is silently dropped from the context. Return the substituted copy instead. Per the analysis, this is a pre-existing bug moved verbatim by the refactor (not introduced or worsened by it) and was already reported in the prior pass.

findings.description: Unguarded prisma update inside the catch block can throw and abort the entire SMS scheduling cron run. — WHAT: the catch block now performs an unguarded prisma.workflowReminder.update; if it throws, the exception escapes the for-loop. WHY: the most common reason for entering the catch is a database/connectivity failure (or the reminder row was already removed by a concurrent cron run's deleteMany), so the retry-count update is likely to throw too — aborting processing of all remaining reminders and failing the whole cron run with a 500, whereas before this PR the catch only logged and continued to the next reminder. The same double-fault occurs when the else-branch update throws, since catch then re-runs the identical failing update. HOW: wrap the catch-block update in its own try/catch (or use updateMany + increment so a missing row is a no-op) so one reminder's failure cannot abort the run.

retryCount>1 delete clause is not scoped to SMS reminders, so the SMS cron can delete reminders of other methods. — WHAT: the new OR branch { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } in the deleteMany dropped the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter (and has no scheduled filter), so this SMS cron now deletes workflow reminders of any method once their retryCount exceeds 1. WHY: the original cleanup was explicitly scoped to SMS reminders; as written, any current or future code path that increments retryCount on non-SMS (e.g. EMAIL) reminders — or an SMS reminder that later got scheduled — would have those rows silently deleted by the SMS scheduling cron. Today only this handler increments retryCount so the impact is latent, but the clause contradicts the intended SMS-only scope. HOW: keep the method filter inside the retryCount branch: { method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }.

Stale read-modify-write of retryCount loses increments under overlapping cron runs; use atomic increment. — WHAT: retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 is a non-atomic read-modify-write using the value fetched at the start of the run. WHY: if two cron executions overlap (or the same run retries), both read the same retryCount and both write N+1 instead of N+2, so a failing reminder gets more than the intended two scheduling attempts before being deleted — the exact unbounded-rescheduling behavior this PR aims to eliminate. HOW: use Prisma's atomic increment: data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } in both the else branch and the catch branch.

The catch block's retryCount-incrementing database update is unguarded. — Unguarded update in the catch block: the catch handler performs a database update (incrementing retryCount) without guarding that update itself. This is one of the three pre-existing findings the analysis reaffirms; it is located in the new else/catch logic within the changed hunk at lines 267-286.

The deleteMany OR-branch omits the `method: SMS` filter, broadening which reminders get deleted. — The deleteMany call's OR branch drops the `method: SMS` filter, so the deletion is no longer restricted to SMS-method reminders. This is one of the three pre-existing findings the analysis reaffirms; no file path or line numbers for the deleteMany are given in the analysis.

retryCount is updated via a non-atomic read-modify-write instead of an atomic increment. — Non-atomic retryCount read-modify-write: retryCount is read from the fetched reminder and then written back as a separate incremented update rather than via an atomic operation, making it race-prone. This is one of the three pre-existing findings the analysis reaffirms; the increment occurs in the catch logic of the changed hunk at lines 267-286.

goldensDetail.text: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

findings.description: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is never True for spawn-context children, so hung flusher processes are never killed before a duplicate replacement is started. — WHAT: `process.kill()` in `_ensure_processes_alive` is gated behind `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, but the flusher spawns children via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which returns `SpawnProcess` instances — a sibling of `ForkProcess` (what `multiprocessing.Process` resolves to with the default fork context on Linux/Python 3.13), not a subclass. WHY: the isinstance check is always False in production, so a hung flusher child (the `"hang"` path, where `is_alive()` is still True) is never killed before `_create_process_for_shards` starts a replacement — two live processes then flush the same shards concurrently, producing duplicate segments to Kafka and racing `done_flush_segments` deletions, while the dead/hung process leaks and `process_restarts` escalates to RuntimeError. The old code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally, so this is a regression. HOW: check `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.context.BaseProcess)` (or `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`), or simply attempt `process.kill()` in the try/except as before — threads (test mode) are already excluded by the missing attribute, which the new `except (ValueError, AttributeError)` handles.

Inconsistent metrics tag key ("shards" vs "shard") between the two newly added flusher timers breaks per-shard grouping. — WHAT: The newly added `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` timer uses tag key `"shards"` while the sibling `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` timer and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` timing added in the same loop use `"shard"` for the identical `shard_tag` value. WHY: metrics for the same per-process flush cycle cannot be grouped or filtered under one tag key — dashboards/alerts keyed on `shard` silently exclude the wait_produce series, degrading the per-shard observability this PR is adding. HOW: use the same tag key `"shard"` in the wait_produce timer.

findings.description: Removing the global BuildIndex lock without adding per-key synchronization allows concurrent duplicate builds of the same index, racing bleve.New on the same on-disk directory and leaking the overwritten index. — WHAT: Removing the function-wide b.cacheMu from BuildIndex leaves only the final cache write locked, but neither getOrCreateIndex (search.go:287-313) nor build takes any per-key lock, so two concurrent Search/handleEvent calls for the same uncached NamespacedResource now run BuildIndex in parallel for the same key. WHY: for file-based indexes both goroutines call bleve.New on the same directory (racing index creation on disk, risking corruption/error), both execute the full expensive document build this PR is trying to speed up, and both assign b.cache[key] — last write wins and the losing bleve.Index is never Close()d, leaking file handles and scorch goroutines. HOW: guard against duplicate concurrent builds, e.g. use singleflight or a per-key mutex keyed by NamespacedResource around the build, or re-check b.cache under the write lock before overwriting and Close() the superseded index.

New TotalDocs() call in init races with watch-triggered BuildIndex cache writes because TotalDocs reads the index cache map without holding cacheMu. — WHAT: The new 'search index initialized' log calls s.search.TotalDocs() after the WatchWriteEvents goroutine has already been started, and bleveBackend.TotalDocs (bleve.go:203-213) iterates b.cache without holding cacheMu while the watch goroutine can concurrently trigger BuildIndex, which writes b.cache[key]. WHY: concurrent map read (TotalDocs) and map write (BuildIndex cache insert) is a data race that the Go runtime turns into a fatal 'concurrent map read and map write' crash, and events can arrive immediately because the SQL backend streams recent write events on a new watch. HOW: take b.cacheMu.RLock() inside bleveBackend.TotalDocs (and any other cache iteration), or move the log/TotalDocs call before the watch goroutine is started.

Postgres skip added in the same PR that introduces DB-backed init at server startup removes CI coverage for exactly the path being changed. — WHAT: The PR skips TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer on postgres with a TODO, in the same PR that makes ResourceServer run full DB-backed initialization (GetResourceStats, index builds, WatchWriteEvents) at startup. WHY: this removes the only CI coverage exercising the storage-server target against postgres exactly when the new startup-init path is introduced, so a postgres-specific init failure (the test 'works locally' but fails in Drone, suggesting an environment-dependent startup defect) ships undetected. HOW: fix the Drone postgres environment for this test (or gate only the failing assertion) instead of skipping the whole target test, and re-enable before merging the startup-init change.

Starting the event watcher only after the search index build completes drops all write events committed during the build, leaving the index permanently stale for those resources. — WHAT: Moving initWatcher() to run after search.init(ctx) opens a gap where write events are permanently lost from the search index: WatchWriteEvents (pkg/storage/unified/sql/backend.go:558-566) snapshots the latest RVs via listLatestRVs at watcher start and its poller only streams events with RV greater than that snapshot, while each index build lists resources at fetchLatestRV (backend.go:476) captured at build time. WHY: any write committed after a resource's index-build snapshot but before the watcher starts is neither included in the built index nor delivered to handleEvent, so those resources are missing/stale in search results indefinitely (until they happen to be modified again); the window lasts the entire startup index build, which this PR itself notes is slow, and coincides with startup provisioning writes. The previous order (watcher first, then build) was safe because it produced overlap, and index writes are idempotent upserts keyed by resource. HOW: start the watcher before building the indexes again, or capture the build's list RVs and start the watch from those RVs so the two coverages overlap instead of gap.

goldensDetail.text: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

findings.description: REALM_ONLY branch missing isEnabled re-check causes stale disabled IDPs to be shown — WHAT: isEnabled re-check added for ORG_ONLY and ALL paths (lines 75 and 80) but omitted for REALM_ONLY path (line 59), leaving stale disabled realm brokers visible. WHY: getForLogin caches ID sets; after an IDP is disabled the cached ID remains and is re-hydrated via getById, so callers must re-filter; REALM_ONLY now inconsistently skips this filter. HOW: add same `idp.isEnabled() &&` guard to line 59 filter.

getLoginPredicate NPE when config map is null — WHAT: Added predicate `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` dereferences config map without null check. WHY: If IdentityProviderModel.getConfig() returns null (e.g., legacy/deserialized model) the predicate throws NPE, breaking getForLogin and all login invalidation checks. HOW: guard with `idp.getConfig() != null` or use `getConfig().getOrDefault(..., "false")` with null-safe map access as done in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean:107.

getForLogin invalidates whole FetchMode cache on new org query and can skip invalidation on same-org updates — WHAT: getForLogin caches IDs per FetchMode but invalidates entire cache entry on any new searchKey by calling cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) before merging (line 236), and registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate skips invalidation when both original/updated are login IDPs with same organizationId even though cached ID set per organizationId is now stale for that org. WHY: A new organization login request evicts all previously cached orgs for that mode; concurrent updates that keep orgId same but add/remove IDP from login predicate via enabled/hideOnLogin will incorrectly skip invalidation, returning stale list.

removeAll leaves login cache stale — WHAT: removeAll() invalidates only IDP count but not the new IDP login caches. WHY: After removeAll the IdentityProviderListQuery entries for ".idp.login.*" remain cached and still return stale IDs via getForLogin until realm deletion or explicit login invalidation. HOW: Mirror create/remove invalidation and register invalidation for each FetchMode in removeAll().

HashSet loses ordering of getForLogin results — WHAT: getForLogin caches IDs in a HashSet via Collectors.toSet() and rebuilds results via HashSet, losing the delegate's deterministic ordering. WHY: Callers that depend on DB ordering (e.g., sorted login display before bean-level sort, or direct getForLogin consumers) now see nondeterministic order across requests. HOW: Collect to LinkedHashSet/preserve List order and return in insertion order (e.g., Collectors.toCollection(LinkedHashSet::new)).

findings.description: findByName called with wrong arity (3 args vs 2-arg API) in hasPermission — WHAT: resourceStore.findByName is called with 3 arguments (server, client.getId(), server.getId()) at line 214 and (server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId()) at line 244, while ResourceStore.findByName throughout codebase takes 2 arguments (server,name). WHY: causes compile-time mismatch or wrong overload dispatched, breaking client-specific permission checks and global Clients permission checks in V2. HOW: change to resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId()) and resourceStore.findByName(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) — consistent with AdminPermissionsSchema line 101/133 and UserPermissionsV2 line 117.

Missing resourceId filter causes cross-resource scope grant in V2 — WHAT: hasPermission loops over evaluatePermission results without checking permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()) — iterates all granted permissions and returns true if any scope matches. WHY: diverges from correct UserPermissionsV2 pattern (line 135) and can grant VIEW/MANAGE/CONFIGURE/MAP_ROLES for a client when the caller only has that scope on a different resource (e.g., Users or another client), violating authorization contract. HOW: filter by resourceId before scope check, as done in UserPermissionsV2.

NPE when global Clients fallback resource is null in hasPermission(ClientModel,String) — WHAT: hasPermission(ClientModel,String) dereferences fallback resource without null-check after getResourceTypeResource. WHY: getResourceTypeResource can return null (authz disabled, wrong client, or resource not yet created) causing NPE at findByResource or at new ResourcePermission(resource,...). HOW: Add null guard matching hasPermission(String) — if (resource == null) return false; before findByResource and before evaluatePermission.

goldensDetail.text: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

findings.description: Authorization requires both admin AND owner instead of OR — WHAT: Authorization check uses && requiring user to be BOTH team admin AND team owner (line 47-48). WHY: Team admins who are not owners (and vice versa) are incorrectly denied, breaking intended team-admin-or-owner access; variable name isTeamAdminOrOwner implies OR. HOW: Change && to || and handle teamId null to avoid false calls with 0.

Case-sensitive guest filter bypasses blacklist and allows duplicates — WHAT: Guest deduplication and blacklist check is case-sensitive and does not deduplicate within input array (lines 74-78). WHY: "A@b.com" vs "a@b.com" bypasses both duplicate and BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS (which is lowercased) checks, and guests=["a@b.com","a@b.com"] creates duplicate Attendee rows via createMany. HOW: Normalize to lower case for comparison and deduplicate input first.

Email dispatch uses unfiltered input instead of deduplicated guests — WHAT: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with original guests instead of filtered uniqueGuests (line 168). WHY: Sends emails to blacklisted/already-existing/duplicate addresses that were filtered from DB insert, and misses the intent to notify only actually added guests. HOW: Pass uniqueGuests.

Calendar update uses requester credentials instead of organizer's — WHAT: EventManager is constructed with requester's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of organizer's credentials. WHY: When an attendee or team admin (not organizer) adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees attempts to update the calendar with the requester's credentials which lack access to the organizer's destination calendar, causing silent calendar-sync failure while DB attendees already committed (no transaction rollback). HOW: Fetch credentials for booking.userId/organizer.

Missing booking status/time guard allows adding guests to cancelled or past bookings — WHAT: Handler never validates booking.status (or that booking hasn't ended) after fetch. WHY: Guests can be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED/past bookings, creating orphan attendees and triggering calendar updates/emails for a dead event. HOW: Check booking.status and time bounds after the NOT_FOUND guard and reject with BAD_REQUEST if not ACCEPTED/upcoming.

DB write before calendar sync with no transaction leaves orphan attendees on calendar failure — WHAT: prisma.booking.update createMany at lines 92-106 commits before EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees at line 165 with no transaction or compensation. WHY: If calendar sync throws, DB already contains new attendees while calendar does not, leaving persistent inconsistency and no rollback; concurrent requests also TOCTOU past the filter at 74. HOW: Wrap attendee creation and calendar sync in an interactive transaction or create attendees only after successful calendar update, and handle UniqueConstraint violations.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
This calls the email sender with the original guests, so existing attendees included in the input will be treated as new when sending notifications, leading to incorrect emails.

findings.description: Regex char-class mis-handles hyphen causing English lookup to fail for hyphenated locales — WHAT: English-file derivation uses replaceAll regex `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` where `[a-zA-Z-_]` interprets `-` as range Z-_, so locales containing hyphen (zh-CN, pt-BR, etc.) do not match and englishFile is wrong. WHY: The subsequent FileInputStream throws FileNotFound wrapped as RuntimeException, and verify() only catches IOException, so the Mojo crashes instead of reporting a validation error. HOW: Use a literal pattern or escape hyphen: `_[a-zA-Z_\-]*\.properties` or avoid regex entirely via replace/replaceFirst with Pattern.quote, or use lastIndexOf('_') manipulation.

Stale matcher + mutate-during-iterate causes wrong anchor removal and poor diagnostics — WHAT: santizeAnchors mutates `value` with replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(...),"") while iterating matcher over the original string value. WHY: After first removal the matcher state is stale and replaceFirst always removes the first occurrence in the mutated string, so duplicate identical anchors remove the wrong instance and an extra anchor leaves earlier allowed anchors already stripped, producing confusing sanitized vs value diff and an error message without key/file. HOW: Collect allowed anchors first, then remove via a dedicated builder or verify count/equality without mutating during iteration, and include key+file in the anchor mismatch message.

RuntimeException escapes verify() error handling and crashes plugin on missing English file — WHAT: verifySafeHtml wraps FileInputStream IOException in RuntimeException, but verify() only catches IOException. WHY: Missing English file (due to path derivation bug or absent translation) crashes the maven plugin with unhandled RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException with actionable message. HOW: Catch broader exception or make verifySafeHtml throw MojoExecutionException / handle Missing English file explicitly.

Diff trimming can OOB when sanitized is much shorter than value — WHAT: Diff-trimming logic at message construction can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when sanitized length << value length. WHY: start advances to sanitized.length() when value has allowed prefix but sanitized stripped tags, then sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length()-end) is called with start > end index (e.g., value="aaaa", sanitized="aa" => start=2, sanitized.substring(2,0)). HOW: Clamp to avoid overlap: compute safe end or guard substring with if (start > sanitized.length()-end) use whole strings, or use Math.max.

findings.description: Cache poison lets retry bypass device limit after first rejection — WHAT: tagDeviceUI sets localCache before DB call and TagDevice now propagates ErrDeviceLimitReached, so first limit-rejected device poisons cache and second request with same deviceID hits cache early return and bypasses limit. WHY: Cache is written unconditionally at 87 before CreateOrUpdateDevice at 93, and caller TagDevice at 144-148 now returns error only on first call; subsequent call returns nil from cache and client.go allows auth without DB enforcement. HOW: Move localCache.SetDefault to after successful CreateOrUpdateDevice, or delete cache entry on error (defer cleanup) and only cache on success.

TOCTOU race allows device limit to be exceeded under concurrency — WHAT: CreateOrUpdateDevice does check-then-act with separate CountDevices and Insert/Update without transaction or unique constraint to enforce limit. WHY: Two concurrent requests can both see count < limit (e.g., limit-1) and both insert, exceeding limit; conversely two requests when count>=limit for same new device may both take update path and both fail – TOCTOU window between 110-117 and 149-152. HOW: Enforce limit atomically – e.g., conditional insert with SELECT COUNT(*) guard in single statement/transaction, or add DB constraint/advisory lock, or serialize via serverlock.

Sync tagging blocks anonymous auth on DB and removes timeout/recover — WHAT: Authenticate changed from async fire-and-forget goroutine with background timeout and panic recovery to synchronous TagDevice on request ctx. WHY: Anonymous login now blocks on DB Count+Insert (and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached to deny auth), so DB slowness/failure adds latency/failure to hot auth path and loses panic isolation that previously prevented process crash. HOW: Keep tagging async best-effort for non-limit errors, or enforce limit synchronously with timeout + recover and only block on ErrDeviceLimitReached; restore context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), timeoutTag) and recover wrapper for the non-blocking case.
