findings.description: Create records legacy metric on storage failure — WHAT: Create error path records legacy duration instead of storage duration (line 45). WHY: Storage failure is attributed to legacy histogram, storage histogram missing error sample breaks alerting/SLO. HOW: Call d.recordStorageDuration(true,...) on storage error, not recordLegacyDuration.

Update records legacy metric on storage failure — WHAT: Update error path records legacy duration instead of storage duration (line 129). WHY: Same inversion as Create, corrupts metrics cardinality and hides storage errors. HOW: Use d.recordStorageDuration(true,...) when d.Storage.Update fails.

Delete metric uses object name instead of kind — WHAT: Delete success path records storage duration with `name` as kind label (line 106). WHY: Metrics series gets per-object name cardinality explosion and kind label is lost. HOW: Pass options.Kind not name.

DeleteCollection legacy async uses storage metric — WHAT: DeleteCollection async legacy path records storage duration instead of legacy duration (line 166). WHY: Legacy latency/errors never observed, storage histogram double-counted. HOW: Call d.recordLegacyDuration for the d.Legacy.DeleteCollection result.

Delete loses log fields and legacy async inherits cancelled ctx — WHAT: Delete uses d.Log instead of enriched log for klog.NewContext (line 97) and all async goroutines derive from cancellable request ctx. WHY: Loses kind/method fields on context logger and legacy async writes are cancelled when request context ends, silently dropping best-effort legacy backup. HOW: Use log for NewContext and derive async ctx from context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or context.Background().

Nil options dereference panic — WHAT: Get/List/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection unconditionally dereference options.Kind / listOptions.ResourceVersion without nil check. WHY: Callers may pass nil *metav1.GetOptions/*DeleteOptions/*ListOptions causing nil-dereference panic, e.g. Get with nil options after refactor no longer defaults to &metav1.GetOptions{}. HOW: Guard with nil check or default options before WithValues/metrics.

findings.description: Race between exists check and create allows duplicate topics for same embed_url — WHAT: TopicEmbed.import has check-then-act race outside transaction (where(embed_url: url).first at line 15 then Topic.transaction at line 21). WHY: Two concurrent PollFeed/RetrieveTopic jobs for same embed_url both see embed.blank? and both create duplicate topics/posts with duplicate TopicEmbed rows. HOW: Add unique DB constraint on embed_url and use find_or_create / rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, or wrap the lookup inside the transaction with locking.

Unprotected Kernel.open crashes job and allows pipe/SSRF with no timeout — WHAT: TopicEmbed.import_remote uses Kernel.open(url).read at line 48 with no validation, timeout, or rescue. WHY: Invalid/unreachable URL raises unhandled exception crashing RetrieveTopic job; Kernel.open with leading '|' can execute commands (classic Ruby open pipe) and has no SSRF timeout. HOW: Replace open with Net::HTTP/Excon with timeout and rescue, validate url scheme/host first, and use URI.open or File discrimination (e.g., URI.open with explicit http).

Nil i.content crashes entire feed poll via NoMethodError on scrub — WHAT: poll_feed does CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) at line 35 without nil guard. WHY: SimpleRSS items often have nil content (using description instead) - nil.scrub raises NoMethodError aborting the entire hourly feed and skipping all remaining items. HOW: Use (i.content || i.description || '').to_s.scrub and rescue per-item so one bad entry does not abort loop.

Non-atomic setnx/expire can leave permanent throttle key on crash — WHAT: retrieved_recently? uses non-atomic $redis.setnx + expire at lines 27-28. WHY: If process crashes between setnx and expire the key lives forever, permanently throttling all future retrieves for that embed_url (effective DoS). HOW: Use atomic SET with NX+EX or $redis.setex / Lua, e.g., $redis.set(retrieved_key, "1", nx: true, ex: 60).

Invalid X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL blocks embedding in browsers — WHAT: ensure_embeddable sets X-Frame-Options to "ALLOWALL" at line 28. WHY: ALLOWALL is not a valid X-Frame-Options value (spec allows DENY, SAMEORIGIN, ALLOW-FROM); browsers treat invalid value as DENY, breaking the embed feature this PR is meant to enable. HOW: Remove header (no X-Frame-Options) or send ALLOW-FROM with correct syntax, or use Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors.

Unrescued URI parsing and nil contents crash absolutize_urls — WHAT: absolutize_urls does URI(url) with no rescue and assumes contents is a string at lines 56-61. WHY: Malformed embed_url raises URI::InvalidURIError bubbling up and crashing import/RetrieveTopic with no handling; if contents is nil (from nil RSS content) contents mutation (<<) and Nokogiri fragment raise NoMethodError. HOW: Rescue URI::InvalidURIError and return contents unchanged, and guard contents = contents.to_s.

TopicEmbed.import crashes with NoMethodError when contents is nil via contents << — WHAT: TopicEmbed.import does contents << on line 13 assuming contents is a String, but callers pass i.content (PollFeed) and doc.content (import_remote) which SimpleRSS/Readability can return as nil. WHY: nil << raises NoMethodError for any feed item without content or any readability page where extraction fails, crashing the PollFeed loop and the RetrieveTopic job for that embed_url. HOW: Normalize contents before mutation, e.g. contents = contents.to_s before the append, or return early if contents.nil?.

embed.post can be nil causing PostRevisor crash in update path — WHAT: In the update path embed.post is used without nil guard before PostRevisor.new(post) at line 35. WHY: If the associated post was deleted, embed.post returns nil and PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! raises NoMethodError, leaving embed.content_sha1 stale and future imports for that embed_url permanently broken. HOW: Guard with return/ recreate if post.nil? - e.g. if post.nil? then recreate topic/post or return nil.

findings.description: Backup code nulling leaves holes and race, should splice and detect exhaustion — WHAT: Verified backup code is nulled (backupCodes[index]=null) instead of removed, leaving null holes. WHY: Exhausted array of nulls still truthy so `!user.backupCodes` check fails - next use returns IncorrectBackupCode instead of MissingBackupCodes, and two concurrent logins can both pass indexOf before either update, allowing single code double-spend (check-then-act race). HOW: Remove entry with splice/filter and return MissingBackupCodes when no valid codes remain; use atomic update or filter nulls before indexOf.

Incomplete reset and stale ObjectURL revocation leaks backup codes — WHAT: resetState only clears password/error/step and handleSetup revokes ObjectURL via stale state closure (backupCodesUrl). WHY: Re-opening modal shows previous backupCodes/dataUri/secret, leaks prior codes and creates un-revoked blob URLs via stale closure (revokes previous render value, not latest). HOW: Clear backupCodes/backupCodesUrl/dataUri/secret in resetState and revoke via ref or useEffect cleanup, not stale state var.

Throwing instead of returning JSON on missing key causes unhandled 500 — WHAT: Missing encryption key throws Error instead of returning JSON response. WHY: Throwing inside Next.js API handler after headers not sent triggers unhandled rejection/generic 500 via error handler, not the expected {error: ...} shape, and can crash with ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT if partially written. HOW: Return res.status(500).json({error: ErrorCode.InternalServerError}) instead of throw.

TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable call adds backupCode arg but callee not updated, so disable-via-backup-code never reaches server — WHAT: DisableTwoFactorModal now calls TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable(password, totpCode, backupCode) with 3 args but TwoFactorAuthAPI not changed in this PR (not in diff), so callee still expects (password, code) and silently ignores backupCode. WHY: Disabling 2FA via backup code from UI never sends backupCode to server, server falls through to totp branch and returns SecondFactorRequired/IncorrectTwoFactorCode - user with lost access is permanently stuck. HOW: Update TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable to accept backupCode and send { password, code: totpCode, backupCode } in request body.

Backup code login skips password check when totpCode also present, allowing backup-code-only auth — WHAT: New backupCode branch `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)` bypasses password verification when a dummy totpCode is also supplied, because password check is gated by `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`. WHY: Attacker with a stolen/ leaked backup code can authenticate without knowing password by sending { email, backupCode, totpCode: '000000' } - password check is skipped and backup code is accepted, breaking credential authentication. HOW: Verify password unconditionally when user.password exists before accepting backup code, or change gate to `!credentials.totpCode && !credentials.backupCode` and add explicit password check inside backup code branch.

goldensDetail.text: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

findings.description: findMany deleted without raw-query replacement breaks callers — WHAT: findMany() method was deleted in this conversion (replaced by getBaseConditions) with no raw-query replacement, breaking the public service contract. WHY: Any existing caller of insightsBookingService.findMany() (parity with InsightsRoutingService.findMany) will throw TypeError: findMany is not a function at runtime. HOW: Re-introduce findMany that composes getBaseConditions() into a Prisma.$queryRaw / $queryRawUnsafe query (or keep findMany thin wrapper) as done in routing service migration.

Optional teamId weakens type safety and silently suppresses data — WHAT: Constructor now accepts InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions with optional teamId for all scopes, weakening the discriminated-union contract. WHY: Callers can compile scope:"team" without teamId; safeParse then fails, this.options becomes null, and buildAuthorization silently returns 1=0 yielding empty results instead of a compile-time/type error or thrown validation. HOW: Keep constructor param as InsightsBookingServiceOptions (or make PublicOptions discriminated union requiring teamId when scope==="team") and/or throw on !validation.success instead of nulling.

goldensDetail.text: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

findings.description: queued default is evaluated at import, not per-instance — WHAT: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class-definition/import time, so every AssignmentSource created without explicit queued shares the same stale timestamp. WHY: defeats the intent of recording when the assignment was queued and makes all inbound events appear to have identical time, breaking any ordering/dedup logic. HOW: use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead of a call at definition time.

datetime in to_dict/from_dict not JSON-serializable for Celery task — WHAT: `to_dict()` via `asdict(self)` returns a `datetime` for `queued` and `from_dict()` does `cls(**input_dict)` with no datetime parsing, so Celery JSON serialization fails. WHY: `sync_group_assignee_outbound` passes that dict as `assignment_source_dict` to `apply_async` (sync.py:141); JSON serializer raises `TypeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable` and outbound sync is never enqueued/dropped on retry; round-trip via JSON would leave `queued` as a string violating the type. HOW: serialize queued to isoformat in `to_dict()` and parse ISO string back to datetime in `from_dict()`.

should_sync signature change breaks subclasses with old single-arg override when called with assignment_source — WHAT: Changing IssueBasicIntegration.should_sync to def should_sync(self, attribute, sync_source: AssignmentSource | None = None) breaks existing overrides that define def should_sync(self, attribute) with a single arg. WHY: sync_assignee_outbound task now calls installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source) with 2 positional args, so any subclass (e.g. Example integration or custom IssueBasicIntegration) still using the old signature raises TypeError: should_sync() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given and crashes the outbound sync task. HOW: Make the new param backward compatible by accepting *args/**kwargs in base or checking signature, e.g. def should_sync(self, attribute, sync_source=None, **kwargs) and update IssueSyncIntegration to match, or keep old single-arg call sites using inspection.

findings.description: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and will fail to instantiate after base class change — WHAT: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but implements none of its 4 abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data) with only `pass`. WHY: Instantiating via Detector.detector_handler -> group_type.detector_handler(self) raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class with abstract methods, breaking any detector of type metric_alert_fire. HOW: Either keep it as DetectorHandler with stub evaluate, or provide concrete (even NoOp) implementations for the 4 abstract methods, or mark the class as abstract if not intended to be instantiated.

Abstract evaluate signature break silently breaks list-returning subclasses/mocks — WHAT: DetectorHandler.evaluate signature changed from list[DetectorEvaluationResult] to dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult] and StatefulDetectorHandler added new abstract build_occurrence_and_event_data — any existing test double, mock, or out-of-tree subclass returning a list will silently break / fail type checks. WHY: Callers like process_detectors now call .values() on result; a list return will raise AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'values', and concrete subclasses missing build_occurrence_and_event_data will fail instantiation. HOW: Update all overrides/tests to return dict and implement build_occurrence_and_event_data, or provide a compatibility shim that accepts list and converts to dict.

missedGoldens.text: Docstring says this returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. Consider updating the docstring to match the new return type.

goldensDetail.text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains pass, failing to implement its required abstract methods: counter_names (property), get_dedupe_value(), get_group_key_values(), and build_occurrence_and_event_data(). This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.
Docstring says this returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. Consider updating the docstring to match the new return type.

findings.description: Duplicate downsize def overwrites numeric overload breaking ResizeEmoji — WHAT: Duplicate definition of `self.downsize` - lines 145 and 149 define the same method, Ruby keeps only the last (dimensions string) and silently drops the (max_width,max_height) overload. WHY: Existing caller Jobs::ResizeEmoji at app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 args and will now raise `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (5 for 3..4)` breaking emoji resizing; any other caller using numeric width/height is broken. HOW: Keep both signatures via single method with arity check or rename the string version (e.g. `downsize_by_percentage`) or handle both: `def self.downsize(from,to,a,b=nil,opts={})` and dispatch on whether `b` is Hash.

80% downsize fails for animated GIFs and ignores failure, leaving oversized file — WHAT: Loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` in-place and ignores return value; for animated GIFs dispatch goes to `downsize_instructions_animated` -> `resize_instructions_animated` which runs `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%` which expects `WxH` not percentage and fails. WHY: `convert_with` returns false, file size never shrinks, loop burns 5 converts for no effect and leaves oversized/corrupted file to be passed to `Upload.create_for`, causing validation failure or truncated upload. HOW: Check return value and break on failure, handle GIF percentage separately (e.g. compute numeric dimensions or skip animation branch for percentage), and downsize to a temp file then move on success instead of overwriting source in place.

Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores site settings for attachments — WHAT: `validateUploadedFile` and 413 handler hardcode `maxSizeKB = 10*1024` instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb']`. WHY: Client now allows 10MB attachments even when `max_attachment_size_kb` is 1MB (late server error) and incorrectly rejects attachments larger than 10MB when site allows 50MB; also ignores per-site `max_image_size_kb` tuning, breaking contract with server downsizing feature. HOW: Restore type-aware lookup for non-images and keep 10MB as fallback only for images that will be downsized, e.g. `var maxSizeKB = type==='image' ? 10*1024 : Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb'];`.

Nil tempfile after rescued download crashes on tempfile.size in Upload.create_for — WHAT: API download does `FileHelper.download(... ) rescue nil` then `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile, ..., tempfile.size)` dereferences nil without guard. WHY: When download fails (network error, 10MB limit, invalid URL) tempfile is nil and tempfile.size raises NoMethodError crashing request with 500 instead of validation error. HOW: Guard create path: return error or early return if tempfile.nil?, or use `tempfile&.size` and handle nil upload.

goldensDetail.text: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.

findings.description: update/destroy dereference nil host on unknown id — WHAT: update and destroy call save_host(host)/host.destroy without nil guard when EmbeddableHost.where(id:).first returns nil. WHY: Raises NoMethodError (500) on unknown id instead of 404/validation error; an admin typo or stale client state crashes the request. HOW: Guard with not-found response (e.g., render_json_error 404 or raise Discourse::NotFound) before save_host/destroy.

before_validation crashes on nil host — WHAT: before_validation does self.host.sub! without nil guard and save_host blindly assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host]. WHY: Blank/missing host (params missing or empty) raises NoMethodError inside validation lifecycle instead of returning validation error; create with empty host crashes. HOW: Guard in callback (return unless self.host.present?) and in save_host with params.dig + presence check.

case-sensitive lookup breaks host_allowed? — WHAT: record_for_host uses where("lower(host) = ?", host) without downcasing the looked-up host. WHY: URI-parsed host retains original case so 'Example.COM' != lower('example.com') match fails; host_allowed? returns false for valid referer with different casing and TopicEmbed.import assigns nil category. HOW: Downcase parameter: where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase).first

EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that discards updates — WHAT: Admin::EmbeddingController#update renders the embedding without applying or persisting any parameters. WHY: PUT to /admin/embedding silently succeeds while discarding edits, so admin changes appear saved but are lost on reload, breaking the embedding configuration flow. HOW: Implement update logic for the embedding (e.g., update embeddable hosts or SiteSettings from params) or remove the route/action if update is handled elsewhere.

goldensDetail.text: NoMethodError before_validation in EmbeddableHost

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

findings.description: Fallback list crashes on nil SiteSetting.default_locale and fails to dedupe String vs Symbol locales — WHAT: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym without nil guard and without normalizing the incoming locale type, so String 'en' vs Symbol :en are distinct. WHY: If SiteSetting.default_locale is nil/blank (DB not seeded, migration, early boot) to_sym raises NoMethodError crashing every request in ApplicationController#set_locale's ensure_loaded! path, and even when present duplicate entries ["en",:en] survive uniq causing redundant loads and fallback chain with type-mismatched entries breaking expected deduplication. HOW: Normalize all entries to Symbol via presence check, e.g. [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en].map{|l| l.to_s.to_sym if l.present?}.compact.uniq or safe navigation SiteSetting.default_locale.presence&.to_sym and locale.to_sym.

goldensDetail.text: Thread-safety issue with lazy @loaded_locales

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

findings.description: Null return on concurrent delete is inconsistent with exception-throwing path and propagates nullable Long to callers — WHAT: getSubGroupsCount now returns null when modelSupplier.get() is null after concurrent delete, while the isUpdated() path throws IllegalStateException for the same 'not found' condition. WHY: Inconsistent contract causes null Long to propagate to callers such as GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount -> GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount(null), risking NPE on auto-unboxing (long) or incorrect null count in API response and hiding the deleted-group error. HOW: Make paths consistent: either throw IllegalStateException when model == null (matching getDelegateForUpdate/isUpdated) or return a defined fallback like 0L / cached.getSubGroups(...).size().

The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

findings.description: Inverted slug condition creates orgs without slug when billing disabled and with wrong slug when enabled — WHAT: Top-level `slug` spread condition is inverted from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`. WHY: When billing is disabled the organization is now created without a `slug` (DB unique violation / missing URL), and when billing is enabled `slug` is set directly instead of via `requestedSlug` flow, breaking org creation. HOW: Restore negated condition: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` or `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` while keeping `requestedSlug` on `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`.

findings.description: Member route param mismatch causes ParameterMissing for add/remove — WHAT: add_members/remove_member require :group_id but route is a member route that provides :id, so params.require(:group_id) raises ActionController::ParameterMissing. WHY: JS calls PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members.json (routes.rb 49-50 inside resources without member/collection), Rails sets params[:id] not :group_id, so every membership change 400s. HOW: change controller to params.require(:id) or params[:group_id]||params[:id] or fix routes to 'member do put/delete members' with explicit param.

Update forces visible=false when param omitted — WHAT: update unconditionally sets visible to false when param is absent. WHY: params[:visible]=="true" is false when key missing, so PATCH that only changes alias_level/name silently flips visible off, breaking visibility. HOW: only assign when key present: group.visible = params[:visible]=="true" if params.key?(:visible)

totalPages off-by-one creates phantom empty page — WHAT: totalPages uses Math.floor(count/limit)+1 which is off-by-one for exact multiples (e.g., 50/50 => 2 instead of 1). WHY: causes showingLast to be false on last page and next to compute offset past total, yielding an empty phantom page. HOW: use Math.ceil(user_count/limit)

Split without strip silently drops usernames with spaces — WHAT: usernames.split(",") iterates without stripping whitespace, so "alice, bob" yields " bob" which User.find_by_username misses. WHY: user-selector typically inserts ", " separator, so bulk adds silently drop every user after the first, wrong output with no error. HOW: strip each token and reject blanks: usernames.split(",").map(&:strip).reject(&:blank?).each

remove_member passes Integer to has_many :through delete, which expects User objects and will fail — WHAT: remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) where user_id is an Integer (params.require(:user_id).to_i). WHY: For has_many :through (Group has_many :users through: :group_users) Rails expects model instances, not ids - passing Integer raises ActiveRecord::AssociationTypeMismatch or silently deletes nothing, so admin removal of group members crashes (500) or silently fails instead of removing. HOW: Use the join model or the domain method: group.group_users.where(user_id: user_id).delete_all or if user = User.find_by(id: user_id); group.remove(user) if user; end

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.

findings.description: PasswordForm.configuredFor incorrectly treats passkey-only users as password-configured — WHAT: PasswordForm.configuredFor now returns true for users who have only a passkey and no password due to ||isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user). WHY: Breaks the CredentialValidator contract for the password authenticator — flows/required-actions will treat a passkey-only user as password-configured and present/createLoginPassword challenges that can never succeed or incorrectly skip password setup. HOW: Remove the passkey branch from PasswordForm.configuredFor or gate it on password credential presence; keep passkey UI enablement only in authenticate/challenge, not in configuredFor.

Re-auth error helper NPEs when authenticationSession is null via new WebAuthn path — WHAT: setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError dereferences context.getAuthenticationSession() without null check and is now called from WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse. WHY: If createErrorResponse is invoked when the authenticationSession is null/cleared, getAuthNote throws NPE, crashing the error challenge that the PR intends to fix for re-auth passkey failures. HOW: Guard with if (context.getAuthenticationSession()==null) return; before getAuthNote.

missedGoldens.text: ConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called without UserModel parameter

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is sti

goldensDetail.text: ConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called without UserModel parameter

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

findings.description: Missing re-check after write-lock acquisition causes stampede and can overwrite valid cache with nil — WHAT: Double-checked locking is broken - after RUnlock miss the code acquires Lock but never re-checks entryPointAssetsCache before recomputing. WHY: N concurrent cache misses all pass the first nil check, then serialize on Lock and each re-reads assets-manifest.json (or CDN) and overwrites the cache, causing thundering herd, wasted I/O, and allowing a later error (result=nil) to clobber a valid value just stored by the first waiter. HOW: Re-check cache after acquiring write lock and only cache on success: Lock(); defer Unlock(); if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }; ... if err==nil && result != nil { entryPointAssetsCache = result }.

Exclusive lock held across file/HTTP I/O blocks all readers and serializes startup — WHAT: Exclusive Lock is held across blocking I/O (readWebAssetsFromFile / readWebAssetsFromCDN) from Lock() at line 48 to deferred Unlock at return, while RWMutex writers block all RLock readers. WHY: Serializes all concurrent GetWebAssets callers on file and HTTP I/O; thundering-herd that previously wasted work now also blocks fast-path readers for the duration of os.Open/json.Decode/http.Do, creating latency spike and liveness bottleneck on startup. HOW: Do not hold entryPointAssetsCacheMu across I/O — load outside the lock (optimistic load) then re-acquire Lock, re-check cache, and only then publish; or use singleflight to coalesce loads.

goldensDetail.text: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

findings.description: Unprotected metadata["sender"]["login"] access crashes pipeline on missing keys — WHAT: Direct access integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] raises KeyError if metadata/sender/login missing. WHY: Uncaught exception crashes install with 500 instead of rendering the added error page, breaking the new validation flow for any malformed or legacy integration. HOW: Use chained .get() with default and treat missing sender as invalid installation request -> return error(request, self.active_organization).

Unhandled exceptions from token exchange/user-info leave pipeline with 500 instead of error page — WHAT: safe_urlopen and get_user_info calls have no try/except, only parse_qsl is guarded. WHY: Network errors, HTTP error status, or invalid token raise and propagate as 500, aborting the pipeline before the added error() handling can run and leaving the external GitHub OAuth call on the hot request path without timeout handling. HOW: Wrap safe_urlopen/safe_urlread and get_user_info in try/except and return error(request, self.active_organization) on any exception, and pass explicit timeout to safe_urlopen.

Redirect with None installation_id creates broken URL on forward install — WHAT: Forward-install redirect builds URL with installation_id = request.GET.get("installation_id") without checking for None. WHY: reverse("integration-installation", args=["github", None]) produces a malformed URL (/extensions/github/setup/None/) or reverse failure, breaking direct-from-GitHub installs when GitHub omits the param. HOW: Validate installation_id is not None before redirect; if None return invalid request error or redirect to integration directory.

Early return on Integration.DoesNotExist bypasses new sender validation for fresh installs — WHAT: GitHubInstallation returns pipeline.next_step() on Integration.DoesNotExist before the new sender-login check, so the added validation is skipped when the Integration row has not yet been created by the webhook. WHY: An attacker can race the webhook or supply a fresh installation_id to advance the pipeline without the github_authenticated_user vs sender comparison the PR was meant to enforce, defeating the security goal for first-time installs. HOW: Move the github_authenticated_user validation before the early return or explicitly return error when Integration does not exist after OAuth step instead of silently advancing.

Request GET installation_id overrides validated pipeline state allowing ID swap after OAuth — WHAT: GitHubInstallation prefers request.GET.get("installation_id") over pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id") via dict get fallback. WHY: After OAuthLoginView validated and bound installation_id to pipeline state, a subsequent request to the installation step can override it with a different installation_id in the query string, causing the sender check to run against an attacker-chosen integration or to link the wrong installation to the organization. HOW: Validate that request GET installation_id, if present, equals pipeline state, or ignore query param and use pipeline state exclusively after OAuth.

findings.description: Constructor copy-paste checks grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId — WHAT: AccessTokenContext constructor validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId (line 73 checks grantType again). WHY: Null rawTokenId silently passes construction, later encodeTokenId produces prefix+":null" or NPE on substring and bypasses the intended fail-fast invariant. HOW: Change second check to Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")

setFormParams desynchronizes cached grantType — WHAT: OAuth2GrantType.Context caches grantType in constructor but setFormParams() does not refresh it. WHY: Any code that mutates formParams via setFormParams leaves getGrantType() returning the stale original value, causing encoders/consumers to see wrong grant_type (e.g., "na" vs actual) and produce incorrect token prefix. HOW: Update grantType inside setFormParams from the new formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)

Missing null check before indexOf on token ID — WHAT: getTokenContextFromTokenId calls encodedTokenId.indexOf(':') without null guard. WHY: Null token ID (e.g., legacy/introspection path or caller error) throws NPE instead of controlled IllegalArgumentException, crashing the request. HOW: Add null check and throw IllegalArgumentException if encodedTokenId is null

GrantType captured in Context is never written to ClientSessionContext so initial tokens always encode as UNKNOWN — WHAT: OAuth2GrantType.Context captures grantType from formParams at line 102 but never propagates it to ClientSessionContext, and the only writer of Constants.GRANT_TYPE is TokenManager line 248 for refresh_token. WHY: All non-refresh initial tokens (authorization_code, client_credentials, password, etc.) read Constants.GRANT_TYPE in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider:57 and find null, falling back to UNKNOWN "na", so the new encoding always stores "na" for grantType and the feature is dead for normal flows. HOW: In each OAuth2GrantType implementation (or centrally when ClientSessionContext is built from the grant Context), set clientSessionContext.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType()) so initToken can encode the real grant.

Missing null guard on getClientSession().getUserSession() risks NPE for service-account tokens — WHAT: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext dereferences clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession() without null checks at lines 47-48. WHY: For service-account/client_credentials flows there may be no ClientSession or UserSession (transient or absent), causing NPE during initToken/encode and breaking token issuance with 500 instead of handling gracefully. HOW: Add null guards: if clientSession==null or userSession==null return UNKNOWN sessionType or fallback to ONLINE, and guard getPersistenceState/isOffline calls.

Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage p

In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.

Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.

findings.description: Pause/Delete menu items stay hidden in list view despite grafana abilities being true because they still gate on rulerRule. — WHAT: Abilities are ORed between ruler and grafana-prom but render gates still require rulerRule (pause checks rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) and delete checks rulerRule truthy). WHY: In list view rulerRule is undefined, so canPause/canDelete can be true via grafana branch yet menu items never render, leaving pause/delete inaccessible. HOW: Gate on the same OR or on promRule – e.g., use prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) || rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) for pause and allow delete when either identifier is available, and make handleDelete accept prom-derived identifier.

Silence drawer never opens in list view because it only checks rulerRule. — WHAT: Silence drawer render checks rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) while list view only supplies promRule. WHY: Clicking Silence sets showSilenceDrawer=true but drawer condition fails when rule is undefined, so silence is dead for grafana prom rules in list view despite canSilence being true via grafana abilities. HOW: Check prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(promRule) as fallback and render SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer with promRule or unify prop to support both DTO types.

Hardcoding federated to false lifts immutability guard for federated rules. — WHAT: isFederated hardcoded to false in useAllRulerRuleAbilities/useAllAlertRuleAbilities (TODO comment) dropping isFederatedRuleGroup check. WHY: Federated Mimir rule groups become incorrectly mutable – Pause/Update/Delete/Restore are offered when they must be blocked as immutable. HOW: Restore isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(group) for ruler path or keep explicit guard and thread group info into useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities if needed.

List view no longer shows Creating/Deleting states after ruler removal. — WHAT: Removed ruler/prom matching loses Creating (ruler-only) and Deleting (prom-only) transient states; loader now renders only prom rules. WHY: Newly created rules are invisible until Prometheus syncs and deleting rules appear as normal instead of Deleting, breaking previous UX contract. HOW: Either keep lightweight ruler presence check for operations or document gap and add empty-state handling for groups.at(0) missing.

GrafanaGroupLoader crashes on empty prom groups due to unsafe `?.rules.map` without fallback — WHAT: Unsafe optional chaining before .map in GrafanaGroupLoader – `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules.map` throws when groups is empty or first group has no rules. WHY: `undefined?.rules` is undefined, then `.map` is property access on undefined → TypeError crashes list view. HOW: Fallback to empty array or optional map: `(promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules ?? []).map(...)` or `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules?.map`.

missedGoldens.text: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.

goldensDetail.text: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.

RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.

findings.description: Salesforce service returns stale credentials after refresh instead of new tokens — WHAT: Jsforce connection is created with stale credentialKey.access_token and credentialKey.instance_url after a refresh, ignoring the freshly parsed accessTokenParsed.data. WHY: The token refresh is persisted to prisma but never used for the returned Connection, so every call after a refresh still uses the expired access_token and fails. HOW: Use the refreshed data for the connection: accessToken: accessTokenParsed.data.access_token, instanceUrl: accessTokenParsed.data.instance_url (or fall back to credentialKey.instance_url only if missing).

Webex still uses strict safeParse so sharing-mode minimal tokens always fail — WHAT: Webex refresh wraps fetch with refreshOAuthTokens for credential-sharing but still validates with strict webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse that requires scope literal and refresh_token fields. WHY: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED the sync endpoint only returns {access_token, expiry}, so safeParse always fails and refresh always rejects, while zoom/office365 correctly use parseRefreshTokenResponse with minimum schema. HOW: Import and use parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseBody, webexRefreshedTokenSchema) like zoom does, or handle the shared-mode minimal response explicitly.

Dummy refresh_token injection overwrites real refresh_token in sharing mode — WHAT: parseRefreshTokenResponse injects dummy refresh_token="refresh_token" when missing and office365/zoom spread the parsed data over existing credentials, overwriting the real refresh_token. WHY: In sharing mode the sync endpoint returns only access_token+expiry, so the placeholder overwrites the valid refresh_token in memory/DB, corrupting future refresh flows and persisting a literal string as the token. HOW: Preserve the original refresh_token instead of overwriting: don't inject dummy into parsed data, or merge as {refresh_token: o365AuthCredentials.refresh_token, ...tokenResponse.data} and only fill if undefined.

Webhook missing method check and unhandled decrypt/parse crashes — WHAT: Handler has no HTTP method guard and lets Zod .parse and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) throw unhandled, plus uses findFirst+update/create race. WHY: GET or malformed/encrypted payloads crash with 500 instead of 4xx, leaks stack, and concurrent webhooks can duplicate credentials. HOW: Add if (req.method !== "POST") return 405, wrap schema parse + decrypt+JSON in try/catch returning 400, and use an atomic upsert/transaction on (userId,appId) unique constraint or catch unique-violation.

Broken Zod catch-all makes credential-sync parsing always fail — WHAT: minimumTokenResponseSchema is constructed with computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] which evaluate to a literal string like "ZodString" instead of a dynamic catch-all. WHY: The schema therefore requires a property named "ZodString" (number) that never exists, so safeParse always fails when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and every sync-endpoint response throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned", breaking credential sharing for Office365/Zoom/Webex/Salesforce. HOW: Replace with z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough() or .catchall(z.unknown()) and optionally refine expiry validation, e.g. z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough().superRefine(...).

Fragile statusText check mishandles Salesforce refresh errors — WHAT: Salesforce refresh checks if (response.statusText !== "OK") to detect errors. WHY: fetch response.statusText is implementation-dependent and often empty in Node, so valid 200 responses with statusText "" incorrectly throw, and non-200 responses with "OK" (or empty) are missed; error message also discards the JSON error body. HOW: Check response.ok or response.status (e.g., if (!response.ok) { const body = await response.text(); throw new HttpError({ statusCode: response.status, message: body || response.statusText }); }).

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from r

goldensDetail.text: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
Invalid Zod schema syntax. Computed property keys like [z.string().toString()] are not valid in Zod object schemas and will cause runtime errors.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

findings.description: order mixin off-by-one for legacy box ordinal-group — WHAT: @mixin order($val) passes $val directly to -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group, which are 1-indexed whereas CSS order is 0-indexed. WHY: Call sites @include order(2) and @include order(3) render one position too early on old WebKit/Firefox (ordinal-group 2 = order 1), breaking header panel/extra-info ordering on those browsers. HOW: Use $val + 1 for legacy ordinal-group: -webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val + 1; -moz-box-ordinal-group: $val + 1;

align-items mixin emits invalid -ms-align-items prefix — WHAT: @mixin align-items emits invalid property -ms-align-items and blindly copies $alignment to -webkit-box-align. WHY: -ms-align-items does not exist (correct is -ms-flex-align only) and legacy box-align values are start/end not flex-start/flex-end, so future callers with flex-start will generate invalid CSS and the extra property is dead code that may confuse autoprefixer/lint. HOW: Remove -ms-align-items: $alignment; and map flex-start/flex-end to start/end for -webkit-box-align if supported.

flexbox on .small-action makes float:right on button ineffective — WHAT: .small-action is changed to @include flexbox() but its child button retains float:right and .topic-avatar retains float:left. WHY: Float is ignored on flex items per spec, so the close/remove button no longer pins to the right edge and avatar/desc layout shifts, breaking the small-action row on all browsers. HOW: Replace float:right with margin-left:auto on the button (and remove floats from flex children) or add justify-content: space-between on .small-action.

leftover valign-helper becomes spurious flex item in header — WHAT: .contents is made a flex container but .valign-helper (display:inline-block; height:100%) is left inside it as a flex child. WHY: The helper was a pre-flex vertical-centering hack; as a flex item it becomes an extra zero-content child that participates in flex layout, creating unwanted gap/stretch and defeating align-items:center. HOW: Remove or hide .valign-helper when .contents is flex (display:none) or delete the rule.

margin-left:auto ineffective in legacy -webkit-box header, panel not right-aligned — WHAT: .panel uses margin-left:auto to push right inside .contents made flex via 2009 -webkit-box/-moz-box mixin. WHY: 2009 spec ignores auto margins - packing is via -webkit-box-pack / box-flex, so on Android 4.3, iOS 6-7, old Firefox the panel stays left-adjacent to title/extra-info instead of docked right, breaking header layout. HOW: add legacy fallback: -webkit-box-flex:1 / box-flex or use justify-content, or keep float:right fallback inside @supports check, or add -webkit-box-pack:justify / justify-content:space-between on parent.

flexbox mixin missing legacy box-orient causes vertical stacking — WHAT: @mixin flexbox() emits display:-webkit-box / -moz-box / -ms-flexbox without required legacy direction properties. WHY: 2009 spec requires -webkit-box-orient:horizontal and -moz-box-orient:horizontal (and direction) - without them old WebKit/Firefox default or inherit vertical orientation, so .contents and .small-action stack vertically instead of horizontally, breaking header and small-action. HOW: add -webkit-box-orient:horizontal; -webkit-box-direction:normal; -moz-box-orient:horizontal; -moz-box-direction:normal; -ms-flex-direction:row; flex-direction:row to the mixin.

missedGoldens.text: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (wh

goldensDetail.text: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

findings.description: ContextualLoggerMiddleware panics on nil request - missing guard — WHAT: ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods dereference req.PluginContext without nil check and will panic on nil request. WHY: LoggerMiddleware explicitly guards if req==nil return next, but this new middleware does not, so a nil *backend.QueryDataRequest etc. causes nil dereference crash. HOW: Add nil guard matching LoggerMiddleware before instrumentContext, e.g. if req==nil return m.next.QueryData(ctx, req).

Logger loses plugin/trace fields, depends on unwired middleware — WHAT: LoggerMiddleware.logRequest stripped pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, uname and traceID from logParams and now relies on m.logger.FromContext(ctx) populated by ContextualLoggerMiddleware. WHY: Grep shows NewContextualLoggerMiddleware has no callers/wiring, so context never gets those attributes and traceID is dropped entirely (instrumentContext does not add traceID, old code added it via tracing.TraceIDFromContext), silently losing plugin correlation and trace linkage. HOW: Wire NewContextualLoggerMiddleware before LoggerMiddleware in the client middleware chain, and restore traceID handling either in instrumentContext or in logRequest via tracing.TraceIDFromContext.

FromContext fallback discards contextual attributes on type assertion failure — WHAT: grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext asserts underlying logger to *log.ConcreteLogger and on failure returns d.New() discarding all contextual attributes. WHY: When wrapped logger is a test Fake or any non-ConcreteLogger, WithContextualAttributes stored in context is silently lost, breaking log correlation in tests and any alternative logger. HOW: Fall back to preserving context via d.l.FromContext or return wrapper around returned Logger instead of discarding; e.g. if !ok { return &grafanaInfraLogWrapper{l: d.l} } or handle Logger interface generically.

goldensDetail.text: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

findings.description: Mutual-exclusivity validators use truthiness and bypass when age/timestamp is 0 — WHAT: validate_timestamp and validate_age use falsy checks `self.initial_data.get("age")` / `get("timestamp")` instead of existence checks. WHY: When age=0 or timestamp=0 (valid min_value=0), the check is falsy so a report containing BOTH age and timestamp incorrectly passes validation, violating the spec's mutual-exclusivity and allowing ambiguous timing data. HOW: Check key presence explicitly: `if "age" in self.initial_data` and `if "timestamp" in self.initial_data` (or `is not None`).

Detector validator uses wrong key when updating type

Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (miss

goldensDetail.text: Breaking changes in error response format
Detector validator uses wrong key when updating type

Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).

findings.description: Translated config is discarded and original config returned, losing schedule_type display value — WHAT: get_monitor_environment_context copies config and translates schedule_type but returns the original monitor_environment.monitor.config instead of the copied/translated config. WHY: The schedule_type display transformation is discarded, so the occurrence context sent to Kafka contains the raw schedule_type value (e.g. 'crontab') instead of the intended human-readable display value. HOW: Return the modified 'config' variable instead of monitor_environment.monitor.config.

IndexError if previous_checkins is empty for threshold>1 — WHAT: starting_checkin = previous_checkins[0] assumes previous_checkins is non-empty when failure_issue_threshold >1, but the filtered QuerySet can be empty (e.g. no history or failed_checkin not yet visible via date_added__lte). WHY: Empty list causes IndexError, crashing mark_failed and preventing monitor status transition and occurrence creation. HOW: Guard with if not previous_checkins: return False before accessing [0].

missedGoldens.text: The code fetches MonitorCheckIn objects by ID when the required data already exists in previous_checkins. This creates an unnecessary database query.

goldensDetail.text: The function modifies the config variable to include display values but then returns the original monitor.config instead of the modified version.
The code fetches MonitorCheckIn objects by ID when the required data already exists in previous_checkins. This creates an unnecessary database query.

findings.description: retryCount delete branch missing method filter deletes non-SMS reminders — WHAT: deleteMany OR second branch `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` lacks `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, so it deletes ANY WorkflowReminder with retryCount>1 regardless of method or scheduled state. WHY: EMAIL/WhatsApp or already-scheduled SMS reminders that ever reach retryCount>1 (including future-dated ones) are deleted without canceling their Twilio reference, causing data loss / orphan sends. HOW: scope the retry branch to SMS: `OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } }, { method: SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]` (and consider adding `scheduled: false` if only unscheduled should be cleaned).

invalid sendTo/message path skips retry increment causing infinite retries — WHAT: retryCount is only incremented when `scheduledSMS` is falsy or on throw, both inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)` — when message is empty or sendTo is missing the outer if is false and no update occurs. WHY: invalid-phone / missing-data reminders never increment retryCount, so they loop forever every cron run until scheduledDate expires, bypassing the "delete after 2 failures" guarantee. HOW: increment retryCount (or handle invalid case) in the else of the outer message/sendTo check, and also when `!workflowStep || !booking` continue path.

Non-atomic retryCount increment loses concurrent updates and can prevent deletion after 2 failures — WHAT: retryCount increment uses stale local value `reminder.retryCount + 1` instead of atomic increment. WHY: Two concurrent cron invocations fetch same retryCount=0, both fail and both write 1, losing one increment - reminder never reaches gt:1 and is retried forever instead of being deleted after 2 failures (or conversely overwrites a concurrent success). HOW: Use atomic `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }` in both update sites (lines 184 and 195).

goldensDetail.text: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

findings.description: join() leaves orphan flusher processes when timeout expires — WHAT: join() breaks out of the for-loop when remaining_time <=0 without terminating remaining processes. WHY: With num_processes>1 the first process's wait loop consumes the whole deadline; the next iteration breaks and skips terminate() for all remaining entries, leaking alive child processes after shutdown. HOW: Replace the early break with a per-process timeout check and always attempt terminate/join; e.g., compute remaining_time each iteration and if <=0 immediately terminate current and remaining processes instead of breaking.

Empty shard assignment creates zero processes and never flushes — WHAT: num_processes can become 0 when buffer.assigned_shards is empty, creating zero flusher processes and a silent no-op. WHY: max_processes or len(...) is 0 and min(0,0)=0; process_to_shards_map/processes/buffers stay empty so submit never flushes, backpressure and memory checks are skipped, and segments are never produced with no error. HOW: Clamp num_processes to at least 1 when shards empty or early-return/raise; e.g., self.num_processes = max(1, min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))) if buffer.assigned_shards else 0 with explicit handling, or guard __init__ to require non-empty assigned_shards.

Falsy `or` fallback mishandles 0 for max_processes — WHAT: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` uses truthiness so an explicit `0` is ignored and treated as `len(shards)`. WHY: Caller contract allows `flusher_processes=0` (int click option) to mean 0/max-unlimited; the `or` silently creates `len(shards)` processes instead, breaking the caller's requested limit and making tests that construct factory with `None` unexpectedly get `len` processes instead of default 1. HOW: Use `max_processes if max_processes is not None else len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and ensure factory default aligns (1).

Inconsistent shard tag key singular vs plural breaks metrics grouping — WHAT: Metric tag key is inconsistent in same flusher loop: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` uses `{"shard": shard_tag}` while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses `{"shards": shard_tag}`. WHY: Dashboards/alerts grouping by tag key will split or miss data, and the plural key diverges from `segment_size_bytes` which also uses singular `shard`. HOW: Use consistent key `shard` (or `shards`) for all three metrics in `main`.

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

Fixed sleep in tests can be flaky; wait on condition instead

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

findings.description: Narrowed lock allows duplicate concurrent index builds for same key corrupting file backend — WHAT: BuildIndex lock narrowed from whole function to only cache write, allowing concurrent builds for same NamespacedResource to both create bleve indexes on same directory and double-inc metrics. WHY: Two errgroup workers for same key (duplicate stats or retry) can race through bleve.New(dir) simultaneously corrupting file index and leaking the first index while second overwrites cache. HOW: Hold lock or add double-checked existence check / per-key mutex around builder; e.g., check cache under RLock before building and re-check under Lock before inserting, or use singleflight per key.

Init failure leaks server context/cancel func — WHAT: NewResourceServer creates cancelable ctx (WithCancel) stored in s but on Init error returns nil without calling cancel, leaking context and watcher goroutine. WHY: Init failure path logs and returns nil,err leaving s.cancel unreachable; server ctx never cancelled and any started watcher/resources leak until process exit. HOW: Defer cancel on error path: if err != nil { cancel(); return nil, err } or store cancel and call it before return.

Swapped initWatcher/search.init order opens lost-update window for search index — WHAT: Init order was swapped to build search index before starting the watcher (search.init then initWatcher). WHY: This inverts the required subscribe-before-snapshot pattern – writes that occur between the GetResourceStats snapshot and the WatchWriteEvents subscription are not observed, leaving the index stale/missing recent documents until the next write for that key. HOW: Restore original order: start initWatcher before s.search.init, or make search.init re-query/reconcile the gap RV after watcher subscription (as before).

goldensDetail.text: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

findings.description: Login-cache invalidation on update misses BROKER_PUBLIC toggles on org-unlinked IDPs, leaving the ORG_ONLY(null) cached list stale. — WHAT: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate skips login-cache invalidation whenever getLoginPredicate() yields the same result and organizationId is unchanged, but the predicate's new condition (idp.getOrganizationId() == null || BROKER_PUBLIC) short-circuits to true for org-NULL IDPs, while the delegate's ORG branch (IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin, interface line 173-180) applies BROKER_PUBLIC="true" with NO ORGANIZATION_ID constraint when organizationId is null — so an org-NULL IDP with brokerPublic=true is a member of the ORG_ONLY("") cached set even though its predicate state never changes. WHY: toggling an org-unlinked IDP's BROKER_PUBLIC config from true to false (or false to true) never flips the predicate and orgId stays null, so no invalidation is registered and the cached ORG_ONLY(null) list served to OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean (line 74, 'public enabled IDPs linked to any org') keeps showing/hiding the IDP incorrectly until some unrelated invalidation happens — a stale-cache regression that could not occur before this PR added the cache. HOW: also compare the BROKER_PUBLIC config value in the no-invalidation condition, e.g. add '&& Objects.equals(Boolean.parseBoolean(original.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)), Boolean.parseBoolean(updated.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))' to the second early-return (or simply drop the skip optimization and always invalidate all FetchMode keys on update, matching create/remove).

findings.description: Feature-flag mismatch in the removal listener lets V2's UnsupportedOperationException-throwing setPermissionsEnabled execute on client deletion when both ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 are enabled. — WHAT: the new guard checks Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), but AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, and this PR's MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() override returns ClientPermissionsV2 whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. WHY: when both features are enabled (a valid configuration during V1→V2 migration), every ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent makes the listener call management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) → UnsupportedOperationException, which propagates out of the provider event fire and breaks client deletion; before this PR the V2 class inherited the V1 clients() implementation which did not throw (role/group deletion is unaffected only because V2 does not override roles()/groups()). HOW: make the guard consistent with the dispatch — skip the V1 cleanup when V2 is active, e.g. `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) && !Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2))` (or guard each management() call with the same V2 check used in management()).

Missing null check on the 'Clients' all-clients resource before findByResource causes an NPE in permission evaluation on realms where that resource was never created. — WHAT: when the per-client resource does not exist, getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) is passed unchecked to policyStore.findByResource(server, resource), and getResourceTypeResource has three explicit null-return paths (schema unsupported, unknown type, resource not found in store). WHY: on a realm whose admin-permission resource server was initialized before this PR added the 'Clients' resource type, the 'Clients' all-clients resource may not exist, so resource is null and the store's findByResource dereferences it (resource.getId() in the query build) → NullPointerException → 500 on every admin client operation that requires a permission check for that client; the sibling no-arg hasPermission(String scope) in this same file null-checks the identical lookup and returns false, and the 'Users' resource that UserPermissionsV2 relies on was guaranteed at original setup whereas 'Clients' is new. HOW: add `if (resource == null) return false;` after the getResourceTypeResource call (optionally combined with the existing policy-existence check).

Potentially null "Clients" resource is passed unguarded into findByResource. — hasPermission(client, scope) fallback: getResourceTypeResource() returns resourceStore.findByName(server, "Clients"), which is null until such a resource exists, and the result is passed unguarded into findByResource(server, resource). The identical pre-existing pattern is noted at UserPermissionsV2 lines 121-123, and this issue is already recorded as an existing finding.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-le

goldensDetail.text: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

findings.description: Handler calls EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees which is not defined anywhere in the repo, breaking the build. — WHAT: `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` calls a method that does not exist on EventManager. WHY: a repo-wide search for `updateCalendarAttendees` returns only this call site — no definition in packages/core/EventManager or any base class — so the trpc package fails TypeScript compilation and the whole bookings router build breaks. HOW: add an `updateCalendarAttendees(calEvent, booking)` method to EventManager that updates the attendee list on the destination calendar (as this feature requires), or call the existing calendar attendee-update API if one already exists.

Team admin/owner permission check uses && instead of ||, so team admins can never add guests. — WHAT: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` instead of `||`, requiring the user to simultaneously be a team admin AND a team owner. WHY: a team member holds exactly one role, so the AND is effectively always false (at best it reduces to isTeamOwner, excluding pure admins) — team admins/owners are wrongly rejected by the FORBIDDEN check on the next gate even though the variable name and this feature's intent grant them permission to add guests. HOW: use `||` between the two checks.

Guest emails are not lowercased, allowing blacklist bypass and duplicate attendees via case variants. — WHAT: guest emails are compared case-sensitively against existing attendees and against a lowercased blacklist, while the raw input is never normalized. WHY: emails are case-insensitive — 'Guest@Domain.com' bypasses a BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entry 'guest@domain.com' (env values are lowercased at line 71, input is not) and duplicates an already-registered attendee 'guest@domain.com' instead of being filtered at line 76, creating a duplicate BookingAttendee row. HOW: lowercase the guest list once (e.g. `const uniqueGuests = guests.map(g => g.toLowerCase()).filter(...)`) and compare lowercased values.

Raw input guests (including existing attendees/duplicates) are passed to the email sender instead of the deduplicated uniqueGuests. — WHAT: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw input array instead of `uniqueGuests`. WHY: the input may contain emails that are already booking attendees or duplicates; verified the callee signature `sendAddGuestsEmails(calEvent, newGuests: string[])` in email-manager.ts treats its second argument as the NEW guests — so pre-existing attendees get spurious 'guests added' notifications and duplicate entries cause duplicate sends. HOW: pass `uniqueGuests`.

Raw i18n keys passed as title/subject override the internally translated values via JSX spread order, so emails show literal translation keys. — WHAT: the wrappers pass raw i18n keys (title='new_guests_added', subject='guests_added_event_type_subject') and OrganizerScheduledEmail spreads `{...props}` AFTER its explicit `subject={t(subject)}`/`title={t(title)}` (line 52 of OrganizerScheduledEmail.tsx), so the last-wins JSX semantics make the raw keys override the translated strings. WHY: the 'guests added' emails go out with the literal un-translated key 'guests_added_event_type_subject' as the subject line and 'new_guests_added' as the title instead of localized text. HOW: make the overrides translated (apply t() before passing) or fix the spread order in OrganizerScheduledEmail/AttendeeScheduledEmail so caller-provided title/subject do not clobber the computed translated values; the same issue exists in AttendeeAddGuestsEmail.tsx.

email-manager.ts imports kebab-case add-guests template files that don't exist; the PR's templates are in a different path/casing, breaking the @calcom/emails build. — WHAT: this handler imports `sendAddGuestsEmails` from @calcom/emails, but email-manager.ts in that package imports the guest templates as `./templates/attendee-add-guests-email` and `./templates/organizer-add-guests-email` (kebab-case under packages/emails/templates/), and no such files exist anywhere in the repo (searched; only the import lines reference them) — this PR instead adds PascalCase files under packages/emails/src/templates/. WHY: the unresolved imports make packages/emails fail to build, so the addGuests mutation cannot compile or run even after the other issues are fixed. HOW: either add the template files at the kebab-case paths email-manager.ts imports, or change email-manager.ts's imports to point at the new src/templates files (it already uses that style, e.g. `./src/templates/MonthlyDigestEmail`).

Wrappers pass headerType/callToAction props that do not exist on the wrapped components' prop types, causing TS errors or silent no-ops. — WHAT: the wrappers pass `headerType="calendarCircle"` and `callToAction={null}` to OrganizerScheduledEmail/AttendeeScheduledEmail, but neither `headerType` nor `callToAction` exists on BaseScheduledEmail (grepped — zero matches) nor on the explicit OrganizerScheduledEmail prop fields. WHY: `React.ComponentProps<typeof OrganizerScheduledEmail>` does not include these props, so the JSX object literals are type errors (excess properties) and, at runtime, the props are silently dropped — the intended header icon and CTA suppression have no effect. HOW: add the props to BaseScheduledEmail (and thread them through) or remove the unsupported props from the wrappers.

Input guest list is not de-duplicated, so duplicate emails create duplicate attendee rows and trigger duplicate emails. — WHAT: the `uniqueGuests` filter only excludes emails already present in `booking.attendees` and the blacklist — it never de-duplicates within the caller-supplied `guests` array, and the `Attendee` model has no `@@unique([bookingId, email])` constraint. WHY: an input like `guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"]` (or the same address reaching the array twice) passes the filter and `attendees.createMany` inserts duplicate attendee rows for the same booking, which then causes duplicate attendees in the calendar update and a duplicate 'new guests added' email per duplicate row (the attendee email loop in email-manager.ts matches every attendee whose email is in the list). HOW: de-duplicate the input before filtering, e.g. `const uniqueGuests = [...new Set(guests)].filter(...)`, ideally normalizing to lowercase as well.

Unbounded guests array allows a single request to trigger unbounded attendee inserts and email/calendar fanout. — WHAT: `guests` is `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()` bound, and the handler fans out per guest (one `createMany` row, one 'guests added' email per new guest, plus a full calendar attendee update). WHY: a single authenticated request from any organizer/attendee can pass thousands of emails, causing unbounded attendee inserts, unbounded email sends, and an oversized calendar API update — a resource-exhaustion path on a hot mutation. HOW: add a sensible cap such as `z.array(z.string().email()).max(50)` (or a similar bound consistent with product limits) to the schema.
